# crap4dart configuration for flutter_agent_harness.
# https://github.com/IstiN/crap4dart
#
# RATCHET: the CRAP threshold is pinned at the current worst score
# (356.34, `_handleKey` in bin/../tui_repl.dart) — pushes may only make
# the codebase BETTER, never worse. Lower the threshold whenever the top
# offenders are fixed (run: dart pub global run crap4dart analyze).

sources: [lib, bin]

exclude:
  - '**.g.dart'
  - '**.freezed.dart'
  - '**.mocks.dart'
  - 'build/**'
  - 'vendor/**'

crap:
  enabled: true
  # Current max CRAP score in the repo (2026-08-12 — GREEN zone after the
  # cleanup rounds 356.34 → 65.1 → 16 → 8 → 12; three TUI-only dispatchers
  # at CC 3 / 0% cov land at CRAP 12 — they need a real PTY to test). Only
  # down from here.
  threshold: 12.0
# NOTE: _listModels (provider_commands.dart) hits 20 with 0% coverage
# because it is line-mode-only output; it pre-dates the dial work. Fix
# separately — do not ratchet up for it.

coverage:
  # scripts/pre-commit regenerates this (dart test --coverage) right
  # before the CRAP step runs.
  lcov_path: coverage/lcov.info
  required: true
  branch_coverage: true
  # crap4dart 0.9.5 flipped the run_tests default to true — a bare
  # `analyze`/`check` would silently re-run the whole core suite first.
  # Coverage is regenerated explicitly (pre-commit hook, CI shard merge);
  # do not pay for it twice.
  run_tests: false

# ─── Gates (issue #447) ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# 0.9.5 default-enables ALL built-in gates; only broken_goldens is
# enforced here, everything else is disabled explicitly so a bare
# `check --staged` (pre-commit, core-only #433 split) means exactly the
# pixel gate. The flutter_app goldens live in flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml.
gates:
  loc: {enabled: false} # own ≤2800 gate (scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh)
  test_coverage: {enabled: false} # own ≥80% coverage-gate job
  complexity: {enabled: false} # CRAP ratchet above already covers it
  method_size: {enabled: false}
  nesting: {enabled: false}
  class_size: {enabled: false}
  weight_of_class: {enabled: false}
  unused_code: {enabled: false}
  unused_files: {enabled: false}
  banned_imports: {enabled: false}
  # Type-2 duplication gate (issue #1106, crap4dart 0.11.0). Renamed-clone
  # detection on top of the Type-1 default; the union with the raw pass can
  # only ADD findings, never lose exact copies. severity: warning starts
  # soft — escalate to error once the 13-file triage debt is paid
  # (follow-up, owner-side). The global jscpd <1% guards stay as-is.
  #
  # Two suppression channels with different contracts:
  # - `// crap:ignore` (needs ignorable: true) = a JUSTIFIED structural
  #   twin, suppressed forever, with a one-line reason in the comment.
  # - `.crap-baseline.json` (via `check --baseline`) = LEGACY debt; the
  #   committed snapshot must only SHRINK: after each triage batch re-run
  #   `dart pub global run crap4dart check --save-baseline` and commit the
  #   only-down diff, or the snapshot rots and starts masking shifts.
  #
  # WINDOW (until severity flips to error): the gate never fails a build —
  # new (not-baselined) duplication only surfaces as a `[WARN]` line in
  # `check` output. Enforcement becomes hard exactly when the owner-side
  # escalation lands; from then on any finding outside the two channels
  # fails CI/pre-commit.
  duplication:
    enabled: true
    severity: warning
    ignorable: true # enables `// crap:ignore` for justified structural twins
    ignore_locals: true # Type-2: rename locals before hashing (API names stay)
    ignore_literals: false # keeps l10n/theme/symbol tables out
    sources: # cross-module scope from #487
      - flutter_app/lib
      - packages/fa_ui/lib
      - packages/fa_llm/lib
  file_naming: {enabled: false}
  magic_constants: {enabled: false}
  test_assertions: {enabled: false}
  folder_structure: {enabled: false}
  external: {enabled: false}
  public_docs: {enabled: false}
  golden: {enabled: false} # flutter-only gate (core is not a Flutter project)
  accessibility: {enabled: false}
  hardcoded_strings: {enabled: false}

  # Pixel gate over core test/ goldens — none exist today, so this is a
  # no-op that guards the future (issue #447 AC: "and core test/ goldens
  # if any appear"). WARNING, same rationale as flutter_app: the 0.9.5
  # detector misses the Ahem-solid-rect and hollow-square classes and
  # false-positives on V-converging shapes; flip to error when the
  # upstream detector fixes land.
  broken_goldens:
    enabled: true
    severity: warning
    dirs: [test]
    exclude:
      # TUI screenshots, not goldens: amber/yellow text on the dark theme
      # trips the stripe heuristic (measured 14/14 "overflow stripes" —
      # the same yellow-on-dark detector bug the issue documents for
      # apps_panel/panel_dark). Revisit when upstream fixes land.
      - 'test/integration/**'

      # weekly by shard-rebalance.yml from junit durations. Bootstrap here
      # is filecount-balanced; the first weekly junit rebalance converges
      # to duration balance. Unknown test files are bin-packed in at
      # runtime by shard_files.py, so a PR adding one never silently skips
      # it. The json file-reporter (converted to junit below — dart test
      # has no built-in junit reporter) feeds the rebalancer real durations
      # (issue #194 AC3).
      - name: dart test --coverage (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }})
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py \
            test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json \

# ── Stage implementations ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
stage_size() {
  # Hook mode scopes the guard to the STAGED Dart files: the guard ratchets
  # what a commit touches, so a pre-existing oversized file elsewhere (e.g.
  # flutter_app/lib/services/agent_service.dart, which ci.yml's guard never
  # measures — it scans lib/test/example only) cannot block an unrelated
  # commit. Non-hook runs keep the whole-tree scan below.
  if [ "$HOOK_MODE" -eq 1 ]; then
    local violations
    violations=$(git diff --cached --name-only --diff-filter=ACM \
      | grep '\.dart$' \
      | grep -vE '\.g\.dart$|\.freezed\.dart$|\.mocks\.dart$|bridge_generated|app_localizations|localizations_' \
      | while IFS= read -r f; do
          [ -f "$f" ] || continue
          lines=$(wc -l < "$f")
          if [ "$lines" -gt "$MAX_LINES" ]; then echo "$f: $lines lines"; fi
        done || true)
    if [ -n "$violations" ]; then
      echo "❌ QUALITY GATE FAILED — FILE SIZE (max $MAX_LINES lines)" >&2
      echo "$violations" >&2
      exit 1
    fi
    return 0
  fi
  # Same find-exec guard as ci.yml / pre-commit: no dart file over MAX_LINES.
  local dirs=""
  local d
  for d in lib test example bin; do
    [ -d "$d" ] && dirs="$dirs $d"
  done
  if [ "$APP_IN_SCOPE" -eq 1 ] && [ -d flutter_app/lib ]; then
    dirs="$dirs flutter_app/lib"
  fi
  local violations
  violations=$(find $dirs -name '*.dart' \
    ! -name '*.g.dart' ! -name '*.freezed.dart' ! -name '*.mocks.dart' \
    ! -name '*bridge_generated*.dart' ! -name '*app_localizations*.dart' \
    ! -name '*localizations_*.dart' \
    -exec sh -c 'lines=$(wc -l < "$1"); if [ "$lines" -gt '"$MAX_LINES"' ]; then echo "$1: $lines lines"; fi' _ {} \;)
  if [ -n "$violations" ]; then
    echo "❌ QUALITY GATE FAILED — FILE SIZE (max $MAX_LINES lines)" >&2
    echo "$violations" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
}

stage_analyze() {
  echo "🔍 Running dart analyze..."
  dart analyze
  if [ "$APP_IN_SCOPE" -eq 1 ] && command -v flutter >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    ensure_app_placeholders

    (cd flutter_app && flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos --no-fatal-warnings)
    FLUTTER_ANALYZED=1
  fi
}

stage_test_core() {
  echo "🧪 Running dart test --coverage (excluding integration tests)..."
  rm -rf coverage
  local conc="${FA_DART_TEST_CONCURRENCY:-$(detect_test_concurrency)}"
  echo "   concurrency: ${conc:-default}"
  dart test ${conc:+--concurrency=$conc} --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration
  # gh-1033 (review thread 7 + gate wiring): the fa jsr delegate suites are
  # integration-tagged — the PTY leg's CLI coverage ratchet measures
  # lib/src/cli hits from them — so the unit run above skips them. Their
  # hits must ALSO reach the unit-side lcov consumers (>= 80% ratchet, PR
  # diff-coverage, CRAP: jsr_cli.dart at 0% line coverage reads CRAP 156
  # against the 12.0 ceiling), so the trio runs into the SAME coverage/
  # dir; format_coverage merges the per-isolate files. Keep this list in
  # sync with ci.yml (test-core shard 0) and nightly.yml.
  dart test ${conc:+--concurrency=$conc} --tags integration \
    test/cli/jsr_cli_test.dart \
    test/cli/cli_args_jsr_test.dart \
    test/cli/agent_cli_jsr_test.dart \
    --coverage=coverage
}

stage_integration_mock() {
  # Issue #551: the no-key integration legs run on EVERY PR that touches
  # them — MockLlmServer scenarios, no secrets, no network, so they cannot
  # rot silently between releases (#538 class). Real-provider files carry
  # the `llm` tag and stay in the tag-only smoke job; browser-ext owns its
  # own workflow; perf has the #303 per-PR trajectory gate; `pty` marks
  # child-agent-spawn tests (issue #553) — nightly-only, unbounded boot time.
  #
  # TMPDIR normalization (macOS hook parity): several PTY legs assert the
  # status row still shows `· ctx ` — with macOS's per-user temp root
  # (/var/folders/<30 chars>/T/...) the temp cwd eats the whole row width
  # and the assertion fails locally while ubuntu CI (/tmp) is green. Pin
  # the stage to the same short temp root CI has so hook/CI agree.
  echo "🧪 Running no-key integration legs (MockLlmServer)..."
  local conc="${FA_DART_TEST_CONCURRENCY:-$(detect_test_concurrency)}"
  echo "   concurrency: ${conc:-default}"
  #
  # Flake budget (gh-1026): FA_GATE_PTY_RETRIES=N reruns ONLY the failed
  # files, up to N times, before the stage fails. The PTY/grid timing legs
  # are load-sensitive (the gh-1026 class: 3 red 2.5 h gate runs on an
  # unchanged head, a different ambient test red each time, every file
  # green in isolation) — the budget turns one flaky PTY case from a full
  # leg rerun into a minutes-scoped file rerun, mirroring CI's
  # retrigger-recovery behaviour (ci.yml watchdog: ONE retrigger, never a
  # blind rerun). 0 (the default) keeps the single-shot leg below
  # byte-identical. Files come from scripts/gate_failed_targets.py over
  # the dart json file-reporter log; when the log yields no targets
  # (crash before the reporter flushed) the stage fails WITHOUT a rerun —
  # never rerun blind.
  local retries="${FA_GATE_PTY_RETRIES:-0}"
  if [ "$retries" -le 0 ]; then
    TMPDIR="${FA_GATE_TMPDIR:-/tmp}" \
      dart test ${conc:+--concurrency=$conc} test/integration \
      --exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,perf,pty
    return
  fi
  local log="test-results/gate-integration-mock.json"
  mkdir -p test-results
  local targets="test/integration"
  local attempt=0
  while true; do
    attempt=$((attempt + 1))
    if TMPDIR="${FA_GATE_TMPDIR:-/tmp}" \
        dart test ${conc:+--concurrency=$conc} $targets \
        --exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,perf,pty \
        --file-reporter="json:$log"; then
      return 0
    fi
    if [ "$attempt" -gt "$retries" ]; then
      echo "❌ flake budget exhausted ($retries rerun(s)) — integration leg stays red" >&2
      exit 1
    fi
    local failed
    failed=$(python3 scripts/gate_failed_targets.py "$log")
    if [ -z "$failed" ]; then
      echo "   no failed-file targets in $log — not rerunning blind" >&2
      exit 1
    fi
    echo "🔁 flake budget: rerun $attempt/$retries — failed files only:" >&2
    printf '%s\n' "$failed" | sed 's/^/   /' >&2
    targets="$failed"
  done
}

stage_coverage() {
  if [ ! -d coverage ]; then
    echo "❌ coverage/ not found — run the test-core stage first" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  echo "📊 Formatting coverage to lcov..."
  dart run coverage:format_coverage --lcov -i coverage -o coverage/lcov.info
  echo "🔍 Checking line coverage (baseline: >= ${COVERAGE_BASELINE}%)..."
  if ! python3 scripts/check_coverage.py "$COVERAGE_BASELINE"; then
    echo "❌ QUALITY GATE FAILED — TEST COVERAGE (baseline ${COVERAGE_BASELINE}%)" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
}

"Only down from here", threshold 12.0 — the existing worst offenders at CRAP 12 pass, so the check is CRAP > 12.0 fails. CC 12 fully covered = CRAP 12.0 → borderline pass. But at 57.1% → 23.34 → FAIL.

2. **`HostKeyResolver.resolveKey`** — CRAP 15.0 at CC 15, 100% coverage → 15 > 12 → **FAIL even with perfect coverage**. This is a hard fail in CI: the coverage is complete (100%), so CI's merged coverage also reads CC 15 → CRAP 15 > 12 → the CRAP ratchet fails. That's the root cause of the guards failure!

Note: the switch-expressions in `_message`/`_tail` apparently don't count per-case (CC 2 for `_message` — so crap4dart doesn't count switch expression cases, or counts them as 1 total). Good.

So the CRAP ratchet failure is real: `HostKeyResolver.resolveKey` CC 15 → CRAP 15 (> 12) even fully covered. And `AgentTelemetry._record` CC 12 with partial coverage → 23.34.

Wait — but let me confirm the formula: CRAP = comp² × (1 − cov)³ + comp. For CC 15, cov 100%: 15. Yes → 15 > 12 → fails. For CC 12, cov 57.1%: 144 × 0.429³ + 12 = 144 × 0.0789 + 12 = 11.36 + 12 = 23.36 ≈ 23.34 ✓.

In CI with the full suite, `AgentTelemetry._record` coverage might be higher (the full suite might exercise more of the switch — e.g. stuck-tool heartbeats might be covered by other tests? Whatever the exact CI coverage is, `HostKeyResolver.resolveKey` at CRAP 15 with 100% cov is a definite ratchet failure — that alone fails the guards job. And `_record` at CC 12/57.1% is another likely failure (CI coverage won't hit 100%: heartbeat/stuck paths need specific wiring; even if they are covered, CRAP = 12.0 exactly = borderline pass — too risky).

**Finding 1: `HostKeyResolver.resolveKey` CC 15 → CRAP 15 > 12.**

blocks.text:
Empirical CC counting rules in crap4dart:
- `if`: +1 each ✓ (3 ifs → CC 4)
- ternary: +1 ✓
- **switch statement: +1 per case** (4 cases → CC 5)
- **switch expression: +0 (!)** — CC 1
- **stacked cases: +1 per case LABEL** (4 labels over 2 bodies → CC 5)
- `||`: +1 each (3 || → CC 5)
- collection-if: +0
- for/catch: +1 each
- when guard: case +1, `when` +1 (CC 3 = base + case + when)

So the plan for `_record`:
- Split into `_record` (run-phase switch: AgentStart, TurnStart, MessageUpdate+when, TurnEnd, AgentEnd, default → CC = 1+5+1(when) = 7) + `_recordToolEvent` (4 cases + default → CC 5-6).
- Dispatch: `if (event is Tool...) { _recordToolEvent(event); return; }` would add if+||s. Alternative: use a switch EXPRESSION or avoid the or-pattern...

Option: `_record` keeps ALL cases but tool cases just call `_recordToolEvent(event)` — stacked labels each +1: tool case labels = 4 stacked → +4, run cases 5 + when 1 → CC = 1 + 4 + 5 + 1 = 11. Too high.

Better: two independent switches is impossible one event without a pre-dispatch... Use stacked cases but ONLY 2: hmm.

Cleanest low-CC: pre-dispatch with a single `is` check against a helper... Dart has no multi-is. What about:

```dart
void _record(AgentEvent event) {
  if (event is ToolExecutionStartEvent ||
      event is ToolExecutionEndEvent ||
      event is ToolCallHeartbeatEvent ||
      event is ToolCallStuckEvent) {
    _recordToolEvent(event);
    return;
  }
  _recordRunPhase(event);
}
```
CC = 1 + 1(if) + 3(||) = 5. 
`_recordToolEvent`: switch statement, 4 cases (exhaustive over the four types? no — compiler can't know; needs default or end) → CC = 1+4+1(default) = 6. At 100% cov = 6. 
`_recordRunPhase`: switch with AgentStart, TurnStart, MessageUpdate+when, TurnEnd, AgentEnd, default → CC = 1+5+1 = 7. Existing tests cover it 100% → CRAP 7. 

Wait — can I do better? switch expression for _recordRunPhase: switch EXPRESSIONS count 0! But the cases have side effects and one has a when-guard... switch expressions support when-guards. Side effects in expression cases are fine (each branch an expression). E.g.:

```dart
void _recordRunPhase(AgentEvent event) => switch (event) {
  AgentStartEvent() => _onRunStart(),
  TurnStartEvent() => _emit(AgentTelemetryEventKind.turnStart),
  MessageUpdateEvent() when !_sawFirstToken => _onFirstStreamedUpdate(),
  TurnEndEvent(:final message) => _emit(..., stopReason: message.stopReason.name),
  AgentEndEvent() => _onAgentEnd(event),
  _ => null,  // hmm — expression must return a value; use void-ish
};
```
Each case returns void — switch expression arms returning void is allowed? The expression type would be void — `void switchExpr` — allowed in Dart? An expression switch whose arms all have type void: the switch expression's static type is void, and `void _recordRunPhase(AgentEvent event) => switch ...` works. Hmm, `when` guard +1 (when counts even in expressions? Probably same counting — probe didn't test switch-expression with when. Conservative: assume +1).

But honestly CC 7 @ 100% cov (CRAP 7) is comfortably under 12. And even if CI coverage dipped to 80%: 49×0.008+7 = 7.4. Totally safe. Keep switch STATEMENT (matches existing file style — `_record` was a statement switch; minimal diff).

Same for _recordToolEvent (CC 6) — must be 100% covered via new tests, else CC 6 @ 0% = 36+6 = 42. New tests required for all four kinds.

For `resolveKey` (CC 15 @ 100% = 15): refactor into helpers, each ≤ 6:
- `resolveKey` body: canonical + chained + name + return HostKeyResolution(...) → CC ~2
- `_effectiveSlotName(canonical, chained)`: firstWhere closure — does the closure's inner ||s count toward the METHOD's CC? `probeLogicalOr` counted them as top-level statements; closures — likely counted within the enclosing function by crap4dart's visitor (typical). firstWhere closure: `(slot) => slot != canonical && ... && _hasStoreValue(...)` — 2 &&s. `_missingKeyHint`: if + ternary → CC ~3-4.

sources: [lib, bin]

exclude:
  - '**.g.dart'
  - '**.freezed.dart'
  - '**.mocks.dart'
  - 'build/**'
  - 'vendor/**'

crap:
  enabled: true
  # Current max CRAP score in the repo (2026-08-12 — GREEN zone after the
  # cleanup rounds 356.34 → 65.1 → 16 → 8 → 12; three TUI-only dispatchers

# because it is line-mode-only output; it pre-dates the dial work. Fix

coverage:
  # scripts/pre-commit regenerates this (dart test --coverage) right
  # before the CRAP step runs.
  lcov_path: coverage/lcov.info
  required: true
  branch_coverage: true
  # crap4dart 0.9.5 flipped the run_tests default to true — a bare
  # `analyze`/`check` would silently re-run the whole core suite first.
  # Coverage is regenerated explicitly (pre-commit hook, CI shard merge);
  # do not pay for it twice.
  run_tests: false

# ─── Gates (issue #447) ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# 0.9.5 default-enables ALL built-in gates; only broken_goldens is
# enforced here, everything else is disabled explicitly so a bare
# `check --staged` (pre-commit, core-only #433 split) means exactly the
# pixel gate. The flutter_app goldens live in flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml.

  loc: {enabled: false} # own ≤2800 gate (scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh)
  test_coverage: {enabled: false} # own ≥80% coverage-gate job
  complexity: {enabled: false} # CRAP ratchet above already covers it
  method_size: {enabled: false}
  nesting: {enabled: false}
  class_size: {enabled: false}
  weight_of_class: {enabled: false}
  unused_code: {enabled: false}
  unused_files: {enabled: false}
  banned_imports: {enabled: false}
  # Type-2 duplication gate (issue #1106, crap4dart 0.11.0). Renamed-clone
  # detection on top of the Type-1 default; the union with the raw pass can
  # only ADD findings, never lose exact copies. severity: warning starts
  # soft — escalate to error once the 13-file triage debt is paid
  # (follow-up, owner-side). The global jscpd <1% guards stay as-is.
  #
  # Two suppression channels with different contracts:
  # - `// crap:ignore` (needs ignorable: true) = a JUSTIFIED structural
  #   twin, suppressed forever, with a one-line reason in the comment.
  # - `.crap-baseline.json` (via `check --baseline`) = LEGACY debt; the
  #   committed snapshot must only SHRINK: after each triage batch re-run
  #   `dart pub global run crap4dart check --save-baseline` and commit the
  #   only-down diff, or the snapshot rots and starts masking shifts.
  #
  # WINDOW (until severity flips to error): the gate never fails a build —
  # new (not-baselined) duplication only surfaces as a `[WARN]` line in
  # `check` output. Enforcement becomes hard exactly when the owner-side
  # escalation lands; from then on any finding outside the two channels
  # fails CI/pre-commit.
  duplication:
    enabled: true
    severity: warning
    ignorable: true # enables `// crap:ignore` for justified structural twins
    ignore_locals: true # Type-2: rename locals before hashing (API names stay)
    ignore_literals: false # keeps l10n/theme/symbol tables out

      - packages/fa_llm/lib
  file_naming: {enabled: false}
  magic_constants: {enabled: false}
  test_assertions: {enabled: false}
  folder_structure: {enabled: false}
  external: {enabled: false}
  public_docs: {enabled: false}
  golden: {enabled: false} # flutter-only gate (core is not a Flutter project)
  accessibility: {enabled: false}
  hardcoded_strings: {enabled: false}

  # Pixel gate over core test/ goldens — none exist today, so this is a
  # no-op that guards the future (issue #447 AC: "and core test/ goldens
  # if any appear"). WARNING, same rationale as flutter_app: the 0.9.5
  # detector misses the Ahem-solid-rect and hollow-square classes and
  # false-positives on V-converging shapes; flip to error when the
  # upstream detector fixes land.
  broken_goldens:

    severity: warning
    dirs: [test]
    exclude:

      # trips the stripe heuristic (measured 14/14 "overflow stripes" —

      # weekly by shard-rebalance.yml from junit durations. Bootstrap here
      # is filecount-balanced; the first weekly junit rebalance converges
      # to duration balance. Unknown test files are bin-packed in at
      # runtime by shard_files.py, so a PR adding one never silently skips
      # it. The json file-reporter (converted to junit below — dart test
      # has no built-in junit reporter) feeds the rebalancer real durations
      # (issue #194 AC3).
      - name: dart test --coverage (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }})
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets

# ── Stage implementations ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
stage_size() {
  # Hook mode scopes the guard to the STAGED Dart files: the guard ratchets
  # what a commit touches, so a pre-existing oversized file elsewhere (e.g.
  # flutter_app/lib/services/agent_service.dart, which ci.yml's guard never
  # measures — it scans lib/test/example only) cannot block an unrelated
  # commit. Non-hook runs keep the whole-tree scan below.
  if [ "$HOOK_MODE" -eq 1 ]; then
    local violations
    violations=$(git diff --cached --name-only --diff-filter=ACM \
      | grep '\.dart$' \
      | grep -vE '\.g\.dart$|\.freezed\.dart$|\.mocks\.dart$|bridge_generated|app_localizations|localizations_' \
      | while IFS= read -r f; do
          [ -f "$f" ] || continue
          lines=$(wc -l < "$f")
          if [ "$lines" -gt "$MAX_LINES" ]; then echo "$f: $lines lines"; fi
        done || true)
    if [ -n "$violations" ]; then
      echo "❌ QUALITY GATE FAILED — FILE SIZE (max $MAX_LINES lines)" >&2
      echo "$violations" >&2
      exit 1
    fi
    return 0
  fi
  # Same find-exec guard as ci.yml / pre-commit: no dart file over MAX_LINES.
  local dirs=""
  local d
  for d in lib test example bin; do
    [ -d "$d" ] && dirs="$dirs $d"
  done
  if [ "$APP_IN_SCOPE" -eq 1 ] && [ -d flutter_app/lib ]; then
    dirs="$dirs flutter_app/lib"
  fi
  local violations
  violations=$(find $dirs -name '*.dart' \
    ! -name '*.g.dart' ! -name '*.freezed.dart' ! -name '*.mocks.dart' \
    ! -name '*bridge_generated*.dart' ! -name '*app_localizations*.dart' \
    ! -name '*localizations_*.dart' \
    -exec sh -c 'lines=$(wc -l < "$1"); if [ "$lines" -gt '"$MAX_LINES"' ]; then echo "$1: $lines lines"; fi' _ {} \;)
  if [ -n "$violations" ]; then
    echo "❌ QUALITY GATE FAILED — FILE SIZE (max $MAX_LINES lines)" >&2
    echo "$violations" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
}

stage_analyze() {
  echo "🔍 Running dart analyze..."
  dart analyze
  if [ "$APP_IN_SCOPE" -eq 1 ] && command -v flutter >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    ensure_app_placeholders
    echo "🔍 Running flutter analyze (flutter_app)..."
    (cd flutter_app && flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos --no-fatal-warnings)
    FLUTTER_ANALYZED=1
  fi
}

stage_test_core() {
  echo "🧪 Running dart test --coverage (excluding integration tests)..."
  rm -rf coverage
  local conc="${FA_DART_TEST_CONCURRENCY:-$(detect_test_concurrency)}"
  echo "   concurrency: ${conc:-default}"
  dart test ${conc:+--concurrency=$conc} --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration
  # gh-1033 (review thread 7 + gate wiring): the fa jsr delegate suites are
  # integration-tagged — the PTY leg's CLI coverage ratchet measures
  # lib/src/cli hits from them — so the unit run above skips them. Their
  # hits must ALSO reach the unit-side lcov consumers (>= 80% ratchet, PR
  # diff-coverage, CRAP: jsr_cli.dart at 0% line coverage reads CRAP 156
  # against the 12.0 ceiling), so the trio runs into the SAME coverage/
  # dir; format_coverage merges the per-isolate files. Keep this list in
  # sync with ci.yml (test-core shard 0) and nightly.yml.
  dart test ${conc:+--concurrency=$conc} --tags integration \
    test/cli/jsr_cli_test.dart \
    test/cli/cli_args_jsr_test.dart \
    test/cli/agent_cli_jsr_test.dart \
    --coverage=coverage
}

stage_integration_mock() {
  # Issue #551: the no-key integration legs run on EVERY PR that touches
  # them — MockLlmServer scenarios, no secrets, no network, so they cannot
  # rot silently between releases (#538 class). Real-provider files carry
  # the `llm` tag and stay in the tag-only smoke job; browser-ext owns its
  # own workflow; perf has the #303 per-PR trajectory gate; `pty` marks
  # child-agent-spawn tests (issue #553) — nightly-only, unbounded boot time.
  #
  # TMPDIR normalization (macOS hook parity): several PTY legs assert the
  # status row still shows `· ctx ` — with macOS's per-user temp root
  # (/var/folders/<30 chars>/T/...) the temp cwd eats the whole row width
  # and the assertion fails locally while ubuntu CI (/tmp) is green. Pin
  # the stage to the same short temp root CI has so hook/CI agree.
  echo "🧪 Running no-key integration legs (MockLlmServer)..."
  local conc="${FA_DART_TEST_CONCURRENCY:-$(detect_test_concurrency)}"
  echo "   concurrency: ${conc:-default}"
  #
  # Flake budget (gh-1026): FA_GATE_PTY_RETRIES=N reruns ONLY the failed
  # files, up to N times, before the stage fails. The PTY/grid timing legs
  # are load-sensitive (the gh-1026 class: 3 red 2.5 h gate runs on an
  # unchanged head, a different ambient test red each time, every file
  # green in isolation) — the budget turns one flaky PTY case from a full
  # leg rerun into a minutes-scoped file rerun, mirroring CI's
  # retrigger-recovery behaviour (ci.yml watchdog: ONE retrigger, never a
  # blind rerun). 0 (the default) keeps the single-shot leg below
  # byte-identical. Files come from scripts/gate_failed_targets.py over
  # the dart json file-reporter log; when the log yields no targets
  # (crash before the reporter flushed) the stage fails WITHOUT a rerun —
  # never rerun blind.
  local retries="${FA_GATE_PTY_RETRIES:-0}"
  if [ "$retries" -le 0 ]; then
    TMPDIR="${FA_GATE_TMPDIR:-/tmp}" \
      dart test ${conc:+--concurrency=$conc} test/integration \
      --exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,perf,pty
    return
  fi
  local log="test-results/gate-integration-mock.json"
  mkdir -p test-results
  local targets="test/integration"
  local attempt=0
  while true; do
    attempt=$((attempt + 1))
    if TMPDIR="${FA_GATE_TMPDIR:-/tmp}" \
        dart test ${conc:+--concurrency=$conc} $targets \
        --exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,perf,pty \
        --file-reporter="json:$log"; then
      return 0
    fi
    if [ "$attempt" -gt "$retries" ]; then
      echo "❌ flake budget exhausted ($retries rerun(s)) — integration leg stays red" >&2
      exit 1
    fi
    local failed
    failed=$(python3 scripts/gate_failed_targets.py "$log")
    if [ -z "$failed" ]; then
      echo "   no failed-file targets in $log — not rerunning blind" >&2
      exit 1
    fi
    echo "🔁 flake budget: rerun $attempt/$retries — failed files only:" >&2
    printf '%s\n' "$failed" | sed 's/^/   /' >&2
    targets="$failed"
  done
}

stage_coverage() {
  if [ ! -d coverage ]; then
    echo "❌ coverage/ not found — run the test-core stage first" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  echo "📊 Formatting coverage to lcov..."
  dart run coverage:format_coverage --lcov -i coverage -o coverage/lcov.info
  echo "🔍 Checking line coverage (baseline: >= ${COVERAGE_BASELINE}%)..."
  if ! python3 scripts/check_coverage.py "$COVERAGE_BASELINE"; then
    echo "❌ QUALITY GATE FAILED — TEST COVERAGE (baseline ${COVERAGE_BASELINE}%)" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
}

**Root cause found.** The `guards` job's CRAP ratchet (threshold 12.0) fails on the PR's new code:

- `HostKeyResolver.resolveKey` — CC 15, **CRAP 15.0 at 100% coverage** → mathematically over the rat…

blocks.text:
Found it. Two offenders above the 12.0 CRAP threshold:

1. **`AgentTelemetry._record`** — CRAP 23.34, coverage 57.1%, CC 12. The targeted tests leave parts of the switch uncovered (MessageUpdateEvent firstToken fallback at line 181, ToolCallStuckEvent, maybe ToolCallHeartbeatEvent...). With the FULL suite coverage in CI it might better, but 57.1% with CC 12 → CRAP 23.3 > 12. Even with slightly better coverage in CI, still likely over. CC 12 itself means CRAP ≥ 12 even at 100% coverage! CC 12 at 100% = 12.0 — hmm, at exactly 12.0, is it > threshold? "Only down from here", threshold 12.0 — the existing worst offenders at CRAP 12 pass, so the check is CRAP > 12.0 fails. CC 12 fully covered = CRAP 12.0 → borderline pass. But at 57.1% → 23.34 → FAIL.

2. **`HostKeyResolver.resolveKey`** — CRAP 15.0 at CC 15, 100% coverage → 15 > 12 → **FAIL even with perfect coverage**. This is a hard fail in CI: the coverage is complete (100%), so CI's merged coverage also reads CC 15 → CRAP 15 > 12 → the CRAP ratchet fails. That's the root cause of the guards failure!

Note: the switch-expressions in `_message`/`_tail` apparently don't count per-case (CC 2 for `_message` — so crap4dart doesn't count switch expression cases, or counts them as 1 total). Good.

So the CRAP ratchet failure is real: `HostKeyResolver.resolveKey` CC 15 → CRAP 15 (> 12) even fully covered. And `AgentTelemetry._record` CC 12 with partial coverage → 23.34.

Wait — but let me confirm the formula: CRAP = comp² × (1 − cov)³ + comp. For CC 15, cov 100%: 15. Yes → 15 > 12 → fails. For CC 12, cov 57.1%: 144 × 0.429³ + 12 = 144 × 0.0789 + 12 = 11.36 + 12 = 23.36 ≈ 23.34 ✓.

In CI with the full suite, `AgentTelemetry._record` coverage might be higher (the full suite might exercise more of the switch — e.g. stuck-tool heartbeats might be covered by other tests? Unlikely — heartbeat/stuck events only come from stuckTool supervision tests, which are in the PR's own tests... but the PR's targeted tests I ran DO include the telemetry tests). Hmm — actually wait, maybe more of `_record` gets covered in CI: `AgentEndEvent` error path is covered... Let me see which parts are uncovered at 57.1%: the switch has cases: AgentStart ✓, TurnStart ✓, MessageUpdate firstToken (covered? the file-sink test uses hand-built events; the adapter test... the review thread says the `MessageUpdateEvent` fallback is a real path — presumably covered by adapter tests), ToolExecutionStart/End ✓ (integration wiring), ToolCallHeartbeat (maybe not — heartbeat events require stuckTool supervision in a long-running tool test), ToolCallStuck (probably not), TurnEnd ✓, AgentEnd ✓, default.

Whatever the exact CI coverage is, `HostKeyResolver.resolveKey` at CRAP 15 with 100% cov is a definite ratchet failure — that alone fails the guards job. And `_record` at CC 12/57.1% is another likely failure (CI coverage won't hit 100%: heartbeat/stuck paths need specific wiring; even if they are covered, CRAP = 12.0 exactly = borderline pass — too risky).

So the fix (TDD):

**Finding 1: `HostKeyResolver.resolveKey` CC 15 → CRAP 15 > 12.**
Fix: refactor to reduce CC below the ratchet — extract helper(s). The method does: canonical, chained resolution, pinned-twin registry leg, fromEnv computation, driftHint, missingKeyHint. Extract e.g. `_resolvePinnedTwin` / `_driftHint` / `_missingKeyHint` helpers. Each helper needs 100% coverage to keep CRAP = CC ≤ 12. Tests exist covering all these branches (the PR's resolver tests — 240 lines). Let me verify coverage of each extracted piece stays 100%.

**Finding 2: `AgentTelemetry._record` CC 12, cov 57.1% (targeted) → CRAP 23.34.**
Fix options: (a) increase coverage to 100% — requires tests for heartbeat/stuck/fallback paths; (b) reduce CC by splitting the switch; (c) both. blocks.text:
Empirical CC counting rules in crap4dart:
- `if`: +1 each ✓ (3 ifs → CC 4)
- ternary: +1 ✓
- **switch statement: +1 per case** (4 cases → CC 5)
- **switch expression: +0 (!)** — CC 1
- **stacked cases: +1 per case LABEL** (4 labels over 2 bodies → CC 5)
- `||`: +1 each (3 || → CC 5)
- collection-if: +0
- for/catch: +1 each
- when guard: case +1, `when` +1 (CC 3 = base + case + when)

So the plan for `_record`:
- Split into `_record` (run-phase switch: AgentStart, TurnStart, MessageUpdate+when, TurnEnd, AgentEnd, default → CC = 1+5+1(when) = 7) + `_recordToolEvent` (4 cases + default → CC 5-6).
- Dispatch: `if (event is Tool...) { _recordToolEvent(event); return; }` would add if+||s. Alternative: use a switch EXPRESSION or avoid the or-pattern...

Option: `_record` keeps ALL cases but tool cases just call `_recordToolEvent(event)` — stacked labels each +1: tool case labels = 4 stacked → +4, run cases 5 + when 1 → CC = 1 + 4 + 5 + 1 = 11. Too high.

Better: two independent switches is impossible one event without a pre-dispatch... Use stacked cases but ONLY 2: hmm.

Cleanest low-CC: pre-dispatch with a single `is` check against a helper... Dart has no multi-is. What about:

```dart
void _record(AgentEvent event) {
  if (event is ToolExecutionStartEvent ||
      event is ToolExecutionEndEvent ||
      event is ToolCallHeartbeatEvent ||
      event is ToolCallStuckEvent) {
    _recordToolEvent(event);
    return;
  }
  _recordRunPhase(event);
}
```
CC = 1 + 1(if) + 3(||) = 5. 
`_recordToolEvent`: switch statement, 4 cases (exhaustive over the four types? no — compiler can't know; needs default or end) → CC = 1+4+1(default) = 6. At 100% cov = 6. 
`_recordRunPhase`: switch with AgentStart, TurnStart, MessageUpdate+when, TurnEnd, AgentEnd, default → CC = 1+5+1 = 7. Existing tests cover it 100% → CRAP 7. 

Wait — can I do better? switch expression for _recordRunPhase: switch EXPRESSIONS count 0! But the cases have side effects and one has a when-guard... switch expressions support when-guards. Side effects in expression cases are fine (each branch an expression). E.g.:

```dart
void _recordRunPhase(AgentEvent event) => switch (event) {
  AgentStartEvent() => _onRunStart(),
  TurnStartEvent() => _emit(AgentTelemetryEventKind.turnStart),
  MessageUpdateEvent() when !_sawFirstToken => _onFirstStreamedUpdate(),
  TurnEndEvent(:final message) => _emit(..., stopReason: message.stopReason.name),
  AgentEndEvent() => _onAgentEnd(event),
  _ => null,  // hmm — expression must return a value; use void-ish
};
```
Each case returns void — switch expression arms returning void is allowed? The expression type would be void — `void switchExpr` — allowed in Dart? An expression switch whose arms all have type void: the switch expression's static type is void, and `void _recordRunPhase(AgentEvent event) => switch ...` works. Hmm, `when` guard +1 (when counts even in expressions? Probably same counting — probe didn't test switch-expression with when. Conservative: assume +1).

But honestly CC 7 @ 100% cov (CRAP 7) is comfortably under 12. And even if CI coverage dipped to 80%: 49×0.008+7 = 7.4. Totally safe. Keep switch STATEMENT (matches existing file style — `_record` was a statement switch; minimal diff).

# crap4dart configuration for flutter_agent_harness.
# https://github.com/IstiN/crap4dart

sources: [lib, bin]

exclude:
  - '**.g.dart'
  - '**.freezed.dart'
  - '**.mocks.dart'
  - 'build/**'
  - 'vendor/**'

crap:
  enabled: true
  # Current max CRAP score in the repo (2026-08-12 — GREEN zone after the
  # cleanup rounds 356.34 → 65.1 → 16 → 8 → 12; three TUI-only dispatchers
  # at CC 3 / 0% cov land at CRAP 12 — they need a real PTY to test). Only
  # down from here.
  threshold: 12.0
# NOTE: _listModels (provider_commands.dart) hits 20 with 0% coverage
# because it is line-mode-only output; it pre-dates the dial work. Fix
# separately — do not ratchet up for it.

coverage:
  # scripts/pre-commit regenerates this (dart test --coverage) right
  # before the CRAP step runs.
  lcov_path: coverage/lcov.info
  required: true
  branch_coverage: true
  # crap4dart 0.9.5 flipped the run_tests default to true — a bare
  # `analyze`/`check` would silently re-run the whole core suite first.
  # Coverage is regenerated explicitly (pre-commit hook, CI shard merge);
  # do not pay for it twice.
  run_tests: false

# ─── Gates (issue #447) ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# 0.9.5 default-enables ALL built-in gates; only broken_goldens is
# enforced here, everything else is disabled explicitly so a bare
# `check --staged` (pre-commit, core-only #433 split) means exactly the
# pixel gate. The flutter_app goldens live in flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml.
gates:
  loc: {enabled: false} # own ≤2800 gate (scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh)
  test_coverage: {enabled: false} # own ≥80% coverage-gate job
  complexity: {enabled: false} # CRAP ratchet above already covers it
  method_size: {enabled: false}
  nesting: {enabled: false}
  class_size: {enabled: false}
  weight_of_class: {enabled: false}
  unused_code: {enabled: false}
  unused_files: {enabled: false}
  banned_imports: {enabled: false}
  # Type-2 duplication gate (issue #1106, crap4dart 0.11.0). Renamed-clone
  # detection on top of the Type-1 default; the union with the raw pass can
  # only ADD findings, never lose exact copies. severity: warning starts
  # soft — escalate to error once the 13-file triage debt is paid
  # (follow-up, owner-side). The global jscpd <1% guards stay as-is.
  #
  # Two suppression channels with different contracts:
  # - `// crap:ignore` (needs ignorable: true) = a JUSTIFIED structural
  #   twin, suppressed forever, with a one-line reason in the comment.
  # - `.crap-baseline.json` (via `check --baseline`) = LEGACY debt; the
  #   committed snapshot must only SHRINK: after each triage batch re-run
  #   `dart pub global run crap4dart check --save-baseline` and commit the
  #   only-down diff, or the snapshot rots and starts masking shifts.
  #
  # WINDOW (until severity flips to error): the gate never fails a build —
  # new (not-baselined) duplication only surfaces as a `[WARN]` line in
  # `check` output. Enforcement becomes hard exactly when the owner-side
  # escalation lands; from then on any finding outside the two channels
  # fails CI/pre-commit.
  duplication:
    enabled: true
    severity: warning
    ignorable: true # enables `// crap:ignore` for justified structural twins
    ignore_locals: true # Type-2: rename locals before hashing (API names stay)
    ignore_literals: false # keeps l10n/theme/symbol tables out
    sources: # cross-module scope from #487
      - flutter_app/lib
      - packages/fa_ui/lib
      - packages/fa_llm/lib
  file_naming: {enabled: false}
  magic_constants: {enabled: false}
  test_assertions: {enabled: false}
  folder_structure: {enabled: false}
  external: {enabled: false}
  public_docs: {enabled: false}
  golden: {enabled: false} # flutter-only gate (core is not a Flutter project)
  accessibility: {enabled: false}
  hardcoded_strings: {enabled: false}

  # Pixel gate over core test/ goldens — none exist today, so this is a
  # no-op that guards the future (issue #447 AC: "and core test/ goldens
  # if any appear"). WARNING, same rationale as flutter_app: the 0.9.5
  # detector misses the Ahem-solid-rect and hollow-square classes and
  # false-positives on V-converging shapes; flip to error when the
  # upstream detector fixes land.
  broken_goldens:
    enabled: true
    severity: warning
    dirs: [test]
    exclude:
      # TUI screenshots, not goldens: amber/yellow text on the dark theme
      # trips the stripe heuristic (measured 14/14 "overflow stripes" —
      # the same yellow-on-dark detector bug the issue documents for
      # apps_panel/panel_dark). Revisit when upstream fixes land.

# ── Stage implementations ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
stage_size() {
  # Hook mode scopes the guard to the STAGED Dart files: the guard ratchets
  # what a commit touches, so a pre-existing oversized file elsewhere (e.g.
  # flutter_app/lib/services/agent_service.dart, which ci.yml's guard never
  # measures — it scans lib/test/example only) cannot block an unrelated
  # commit. Non-hook runs keep the whole-tree scan below.
  if [ "$HOOK_MODE" -eq 1 ]; then
    local violations
    violations=$(git diff --cached --name-only --diff-filter=ACM \
      | grep '\.dart$' \
      | grep -vE '\.g\.dart$|\.freezed\.dart$|\.mocks\.dart$|bridge_generated|app_localizations|localizations_' \
      | while IFS= read -r f; do
          [ -f "$f" ] || continue
          lines=$(wc -l < "$f")
          if [ "$lines" -gt "$MAX_LINES" ]; then echo "$f: $lines lines"; fi
        done || true)
    if [ -n "$violations" ]; then
      echo "❌ QUALITY GATE FAILED — FILE SIZE (max $MAX_LINES lines)" >&2
      echo "$violations" >&2
      exit 1
    fi
    return 0
  fi
  # Same find-exec guard as ci.yml / pre-commit: no dart file over MAX_LINES.
  local dirs=""
  local d
  for d in lib test example bin; do
    [ -d "$d" ] && dirs="$dirs $d"
  done
  if [ "$APP_IN_SCOPE" -eq 1 ] && [ -d flutter_app/lib ]; then
    dirs="$dirs flutter_app/lib"
  fi
  local violations
  violations=$(find $dirs -name '*.dart' \
    ! -name '*.g.dart' ! -name '*.freezed.dart' ! -name '*.mocks.dart' \
    ! -name '*bridge_generated*.dart' ! -name '*app_localizations*.dart' \
    ! -name '*localizations_*.dart' \
    -exec sh -c 'lines=$(wc -l < "$1"); if [ "$lines" -gt '"$MAX_LINES"' ]; then echo "$1: $lines lines"; fi' _ {} \;)
  if [ -n "$violations" ]; then
    echo "❌ QUALITY GATE FAILED — FILE SIZE (max $MAX_LINES lines)" >&2
    echo "$violations" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
}

stage_analyze() {

  if [ "$APP_IN_SCOPE" -eq 1 ] && command -v flutter >/dev/null 2>&1; then

    (cd flutter_app && flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos --no-fatal-warnings)
    FLUTTER_ANALYZED=1
  fi
}

stage_test_core() {
  echo "🧪 Running dart test --coverage (excluding integration tests)..."
  rm -rf coverage
  local conc="${FA_DART_TEST_CONCURRENCY:-$(detect_test_concurrency)}"
  echo "   concurrency: ${conc:-default}"
  dart test ${conc:+--concurrency=$conc} --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration
  # gh-1033 (review thread 7 + gate wiring): the fa jsr delegate suites are
  # integration-tagged — the PTY leg's CLI coverage ratchet measures
  # lib/src/cli hits from them — so the unit run above skips them. Their
  # hits must ALSO reach the unit-side lcov consumers (>= 80% ratchet, PR
  # diff-coverage, CRAP: jsr_cli.dart at 0% line coverage reads CRAP 156
  # against the 12.0 ceiling), so the trio runs into the SAME coverage/
  # dir; format_coverage merges the per-isolate files. Keep this list in
  # sync with ci.yml (test-core shard 0) and nightly.yml.
  dart test ${conc:+--concurrency=$conc} --tags integration \
    test/cli/jsr_cli_test.dart \
    test/cli/cli_args_jsr_test.dart \
    test/cli/agent_cli_jsr_test.dart \
    --coverage=coverage
}

stage_integration_mock() {
  # Issue #551: the no-key integration legs run on EVERY PR that touches
  # them — MockLlmServer scenarios, no secrets, no network, so they cannot
  # rot silently between releases (#538 class). Real-provider files carry
  # the `llm` tag and stay in the tag-only smoke job; browser-ext owns its
  # own workflow; perf has the #303 per-PR trajectory gate; `pty` marks
  # child-agent-spawn tests (issue #553) — nightly-only, unbounded boot time.
  #
  # TMPDIR normalization (macOS hook parity): several PTY legs assert the
  # status row still shows `· ctx ` — with macOS's per-user temp root
  # (/var/folders/<30 chars>/T/...) the temp cwd eats the whole row width
  # and the assertion fails locally while ubuntu CI (/tmp) is green. Pin
  # the stage to the same short temp root CI has so hook/CI agree.
  echo "🧪 Running no-key integration legs (MockLlmServer)..."
  local conc="${FA_DART_TEST_CONCURRENCY:-$(detect_test_concurrency)}"
  echo "   concurrency: ${conc:-default}"
  #
  # Flake budget (gh-1026): FA_GATE_PTY_RETRIES=N reruns ONLY the failed
  # files, up to N times, before the stage fails. The PTY/grid timing legs
  # are load-sensitive (the gh-1026 class: 3 red 2.5 h gate runs on an
  # unchanged head, a different ambient test red each time, every file
  # green in isolation) — the budget turns one flaky PTY case from a full
  # leg rerun into a minutes-scoped file rerun, mirroring CI's
  # retrigger-recovery behaviour (ci.yml watchdog: ONE retrigger, never a
  # blind rerun). 0 (the default) keeps the single-shot leg below
  # byte-identical. Files come from scripts/gate_failed_targets.py over
  # the dart json file-reporter log; when the log yields no targets
  # (crash before the reporter flushed) the stage fails WITHOUT a rerun —
  # never rerun blind.
  local retries="${FA_GATE_PTY_RETRIES:-0}"
  if [ "$retries" -le 0 ]; then
    TMPDIR="${FA_GATE_TMPDIR:-/tmp}" \
      dart test ${conc:+--concurrency=$conc} test/integration \
      --exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,perf,pty
    return
  fi
  local log="test-results/gate-integration-mock.json"
  mkdir -p test-results
  local targets="test/integration"
  local attempt=0
  while true; do
    attempt=$((attempt + 1))
    if TMPDIR="${FA_GATE_TMPDIR:-/tmp}" \
        dart test ${conc:+--concurrency=$conc} $targets \
        --exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,perf,pty \
        --file-reporter="json:$log"; then
      return 0
    fi
    if [ "$attempt" -gt "$retries" ]; then
      echo "❌ flake budget exhausted ($retries rerun(s)) — integration leg stays red" >&2
      exit 1
    fi
    local failed
    failed=$(python3 scripts/gate_failed_targets.py "$log")
    if [ -z "$failed" ]; then
      echo "   no failed-file targets in $log — not rerunning blind" >&2
      exit 1
    fi
    echo "🔁 flake budget: rerun $attempt/$retries — failed files only:" >&2
    printf '%s\n' "$failed" | sed 's/^/   /' >&2
    targets="$failed"
  done
}

stage_coverage() {
  if [ ! -d coverage ]; then
    echo "❌ coverage/ not found — run the test-core stage first" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  echo "📊 Formatting coverage to lcov..."
  dart run coverage:format_coverage --lcov -i coverage -o coverage/lcov.info
  echo "🔍 Checking line coverage (baseline: >= ${COVERAGE_BASELINE}%)..."
  if ! python3 scripts/check_coverage.py "$COVERAGE_BASELINE"; then
    echo "❌ QUALITY GATE FAILED — TEST COVERAGE (baseline ${COVERAGE_BASELINE}%)" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
}

Empirical CC counting rules in crap4dart:
- `if`: +1 each ✓ (3 ifs → CC 4)
- ternary: +1 ✓
- **switch statement: +1 per case** (4 cases → CC 5)
- **switch expression: +0 (!)** — CC 1
- **stacked cases: +1 per case LABEL** (4 labels over 2 bodies → CC 5)
- `||`: +1 each (3 || → CC 5)
- collection-if: +0
- for/catch: +1 each
- when guard: case +1, `when` +1 (CC 3 = base + case + when)

So the plan for `_record`:
- Split into `_record` (run-phase switch: AgentStart, TurnStart, MessageUpdate+when, TurnEnd, AgentEnd, default → CC = 1+5+1(when) = 7) + `_recordToolEvent` (4 cases + default → CC 5-6).

# ── Stage implementations ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
stage_size() {
  # Hook mode scopes the guard to the STAGED Dart files: the guard ratchets
  # what a commit touches, so a pre-existing oversized file elsewhere (e.g.
  # flutter_app/lib/services/agent_service.dart, which ci.yml's guard never
  # measures — it scans lib/test/example only) cannot block an unrelated
  # commit. Non-hook runs keep the whole-tree scan below.
  if [ "$HOOK_MODE" -eq 1 ]; then
    local violations
    violations=$(git diff --cached --name-only --diff-filter=ACM \
      | grep '\.dart$' \
      | grep -vE '\.g\.dart$|\.freezed\.dart$|\.mocks\.dart$|bridge_generated|app_localizations|localizations_' \
      | while IFS= read -r f; do
          [ -f "$f" ] || continue
          lines=$(wc -l < "$f")
          if [ "$lines" -gt "$MAX_LINES" ]; then echo "$f: $lines lines"; fi
        done || true)
    if [ -n "$violations" ]; then
      echo "❌ QUALITY GATE FAILED — FILE SIZE (max $MAX_LINES lines)" >&2
      echo "$violations" >&2
      exit 1
    fi
    return 0
  fi
  # Same find-exec guard as ci.yml / pre-commit: no dart file over MAX_LINES.
  local dirs=""
  local d
  for d in lib test example bin; do
    [ -d "$d" ] && dirs="$dirs $d"
  done
  if [ "$APP_IN_SCOPE" -eq 1 ] && [ -d flutter_app/lib ]; then
    dirs="$dirs flutter_app/lib"
  fi
  local violations
  violations=$(find $dirs -name '*.dart' \
    ! -name '*.g.dart' ! -name '*.freezed.dart' ! -name '*.mocks.dart' \
    ! -name '*bridge_generated*.dart' ! -name '*app_localizations*.dart' \
    ! -name '*localizations_*.dart' \
    -exec sh -c 'lines=$(wc -l < "$1"); if [ "$lines" -gt '"$MAX_LINES"' ]; then echo "$1: $lines lines"; fi' _ {} \;)
  if [ -n "$violations" ]; then
    echo "❌ QUALITY GATE FAILED — FILE SIZE (max $MAX_LINES lines)" >&2
    echo "$violations" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
}

stage_analyze() {
  echo "🔍 Running dart analyze..."
  dart analyze
  if [ "$APP_IN_SCOPE" -eq 1 ] && command -v flutter >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    ensure_app_placeholders
    echo "🔍 Running flutter analyze (flutter_app)..."
    (cd flutter_app && flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos --no-fatal-warnings)
    FLUTTER_ANALYZED=1
  fi
}

stage_test_core() {
  echo "🧪 Running dart test --coverage (excluding integration tests)..."
  rm -rf coverage
  local conc="${FA_DART_TEST_CONCURRENCY:-$(detect_test_concurrency)}"
  echo "   concurrency: ${conc:-default}"
  dart test ${conc:+--concurrency=$conc} --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration
  # gh-1033 (review thread 7 + gate wiring): the fa jsr delegate suites are
  # integration-tagged — the PTY leg's CLI coverage ratchet measures
  # lib/src/cli hits from them — so the unit run above skips them. Their
  # hits must ALSO reach the unit-side lcov consumers (>= 80% ratchet, PR
  # diff-coverage, CRAP: jsr_cli.dart at 0% line coverage reads CRAP 156
  # against the 12.0 ceiling), so the trio runs into the SAME coverage/
  # dir; format_coverage merges the per-isolate files. Keep this list in
  # sync with ci.yml (test-core shard 0) and nightly.yml.
  dart test ${conc:+--concurrency=$conc} --tags integration \
    test/cli/jsr_cli_test.dart \
    test/cli/cli_args_jsr_test.dart \
    test/cli/agent_cli_jsr_test.dart \
    --coverage=coverage
}

stage_integration_mock() {
  # Issue #551: the no-key integration legs run on EVERY PR that touches
  # them — MockLlmServer scenarios, no secrets, no network, so they cannot
  # rot silently between releases (#538 class). Real-provider files carry
  # the `llm` tag and stay in the tag-only smoke job; browser-ext owns its
  # own workflow; perf has the #303 per-PR trajectory gate; `pty` marks
  # child-agent-spawn tests (issue #553) — nightly-only, unbounded boot time.
  #
  # TMPDIR normalization (macOS hook parity): several PTY legs assert the
  # status row still shows `· ctx ` — with macOS's per-user temp root
  # (/var/folders/<30 chars>/T/...) the temp cwd eats the whole row width
  # and the assertion fails locally while ubuntu CI (/tmp) is green. Pin
  # the stage to the same short temp root CI has so hook/CI agree.
  echo "🧪 Running no-key integration legs (MockLlmServer)..."
  local conc="${FA_DART_TEST_CONCURRENCY:-$(detect_test_concurrency)}"
  echo "   concurrency: ${conc:-default}"
  #
  # Flake budget (gh-1026): FA_GATE_PTY_RETRIES=N reruns ONLY the failed
  # files, up to N times, before the stage fails. The PTY/grid timing legs
  # are load-sensitive (the gh-1026 class: 3 red 2.5 h gate runs on an
  # unchanged head, a different ambient test red each time, every file
  # green in isolation) — the budget turns one flaky PTY case from a full
  # leg rerun into a minutes-scoped file rerun, mirroring CI's
  # retrigger-recovery behaviour (ci.yml watchdog: ONE retrigger, never a
  # blind rerun). 0 (the default) keeps the single-shot leg below
  # byte-identical. Files come from scripts/gate_failed_targets.py over
  # the dart json file-reporter log; when the log yields no targets
  # (crash before the reporter flushed) the stage fails WITHOUT a rerun —
  # never rerun blind.
  local retries="${FA_GATE_PTY_RETRIES:-0}"
  if [ "$retries" -le 0 ]; then
    TMPDIR="${FA_GATE_TMPDIR:-/tmp}" \
      dart test ${conc:+--concurrency=$conc} test/integration \
      --exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,perf,pty
    return
  fi
  local log="test-results/gate-integration-mock.json"
  mkdir -p test-results
  local targets="test/integration"
  local attempt=0
  while true; do
    attempt=$((attempt + 1))
    if TMPDIR="${FA_GATE_TMPDIR:-/tmp}" \
        dart test ${conc:+--concurrency=$conc} $targets \
        --exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,perf,pty \
        --file-reporter="json:$log"; then
      return 0
    fi
    if [ "$attempt" -gt "$retries" ]; then
      echo "❌ flake budget exhausted ($retries rerun(s)) — integration leg stays red" >&2
      exit 1
    fi
    local failed
    failed=$(python3 scripts/gate_failed_targets.py "$log")
    if [ -z "$failed" ]; then
      echo "   no failed-file targets in $log — not rerunning blind" >&2
      exit 1
    fi
    echo "🔁 flake budget: rerun $attempt/$retries — failed files only:" >&2
    printf '%s\n' "$failed" | sed 's/^/   /' >&2
    targets="$failed"
  done
}

stage_coverage() {
  if [ ! -d coverage ]; then
    echo "❌ coverage/ not found — run the test-core stage first" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  echo "📊 Formatting coverage to lcov..."
  dart run coverage:format_coverage --lcov -i coverage -o coverage/lcov.info
  echo "🔍 Checking line coverage (baseline: >= ${COVERAGE_BASELINE}%)..."
  if ! python3 scripts/check_coverage.py "$COVERAGE_BASELINE"; then
    echo "❌ QUALITY GATE FAILED — TEST COVERAGE (baseline ${COVERAGE_BASELINE}%)" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
}

Empirical CC counting rules in crap4dart:
- `if`: +1 each ✓ (3 ifs → CC 4)
- ternary: +1 ✓
- **switch statement: +1 per case** (4 cases → CC 5)
- **switch expression: +0 (!)** — CC 1
- **stacked cases: +1 per case LABEL** (4 labels over 2 bodies → CC 5)
- `||`: +1 each (3 || → CC 5)
- collection-if: +0
- for/catch: +1 each
- when guard: case +1, `when` +1 (CC 3 = base + case + when)

So the plan for `_record`:
- Split into `_record` (run-phase switch: AgentStart, TurnStart, MessageUpdate+when, TurnEnd, AgentEnd, default → CC = 1+5+1(when) = 7) + `_recordToolEvent` (4 cases + default → CC 5-6).
- Dispatch: `if (event is Tool...) { _recordToolEvent(event); return; }` would add if+||s. Alternative: use a switch EXPRESSION or avoid the or-pattern...

Option: `_record` keeps ALL cases but tool cases just call `_recordToolEvent(event)` — stacked labels each +1: tool case labels = 4 stacked → +4, run cases 5 + when 1 → CC = 1 + 4 + 5 + 1 = 11. Too high.

Better: two independent switches is impossible one event without a pre-dispatch... Use stacked cases but ONLY 2: hmm.

Cleanest low-CC: pre-dispatch with a single `is` check against a helper... Dart has no multi-is. What about:

```dart
void _record(AgentEvent event) {
  if (event is ToolExecutionStartEvent ||
      event is ToolExecutionEndEvent ||
      event is ToolCallHeartbeatEvent ||
      event is ToolCallStuckEvent) {
    _recordToolEvent(event);
    return;
  }
  _recordRunPhase(event);
}
```
CC = 1 + 1(if) + 3(||) = 5. 
`_recordToolEvent`: switch statement, 4 cases (exhaustive over the four types? no — compiler can't know; needs default or end) → CC = 1+4+1(default) = 6. At 100% cov = 6. 
`_recordRunPhase`: switch with AgentStart, TurnStart, MessageUpdate+when, TurnEnd, AgentEnd, default → CC = 1+5+1 = 7. Existing tests cover it 100% → CRAP 7.

```dart
void _recordRunPhase(AgentEvent event) => switch (event) {
  AgentStartEvent() => _onRunStart(),
  TurnStartEvent() => _emit(AgentTelemetryEventKind.turnStart),

  AgentEndEvent() => _onAgentEnd(event),
  _ => null,  // hmm — expression must return a value; use void-ish
};
```
Each case returns void — switch expression arms returning void is allowed? The expression type would be void — `void switchExpr` — allowed in Dart? An expression switch whose arms all have type void: the switch expression's static type is void, and `void _recordRunPhase(AgentEvent event) => switch ...` works. Hmm, `when` guard +1 (when counts even in expressions? Probably same counting — probe didn't test switch-expression with when. Conservative: assume +1).

# ── Stage implementations ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
stage_size() {
  # Hook mode scopes the guard to the STAGED Dart files: the guard ratchets
  # what a commit touches, so a pre-existing oversized file elsewhere (e.g.
  # flutter_app/lib/services/agent_service.dart, which ci.yml's guard never
  # measures — it scans lib/test/example only) cannot block an unrelated
  # commit. Non-hook runs keep the whole-tree scan below.
  if [ "$HOOK_MODE" -eq 1 ]; then
    local violations
    violations=$(git diff --cached --name-only --diff-filter=ACM \
      | grep '\.dart$' \
      | grep -vE '\.g\.dart$|\.freezed\.dart$|\.mocks\.dart$|bridge_generated|app_localizations|localizations_' \
      | while IFS= read -r f; do
          [ -f "$f" ] || continue
          lines=$(wc -l < "$f")
          if [ "$lines" -gt "$MAX_LINES" ]; then echo "$f: $lines lines"; fi
        done || true)
    if [ -n "$violations" ]; then
      echo "❌ QUALITY GATE FAILED — FILE SIZE (max $MAX_LINES lines)" >&2
      echo "$violations" >&2
      exit 1
    fi
    return 0
  fi
  # Same find-exec guard as ci.yml / pre-commit: no dart file over MAX_LINES.
  local dirs=""
  local d
  for d in lib test example bin; do
    [ -d "$d" ] && dirs="$dirs $d"
  done
  if [ "$APP_IN_SCOPE" -eq 1 ] && [ -d flutter_app/lib ]; then
    dirs="$dirs flutter_app/lib"
  fi
  local violations
  violations=$(find $dirs -name '*.dart' \
    ! -name '*.g.dart' ! -name '*.freezed.dart' ! -name '*.mocks.dart' \
    ! -name '*bridge_generated*.dart' ! -name '*app_localizations*.dart' \
    ! -name '*localizations_*.dart' \
    -exec sh -c 'lines=$(wc -l < "$1"); if [ "$lines" -gt '"$MAX_LINES"' ]; then echo "$1: $lines lines"; fi' _ {} \;)
  if [ -n "$violations" ]; then
    echo "❌ QUALITY GATE FAILED — FILE SIZE (max $MAX_LINES lines)" >&2
    echo "$violations" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
}

stage_analyze() {
  echo "🔍 Running dart analyze..."
  dart analyze
  if [ "$APP_IN_SCOPE" -eq 1 ] && command -v flutter >/dev/null 2>&1; then

    echo "🔍 Running flutter analyze (flutter_app)..."
    (cd flutter_app && flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos --no-fatal-warnings)
    FLUTTER_ANALYZED=1
  fi
}

stage_test_core() {
  echo "🧪 Running dart test --coverage (excluding integration tests)..."
  rm -rf coverage
  local conc="${FA_DART_TEST_CONCURRENCY:-$(detect_test_concurrency)}"
  echo "   concurrency: ${conc:-default}"
  dart test ${conc:+--concurrency=$conc} --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration
  # gh-1033 (review thread 7 + gate wiring): the fa jsr delegate suites are
  # integration-tagged — the PTY leg's CLI coverage ratchet measures
  # lib/src/cli hits from them — so the unit run above skips them. Their
  # hits must ALSO reach the unit-side lcov consumers (>= 80% ratchet, PR
  # diff-coverage, CRAP: jsr_cli.dart at 0% line coverage reads CRAP 156
  # against the 12.0 ceiling), so the trio runs into the SAME coverage/
  # dir; format_coverage merges the per-isolate files. Keep this list in
  # sync with ci.yml (test-core shard 0) and nightly.yml.
  dart test ${conc:+--concurrency=$conc} --tags integration \
    test/cli/jsr_cli_test.dart \
    test/cli/cli_args_jsr_test.dart \
    test/cli/agent_cli_jsr_test.dart \
    --coverage=coverage
}

stage_integration_mock() {
  # Issue #551: the no-key integration legs run on EVERY PR that touches
  # them — MockLlmServer scenarios, no secrets, no network, so they cannot
  # rot silently between releases (#538 class). Real-provider files carry
  # the `llm` tag and stay in the tag-only smoke job; browser-ext owns its
  # own workflow; perf has the #303 per-PR trajectory gate; `pty` marks
  # child-agent-spawn tests (issue #553) — nightly-only, unbounded boot time.
  #
  # TMPDIR normalization (macOS hook parity): several PTY legs assert the
  # status row still shows `· ctx ` — with macOS's per-user temp root
  # (/var/folders/<30 chars>/T/...) the temp cwd eats the whole row width
  # and the assertion fails locally while ubuntu CI (/tmp) is green. Pin
  # the stage to the same short temp root CI has so hook/CI agree.
  echo "🧪 Running no-key integration legs (MockLlmServer)..."
  local conc="${FA_DART_TEST_CONCURRENCY:-$(detect_test_concurrency)}"
  echo "   concurrency: ${conc:-default}"
  #
  # Flake budget (gh-1026): FA_GATE_PTY_RETRIES=N reruns ONLY the failed
  # files, up to N times, before the stage fails. The PTY/grid timing legs
  # are load-sensitive (the gh-1026 class: 3 red 2.5 h gate runs on an
  # unchanged head, a different ambient test red each time, every file
  # green in isolation) — the budget turns one flaky PTY case from a full
  # leg rerun into a minutes-scoped file rerun, mirroring CI's
  # retrigger-recovery behaviour (ci.yml watchdog: ONE retrigger, never a
  # blind rerun). 0 (the default) keeps the single-shot leg below
  # byte-identical. Files come from scripts/gate_failed_targets.py over
  # the dart json file-reporter log; when the log yields no targets
  # (crash before the reporter flushed) the stage fails WITHOUT a rerun —
  # never rerun blind.
  local retries="${FA_GATE_PTY_RETRIES:-0}"
  if [ "$retries" -le 0 ]; then
    TMPDIR="${FA_GATE_TMPDIR:-/tmp}" \
      dart test ${conc:+--concurrency=$conc} test/integration \
      --exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,perf,pty
    return
  fi
  local log="test-results/gate-integration-mock.json"
  mkdir -p test-results
  local targets="test/integration"
  local attempt=0
  while true; do
    attempt=$((attempt + 1))
    if TMPDIR="${FA_GATE_TMPDIR:-/tmp}" \
        dart test ${conc:+--concurrency=$conc} $targets \
        --exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,perf,pty \
        --file-reporter="json:$log"; then
      return 0
    fi
    if [ "$attempt" -gt "$retries" ]; then
      echo "❌ flake budget exhausted ($retries rerun(s)) — integration leg stays red" >&2
      exit 1
    fi
    local failed
    failed=$(python3 scripts/gate_failed_targets.py "$log")
    if [ -z "$failed" ]; then
      echo "   no failed-file targets in $log — not rerunning blind" >&2
      exit 1
    fi
    echo "🔁 flake budget: rerun $attempt/$retries — failed files only:" >&2
    printf '%s\n' "$failed" | sed 's/^/   /' >&2
    targets="$failed"
  done
}

stage_coverage() {
  if [ ! -d coverage ]; then
    echo "❌ coverage/ not found — run the test-core stage first" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  echo "📊 Formatting coverage to lcov..."
  dart run coverage:format_coverage --lcov -i coverage -o coverage/lcov.info
  echo "🔍 Checking line coverage (baseline: >= ${COVERAGE_BASELINE}%)..."
  if ! python3 scripts/check_coverage.py "$COVERAGE_BASELINE"; then
    echo "❌ QUALITY GATE FAILED — TEST COVERAGE (baseline ${COVERAGE_BASELINE}%)" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
}

But at 57.1% → 23.34 → FAIL.

This is a hard fail in CI: the coverage is complete (100%), so CI's merged coverage also reads CC 15 → CRAP 15 > 12 → the CRAP ratchet fails. That's the root cause of the guards failure!

Note: the switch-expressions in `_message`/`_tail` apparently don't count per-case (CC 2 for `_message` — so crap4dart doesn't count switch expression cases, or counts them as 1 total). Good.

So the CRAP ratchet failure is real: `HostKeyResolver.resolveKey` CC 15 → CRAP 15 (> 12) even fully covered. And `AgentTelemetry._record` CC 12 with partial coverage → 23.34.

Wait — but let me confirm the formula: CRAP = comp² × (1 − cov)³ + comp. For CC 15, cov 100%: 15. Yes → 15 > 12 → fails. For CC 12, cov 57.1%: 144 × 0.429³ + 12 = 144 × 0.0789 + 12 = 11.36 + 12 = 23.36 ≈ 23.34 ✓.

In CI with the full suite, `AgentTelemetry._record` coverage might be higher (the full suite might exercise more of the switch — e.g. stuck-tool heartbeats might be covered by other tests? To pass: either CC ≤ 3 at that coverage (3 + 9×0.1849... wait CC 3 cov 57%: 9×0.0789+3 = 3.71 fine), or raise coverage to ~100% (CC 12 at 100% = 12.0 — borderline pass but scary), or reduce CC to ≤ 8 AND raise coverage: CC 8 cov 90%: 64×0.001+8 = 8.06 fine. blocks.text:
Empirical CC counting rules in crap4dart:
- `if`: +1 each ✓ (3 ifs → CC 4)
- ternary: +1 ✓
- **switch statement: +1 per case** (4 cases → CC 5)
- **switch expression: +0 (!)** — CC 1
- **stacked cases: +1 per case LABEL** (4 labels over 2 bodies → CC 5)
- `||`: +1 each (3 || → CC 5)
- collection-if: +0
- for/catch: +1 each
- when guard: case +1, `when` +1 (CC 3 = base + case + when)

So the plan for `_record`:
- Split into `_record` (run-phase switch: AgentStart, TurnStart, MessageUpdate+when, TurnEnd, AgentEnd, default → CC = 1+5+1(when) = 7) + `_recordToolEvent` (4 cases + default → CC 5-6).
- Dispatch: `if (event is Tool...) { _recordToolEvent(event); return; }` would add if+||s. Alternative: use a switch EXPRESSION or avoid the or-pattern...

Option: `_record` keeps ALL cases but tool cases just call `_recordToolEvent(event)` — stacked labels each +1: tool case labels = 4 stacked → +4, run cases 5 + when 1 → CC = 1 + 4 + 5 + 1 = 11. Too high.

Better: two independent switches is impossible one event without a pre-dispatch... Use stacked cases but ONLY 2: hmm.

Cleanest low-CC: pre-dispatch with a single `is` check against a helper... Dart has no multi-is. What about:

```dart
void _record(AgentEvent event) {
  if (event is ToolExecutionStartEvent ||
      event is ToolExecutionEndEvent ||
      event is ToolCallHeartbeatEvent ||
      event is ToolCallStuckEvent) {
    _recordToolEvent(event);
    return;
  }
  _recordRunPhase(event);
}
```
CC = 1 + 1(if) + 3(||) = 5. 
`_recordToolEvent`: switch statement, 4 cases (exhaustive over the four types? no — compiler can't know; needs default or end) → CC = 1+4+1(default) = 6. At 100% cov = 6. 
`_recordRunPhase`: switch with AgentStart, TurnStart, MessageUpdate+when, TurnEnd, AgentEnd, default → CC = 1+5+1 = 7. Existing tests cover it 100% → CRAP 7. 

Wait — can I do better? switch expression for _recordRunPhase: switch EXPRESSIONS count 0! But the cases have side effects and one has a when-guard... switch expressions support when-guards. Side effects in expression cases are fine (each branch an expression). E.g.:

```dart
void _recordRunPhase(AgentEvent event) => switch (event) {
  AgentStartEvent() => _onRunStart(),
  TurnStartEvent() => _emit(AgentTelemetryEventKind.turnStart),
  MessageUpdateEvent() when !_sawFirstToken => _onFirstStreamedUpdate(),
  TurnEndEvent(:final message) => _emit(..., stopReason: message.stopReason.name),
  AgentEndEvent() => _onAgentEnd(event),
  _ => null,  // hmm — expression must return a value; use void-ish
};
```
Each case returns void — switch expression arms returning void is allowed? The expression type would be void — `void switchExpr` — allowed in Dart? An expression switch whose arms all have type void: the switch expression's static type is void, and `void _recordRunPhase(AgentEvent event) => switch ...` works. Hmm, `when` guard +1 (when counts even in expressions? Probably same counting — probe didn't test switch-expression with when. Conservative: assume +1).

But honestly CC 7 @ 100% cov (CRAP 7) is comfortably under 12. And even if CI coverage dipped to 80%: 49×0.008+7 = 7.4. Totally safe. Keep switch STATEMENT (matches existing file style — `_record` was a statement switch; minimal diff).

# ── Stage implementations ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
stage_size() {
  # Hook mode scopes the guard to the STAGED Dart files: the guard ratchets
  # what a commit touches, so a pre-existing oversized file elsewhere (e.g.
  # flutter_app/lib/services/agent_service.dart, which ci.yml's guard never
  # measures — it scans lib/test/example only) cannot block an unrelated
  # commit. Non-hook runs keep the whole-tree scan below.
  if [ "$HOOK_MODE" -eq 1 ]; then
    local violations
    violations=$(git diff --cached --name-only --diff-filter=ACM \
      | grep '\.dart$' \
      | grep -vE '\.g\.dart$|\.freezed\.dart$|\.mocks\.dart$|bridge_generated|app_localizations|localizations_' \
      | while IFS= read -r f; do
          [ -f "$f" ] || continue
          lines=$(wc -l < "$f")
          if [ "$lines" -gt "$MAX_LINES" ]; then echo "$f: $lines lines"; fi
        done || true)
    if [ -n "$violations" ]; then
      echo "❌ QUALITY GATE FAILED — FILE SIZE (max $MAX_LINES lines)" >&2
      echo "$violations" >&2
      exit 1
    fi
    return 0
  fi
  # Same find-exec guard as ci.yml / pre-commit: no dart file over MAX_LINES.
  local dirs=""
  local d
  for d in lib test example bin; do
    [ -d "$d" ] && dirs="$dirs $d"
  done
  if [ "$APP_IN_SCOPE" -eq 1 ] && [ -d flutter_app/lib ]; then
    dirs="$dirs flutter_app/lib"
  fi
  local violations
  violations=$(find $dirs -name '*.dart' \
    ! -name '*.g.dart' ! -name '*.freezed.dart' ! -name '*.mocks.dart' \
    ! -name '*bridge_generated*.dart' ! -name '*app_localizations*.dart' \
    ! -name '*localizations_*.dart' \
    -exec sh -c 'lines=$(wc -l < "$1"); if [ "$lines" -gt '"$MAX_LINES"' ]; then echo "$1: $lines lines"; fi' _ {} \;)
  if [ -n "$violations" ]; then
    echo "❌ QUALITY GATE FAILED — FILE SIZE (max $MAX_LINES lines)" >&2
    echo "$violations" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
}

stage_analyze() {
  echo "🔍 Running dart analyze..."
  dart analyze
  if [ "$APP_IN_SCOPE" -eq 1 ] && command -v flutter >/dev/null 2>&1; then

    echo "🔍 Running flutter analyze (flutter_app)..."

stage_test_core() {
  echo "🧪 Running dart test --coverage (excluding integration tests)..."
  rm -rf coverage
  local conc="${FA_DART_TEST_CONCURRENCY:-$(detect_test_concurrency)}"
  echo "   concurrency: ${conc:-default}"
  dart test ${conc:+--concurrency=$conc} --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration
  # gh-1033 (review thread 7 + gate wiring): the fa jsr delegate suites are
  # integration-tagged — the PTY leg's CLI coverage ratchet measures
  # lib/src/cli hits from them — so the unit run above skips them. Their
  # hits must ALSO reach the unit-side lcov consumers (>= 80% ratchet, PR
  # diff-coverage, CRAP: jsr_cli.dart at 0% line coverage reads CRAP 156
  # against the 12.0 ceiling), so the trio runs into the SAME coverage/
  # dir; format_coverage merges the per-isolate files. Keep this list in
  # sync with ci.yml (test-core shard 0) and nightly.yml.
  dart test ${conc:+--concurrency=$conc} --tags integration \
    test/cli/jsr_cli_test.dart \
    test/cli/cli_args_jsr_test.dart \
    test/cli/agent_cli_jsr_test.dart \
    --coverage=coverage
}

stage_integration_mock() {
  # Issue #551: the no-key integration legs run on EVERY PR that touches
  # them — MockLlmServer scenarios, no secrets, no network, so they cannot
  # rot silently between releases (#538 class). Real-provider files carry
  # the `llm` tag and stay in the tag-only smoke job; browser-ext owns its
  # own workflow; perf has the #303 per-PR trajectory gate; `pty` marks
  # child-agent-spawn tests (issue #553) — nightly-only, unbounded boot time.
  #
  # TMPDIR normalization (macOS hook parity): several PTY legs assert the
  # status row still shows `· ctx ` — with macOS's per-user temp root
  # (/var/folders/<30 chars>/T/...) the temp cwd eats the whole row width
  # and the assertion fails locally while ubuntu CI (/tmp) is green. Pin
  # the stage to the same short temp root CI has so hook/CI agree.
  echo "🧪 Running no-key integration legs (MockLlmServer)..."
  local conc="${FA_DART_TEST_CONCURRENCY:-$(detect_test_concurrency)}"
  echo "   concurrency: ${conc:-default}"
  #
  # Flake budget (gh-1026): FA_GATE_PTY_RETRIES=N reruns ONLY the failed
  # files, up to N times, before the stage fails. The PTY/grid timing legs
  # are load-sensitive (the gh-1026 class: 3 red 2.5 h gate runs on an
  # unchanged head, a different ambient test red each time, every file
  # green in isolation) — the budget turns one flaky PTY case from a full
  # leg rerun into a minutes-scoped file rerun, mirroring CI's
  # retrigger-recovery behaviour (ci.yml watchdog: ONE retrigger, never a
  # blind rerun). 0 (the default) keeps the single-shot leg below
  # byte-identical. Files come from scripts/gate_failed_targets.py over
  # the dart json file-reporter log; when the log yields no targets
  # (crash before the reporter flushed) the stage fails WITHOUT a rerun —
  # never rerun blind.
  local retries="${FA_GATE_PTY_RETRIES:-0}"
  if [ "$retries" -le 0 ]; then
    TMPDIR="${FA_GATE_TMPDIR:-/tmp}" \
      dart test ${conc:+--concurrency=$conc} test/integration \
      --exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,perf,pty
    return
  fi
  local log="test-results/gate-integration-mock.json"
  mkdir -p test-results
  local targets="test/integration"
  local attempt=0
  while true; do
    attempt=$((attempt + 1))
    if TMPDIR="${FA_GATE_TMPDIR:-/tmp}" \
        dart test ${conc:+--concurrency=$conc} $targets \
        --exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,perf,pty \
        --file-reporter="json:$log"; then
      return 0
    fi
    if [ "$attempt" -gt "$retries" ]; then
      echo "❌ flake budget exhausted ($retries rerun(s)) — integration leg stays red" >&2
      exit 1
    fi
    local failed
    failed=$(python3 scripts/gate_failed_targets.py "$log")
    if [ -z "$failed" ]; then
      echo "   no failed-file targets in $log — not rerunning blind" >&2
      exit 1
    fi
    echo "🔁 flake budget: rerun $attempt/$retries — failed files only:" >&2
    printf '%s\n' "$failed" | sed 's/^/   /' >&2
    targets="$failed"
  done
}

stage_coverage() {
  if [ ! -d coverage ]; then
    echo "❌ coverage/ not found — run the test-core stage first" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  echo "📊 Formatting coverage to lcov..."
  dart run coverage:format_coverage --lcov -i coverage -o coverage/lcov.info
  echo "🔍 Checking line coverage (baseline: >= ${COVERAGE_BASELINE}%)..."
  if ! python3 scripts/check_coverage.py "$COVERAGE_BASELINE"; then
    echo "❌ QUALITY GATE FAILED — TEST COVERAGE (baseline ${COVERAGE_BASELINE}%)" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
}

Empirical CC counting rules in crap4dart:
- `if`: +1 each ✓ (3 ifs → CC 4)
- ternary: +1 ✓
- **switch statement: +1 per case** (4 cases → CC 5)
- **switch expression: +0 (!)** — CC 1
- **stacked cases: +1 per case LABEL** (4 labels over 2 bodies → CC 5)
- `||`: +1 each (3 || → CC 5)
- collection-if: +0
- for/catch: +1 each
- when guard: case +1, `when` +1 (CC 3 = base + case + when)

So the plan for `_record`:
- Split into `_record` (run-phase switch: AgentStart, TurnStart, MessageUpdate+when, TurnEnd, AgentEnd, default → CC = 1+5+1(when) = 7) + `_recordToolEvent` (4 cases + default → CC 5-6).
- Dispatch: `if (event is Tool...) { _recordToolEvent(event); return; }` would add if+||s. Alternative: use a switch EXPRESSION or avoid the or-pattern...

Option: `_record` keeps ALL cases but tool cases just call `_recordToolEvent(event)` — stacked labels each +1: tool case labels = 4 stacked → +4, run cases 5 + when 1 → CC = 1 + 4 + 5 + 1 = 11. Too high.

Better: two independent switches is impossible one event without a pre-dispatch... Use stacked cases but ONLY 2: hmm.

Cleanest low-CC: pre-dispatch with a single `is` check against a helper... Dart has no multi-is. What about:

```dart
void _record(AgentEvent event) {
  if (event is ToolExecutionStartEvent ||
      event is ToolExecutionEndEvent ||
      event is ToolCallHeartbeatEvent ||
      event is ToolCallStuckEvent) {
    _recordToolEvent(event);
    return;
  }
  _recordRunPhase(event);
}
```

`_recordToolEvent`: switch statement, 4 cases (exhaustive over the four types? no — compiler can't know; needs default or end) → CC = 1+4+1(default) = 6. At 100% cov = 6. 
`_recordRunPhase`: switch with AgentStart, TurnStart, MessageUpdate+when, TurnEnd, AgentEnd, default → CC = 1+5+1 = 7. Existing tests cover it 100% → CRAP 7.

Empirical CC counting rules in crap4dart:
- `if`: +1 each ✓ (3 ifs → CC 4)
- ternary: +1 ✓
- **switch statement: +1 per case** (4 cases → CC 5)
- **switch expression: +0 (!)** — CC 1
- **stacked cases: +1 per case LABEL** (4 labels over 2 bodies → CC 5)
- `||`: +1 each (3 || → CC 5)
- collection-if: +0
- for/catch: +1 each
- when guard: case +1, `when` +1 (CC 3 = base + case + when)

So the plan for `_record`:
- Split into `_record` (run-phase switch: AgentStart, TurnStart, MessageUpdate+when, TurnEnd, AgentEnd, default → CC = 1+5+1(when) = 7) + `_recordToolEvent` (4 cases + default → CC 5-6).
- Dispatch: `if (event is Tool...) { _recordToolEvent(event); return; }` would add if+||s. Alternative: use a switch EXPRESSION or avoid the or-pattern...

Option: `_record` keeps ALL cases but tool cases just call `_recordToolEvent(event)` — stacked labels each +1: tool case labels = 4 stacked → +4, run cases 5 + when 1 → CC = 1 + 4 + 5 + 1 = 11. Too high.

Better: two independent switches is impossible one event without a pre-dispatch... Use stacked cases but ONLY 2: hmm.

Cleanest low-CC: pre-dispatch with a single `is` check against a helper... Dart has no multi-is. What about:

```dart
void _record(AgentEvent event) {
  if (event is ToolExecutionStartEvent ||
      event is ToolExecutionEndEvent ||
      event is ToolCallHeartbeatEvent ||
      event is ToolCallStuckEvent) {
    _recordToolEvent(event);
    return;
  }
  _recordRunPhase(event);
}
```
CC = 1 + 1(if) + 3(||) = 5. 
`_recordToolEvent`: switch statement, 4 cases (exhaustive over the four types? no — compiler can't know; needs default or end) → CC = 1+4+1(default) = 6. At 100% cov = 6. 
`_recordRunPhase`: switch with AgentStart, TurnStart, MessageUpdate+when, TurnEnd, AgentEnd, default → CC = 1+5+1 = 7. Existing tests cover it 100% → CRAP 7.
