blocks.text:
Empirical CC counting rules in crap4dart:
- `if`: +1 each ✓ (3 ifs → CC 4)
- ternary: +1 ✓
- **switch statement: +1 per case** (4 cases → CC 5)
- **switch expression: +0 (!)** — CC 1
- **stacked cases: +1 per case LABEL** (4 labels over 2 bodies → CC 5)
- `||`: +1 each (3 || → CC 5)
- collection-if: +0
- for/catch: +1 each
- when guard: case +1, `when` +1 (CC 3 = base + case + when)

So the plan for `_record`:
- Split into `_record` (run-phase switch: AgentStart, TurnStart, MessageUpdate+when, TurnEnd, AgentEnd, default → CC = 1+5+1(when) = 7) + `_recordToolEvent` (4 cases + default → CC 5-6).
- Dispatch: `if (event is Tool...) { _recordToolEvent(event); return; }` would add if+||s. Alternative: use a switch EXPRESSION or avoid the or-pattern...

Empirical CC counting rules in crap4dart:
- `if`: +1 each ✓ (3 ifs → CC 4)
- ternary: +1 ✓
- **switch statement: +1 per case** (4 cases → CC 5)
- **switch expression: +0 (!)** — CC 1
- **stacked cases: +1 per case LABEL** (4 labels over 2 bodies → CC 5)
- `||`: +1 each (3 || → CC 5)
- collection-if: +0
- for/catch: +1 each
- when guard: case +1, `when` +1 (CC 3 = base + case + when)

So the plan for `_record`:
- Split into `_record` (run-phase switch: AgentStart, TurnStart, MessageUpdate+when, TurnEnd, AgentEnd, default → CC = 1+5+1(when) = 7) + `_recordToolEvent` (4 cases + default → CC 5-6).
- Dispatch: `if (event is Tool...) { _recordToolEvent(event); return; }` would add if+||s. Alternative: use a switch EXPRESSION or avoid the or-pattern...

Option: `_record` keeps ALL cases but tool cases just call `_recordToolEvent(event)` — stacked labels each +1: tool case labels = 4 stacked → +4, run cases 5 + when 1 → CC = 1 + 4 + 5 + 1 = 11. Too high.

Better: two independent switches is impossible one event without a pre-dispatch... Use stacked cases but ONLY 2: hmm.

Cleanest low-CC: pre-dispatch with a single `is` check against a helper... Dart has no multi-is. What about:

```dart
void _record(AgentEvent event) {
  if (event is ToolExecutionStartEvent ||
      event is ToolExecutionEndEvent ||
      event is ToolCallHeartbeatEvent ||
      event is ToolCallStuckEvent) {
    _recordToolEvent(event);

  _recordRunPhase(event);
}
```

blocks.text:
Empirical CC counting rules in crap4dart:
- `if`: +1 each ✓ (3 ifs → CC 4)
- ternary: +1 ✓
- **switch statement: +1 per case** (4 cases → CC 5)
- **switch expression: +0 (!)** — CC 1
- **stacked cases: +1 per case LABEL** (4 labels over 2 bodies → CC 5)
- `||`: +1 each (3 || → CC 5)
- collection-if: +0
- for/catch: +1 each
- when guard: case +1, `when` +1 (CC 3 = base + case + when)

So the plan for `_record`:
- Split into `_record` (run-phase switch: AgentStart, TurnStart, MessageUpdate+when, TurnEnd, AgentEnd, default → CC = 1+5+1(when) = 7) + `_recordToolEvent` (4 cases + default → CC 5-6).
- Dispatch: `if (event is Tool...) { _recordToolEvent(event); return; }` would add if+||s. Alternative: use a switch EXPRESSION or avoid the or-pattern...

Option: `_record` keeps ALL cases but tool cases just call `_recordToolEvent(event)` — stacked labels each +1: tool case labels = 4 stacked → +4, run cases 5 + when 1 → CC = 1 + 4 + 5 + 1 = 11. Too high.

Better: two independent switches is impossible one event without a pre-dispatch... Use stacked cases but ONLY 2: hmm.

Cleanest low-CC: pre-dispatch with a single `is` check against a helper... Dart has no multi-is. What about:

```dart
void _record(AgentEvent event) {
  if (event is ToolExecutionStartEvent ||
      event is ToolExecutionEndEvent ||
      event is ToolCallHeartbeatEvent ||
      event is ToolCallStuckEvent) {
    _recordToolEvent(event);
    return;
  }
  _recordRunPhase(event);
}
```
CC = 1 + 1(if) + 3(||) = 5. 
`_recordToolEvent`: switch statement, 4 cases (exhaustive over the four types? no — compiler can't know; needs default or end) → CC = 1+4+1(default) = 6. At 100% cov = 6. 
`_recordRunPhase`: switch with AgentStart, TurnStart, MessageUpdate+when, TurnEnd, AgentEnd, default → CC = 1+5+1 = 7. Existing tests cover it 100% → CRAP 7. 

Wait — can I do better? switch expression for _recordRunPhase: switch EXPRESSIONS count 0! But the cases have side effects and one has a when-guard... switch expressions support when-guards. Side effects in expression cases are fine (each branch an expression). E.g.:

```dart
void _recordRunPhase(AgentEvent event) => switch (event) {
  AgentStartEvent() => _onRunStart(),
  TurnStartEvent() => _emit(AgentTelemetryEventKind.turnStart),
  MessageUpdateEvent() when !_sawFirstToken => _onFirstStreamedUpdate(),
  TurnEndEvent(:final message) => _emit(..., stopReason: message.stopReason.name),
  AgentEndEvent() => _onAgentEnd(event),
  _ => null,  // hmm — expression must return a value; use void-ish
};
```
Each case returns void — switch expression arms returning void is allowed? The expression type would be void — `void switchExpr` — allowed in Dart? An expression switch whose arms all have type void: the switch expression's static type is void, and `void _recordRunPhase(AgentEvent event) => switch ...` works. Hmm, `when` guard +1 (when counts even in expressions? Probably same counting — probe didn't test switch-expression with when. Conservative: assume +1).

But honestly CC 7 @ 100% cov (CRAP 7) is comfortably under 12. And even if CI coverage dipped to 80%: 49×0.008+7 = 7.4. Totally safe. Keep switch STATEMENT (matches existing file style — `_record` was a statement switch; minimal diff).

Same for _recordToolEvent (CC 6) — must be 100% covered via new tests, else CC 6 @ 0% = 36+6 = 42. New tests required for all four kinds.

For `resolveKey` (CC 15 @ 100% = 15): refactor into helpers, each ≤ 6:
- `resolveKey` body: canonical + chained + name + return HostKeyResolution(...) → CC ~2
- `_effectiveSlotName(canonical, chained)`: firstWhere closure — does the closure's inner ||s count toward the METHOD's CC? `probeLogicalOr` counted them as top-level statements; closures — likely counted within the enclosing function by crap4dart's visitor (typical). firstWhere closure: `(slot) => slot != canonical && ... && _hasStoreValue(...)` — 2 &&s. Plus ternary + || → CC ≈ 1+2(&&)+1(ternary)+1(|| from chained==null || ==canonical)... let me just write it and measure.

Also, `fromEnv` computation: `name != null && name == chained && envNames.contains(name) && _isGenuineEnv(...)` = 3 &&s + ternary — extract `_isEnvResolution(...)` static helper: CC 1+3 = 4-5.

`_driftHint`: ifs (3 conditions via || or separate ifs) + ternary → CC ~6.
`_missingKeyHint`: if + ternary → CC ~3-4.

Also double-check `firstWhere` with orElse — covered by tests (pinned twin scenarios exist in provider_key_resolver_test.dart — I saw "all drift scenarios" pass; coverage was 100% for resolveKey, so every branch IS covered — the helpers will inherit 100% coverage from the same tests).

blocks.text:
Empirical CC counting rules in crap4dart:
- `if`: +1 each ✓ (3 ifs → CC 4)
- ternary: +1 ✓
- **switch statement: +1 per case** (4 cases → CC 5)
- **switch expression: +0 (!)** — CC 1
- **stacked cases: +1 per case LABEL** (4 labels over 2 bodies → CC 5)
- `||`: +1 each (3 || → CC 5)
- collection-if: +0
- for/catch: +1 each
- when guard: case +1, `when` +1 (CC 3 = base + case + when)

So the plan for `_record`:
- Split into `_record` (run-phase switch: AgentStart, TurnStart, MessageUpdate+when, TurnEnd, AgentEnd, default → CC = 1+5+1(when) = 7) + `_recordToolEvent` (4 cases + default → CC 5-6).
- Dispatch: `if (event is Tool...) { _recordToolEvent(event); return; }` would add if+||s. Alternative: use a switch EXPRESSION or avoid the or-pattern...

Option: `_record` keeps ALL cases but tool cases just call `_recordToolEvent(event)` — stacked labels each +1: tool case labels = 4 stacked → +4, run cases 5 + when 1 → CC = 1 + 4 + 5 + 1 = 11. Too high.

Better: two independent switches is impossible one event without a pre-dispatch... Use stacked cases but ONLY 2: hmm.

Cleanest low-CC: pre-dispatch with a single `is` check against a helper... Dart has no multi-is. What about:

```dart
void _record(AgentEvent event) {
  if (event is ToolExecutionStartEvent ||
      event is ToolExecutionEndEvent ||
      event is ToolCallHeartbeatEvent ||
      event is ToolCallStuckEvent) {
    _recordToolEvent(event);
    return;
  }
  _recordRunPhase(event);
}

Empirical CC counting rules in crap4dart:
- `if`: +1 each ✓ (3 ifs → CC 4)
- ternary: +1 ✓
- **switch statement: +1 per case** (4 cases → CC 5)
- **switch expression: +0 (!)** — CC 1
- **stacked cases: +1 per case LABEL** (4 labels over 2 bodies → CC 5)
- `||`: +1 each (3 || → CC 5)
- collection-if: +0
- for/catch: +1 each
- when guard: case +1, `when` +1 (CC 3 = base + case + when)

So the plan for `_record`:
- Split into `_record` (run-phase switch: AgentStart, TurnStart, MessageUpdate+when, TurnEnd, AgentEnd, default → CC = 1+5+1(when) = 7) + `_recordToolEvent` (4 cases + default → CC 5-6).
- Dispatch: `if (event is Tool...) { _recordToolEvent(event); return; }` would add if+||s. Alternative: use a switch EXPRESSION or avoid the or-pattern...

Option: `_record` keeps ALL cases but tool cases just call `_recordToolEvent(event)` — stacked labels each +1: tool case labels = 4 stacked → +4, run cases 5 + when 1 → CC = 1 + 4 + 5 + 1 = 11. Too high.

Better: two independent switches is impossible one event without a pre-dispatch... Use stacked cases but ONLY 2: hmm.

Cleanest low-CC: pre-dispatch with a single `is` check against a helper... Dart has no multi-is. What about:

```dart
void _record(AgentEvent event) {
  if (event is ToolExecutionStartEvent ||
      event is ToolExecutionEndEvent ||
      event is ToolCallHeartbeatEvent ||
      event is ToolCallStuckEvent) {
    _recordToolEvent(event);
    return;
  }
  _recordRunPhase(event);
}
```
CC = 1 + 1(if) + 3(||) = 5. 
`_recordToolEvent`: switch statement, 4 cases (exhaustive over the four types? no — compiler can't know; needs default or end) → CC = 1+4+1(default) = 6. At 100% cov = 6. 
`_recordRunPhase`: switch with AgentStart, TurnStart, MessageUpdate+when, TurnEnd, AgentEnd, default → CC = 1+5+1 = 7. Existing tests cover it 100% → CRAP 7. 

Wait — can I do better? switch expression for _recordRunPhase: switch EXPRESSIONS count 0! But the cases have side effects and one has a when-guard... switch expressions support when-guards. Side effects in expression cases are fine (each branch an expression). E.g.:

void _recordRunPhase(AgentEvent event) => switch (event) {

};
```

An expression switch whose arms all have type void: the switch expression's static type is void, and `void _recordRunPhase(AgentEvent event) => switch ...` works. Wait — but let me confirm the formula: CRAP = comp² × (1 − cov)³ + comp. For CC 15, cov 100%: 15. Yes → 15 > 12 → fails. For CC 12, cov 57.1%: 144 × 0.429³ + 12 = 144 × 0.0789 + 12 = 11.36 + 12 = 23.36 ≈ 23.34 ✓.

blocks.text:
Empirical CC counting rules in crap4dart:
- `if`: +1 each ✓ (3 ifs → CC 4)
- ternary: +1 ✓
- **switch statement: +1 per case** (4 cases → CC 5)
- **switch expression: +0 (!)** — CC 1
- **stacked cases: +1 per case LABEL** (4 labels over 2 bodies → CC 5)
- `||`: +1 each (3 || → CC 5)
- collection-if: +0
- for/catch: +1 each
- when guard: case +1, `when` +1 (CC 3 = base + case + when)

So the plan for `_record`:
- Split into `_record` (run-phase switch: AgentStart, TurnStart, MessageUpdate+when, TurnEnd, AgentEnd, default → CC = 1+5+1(when) = 7) + `_recordToolEvent` (4 cases + default → CC 5-6).
- Dispatch: `if (event is Tool...) { _recordToolEvent(event); return; }` would add if+||s. Alternative: use a switch EXPRESSION or avoid the or-pattern...

Option: `_record` keeps ALL cases but tool cases just call `_recordToolEvent(event)` — stacked labels each +1: tool case labels = 4 stacked → +4, run cases 5 + when 1 → CC = 1 + 4 + 5 + 1 = 11. Too high.

Better: two independent switches is impossible one event without a pre-dispatch... Use stacked cases but ONLY 2: hmm.

Cleanest low-CC: pre-dispatch with a single `is` check against a helper... Dart has no multi-is. What about:

```dart
void _record(AgentEvent event) {
  if (event is ToolExecutionStartEvent ||
      event is ToolExecutionEndEvent ||
      event is ToolCallHeartbeatEvent ||
      event is ToolCallStuckEvent) {
    _recordToolEvent(event);
    return;
  }
  _recordRunPhase(event);
}
```
CC = 1 + 1(if) + 3(||) = 5. 
`_recordToolEvent`: switch statement, 4 cases (exhaustive over the four types? no — compiler can't know; needs default or end) → CC = 1+4+1(default) = 6. At 100% cov = 6. 
`_recordRunPhase`: switch with AgentStart, TurnStart, MessageUpdate+when, TurnEnd, AgentEnd, default → CC = 1+5+1 = 7. Existing tests cover it 100% → CRAP 7. 

Wait — can I do better? switch expression for _recordRunPhase: switch EXPRESSIONS count 0! But the cases have side effects and one has a when-guard... switch expressions support when-guards. Side effects in expression cases are fine (each branch an expression). E.g.:

```dart
void _recordRunPhase(AgentEvent event) => switch (event) {
  AgentStartEvent() => _onRunStart(),
  TurnStartEvent() => _emit(AgentTelemetryEventKind.turnStart),
  MessageUpdateEvent() when !_sawFirstToken => _onFirstStreamedUpdate(),
  TurnEndEvent(:final message) => _emit(..., stopReason: message.stopReason.name),
  AgentEndEvent() => _onAgentEnd(event),
  _ => null,  // hmm — expression must return a value; use void-ish
};
```
Each case returns void — switch expression arms returning void is allowed? The expression type would be void — `void switchExpr` — allowed in Dart? An expression switch whose arms all have type void: the switch expression's static type is void, and `void _recordRunPhase(AgentEvent event) => switch ...` works. Hmm, `when` guard +1 (when counts even in expressions? Probably same counting — probe didn't test switch-expression with when. Conservative: assume +1).

But honestly CC 7 @ 100% cov (CRAP 7) is comfortably under 12. And even if CI coverage dipped to 80%: 49×0.008+7 = 7.4. Totally safe. Keep switch STATEMENT (matches existing file style — `_record` was a statement switch; minimal diff).

Same for _recordToolEvent (CC 6) — must be 100% covered via new tests, else CC 6 @ 0% = 36+6 = 42. New tests required for all four kinds.

For `resolveKey` (CC 15 @ 100% = 15): refactor into helpers, each ≤ 6:
- `resolveKey` body: canonical + chained + name + return HostKeyResolution(...) → CC ~2
- `_effectiveSlotName(canonical, chained)`: firstWhere closure — does the closure's inner ||s count toward the METHOD's CC? `probeLogicalOr` counted them as top-level statements; closures — likely counted within the enclosing function by crap4dart's visitor (typical). firstWhere closure: `(slot) => slot != canonical && ... && _hasStoreValue(...)` — 2 &&s. Also, `fromEnv` computation: `name != null && name == chained && envNames.contains(name) && _isGenuineEnv(...)` = 3 &&s + ternary — extract `_isEnvResolution(...)` static helper: CC 1+3 = 4-5.

`_missingKeyHint`: if + ternary → CC ~3-4.

blocks.text:
Empirical CC counting rules in crap4dart:
- `if`: +1 each ✓ (3 ifs → CC 4)
- ternary: +1 ✓
- **switch statement: +1 per case** (4 cases → CC 5)
- **switch expression: +0 (!)** — CC 1
- **stacked cases: +1 per case LABEL** (4 labels over 2 bodies → CC 5)
- `||`: +1 each (3 || → CC 5)
- collection-if: +0
- for/catch: +1 each
- when guard: case +1, `when` +1 (CC 3 = base + case + when)

So the plan for `_record`:
- Split into `_record` (run-phase switch: AgentStart, TurnStart, MessageUpdate+when, TurnEnd, AgentEnd, default → CC = 1+5+1(when) = 7) + `_recordToolEvent` (4 cases + default → CC 5-6).
- Dispatch: `if (event is Tool...) { _recordToolEvent(event); return; }` would add if+||s. Alternative: use a switch EXPRESSION or avoid the or-pattern...

Option: `_record` keeps ALL cases but tool cases just call `_recordToolEvent(event)` — stacked labels each +1: tool case labels = 4 stacked → +4, run cases 5 + when 1 → CC = 1 + 4 + 5 + 1 = 11. Too high.

Better: two independent switches is impossible one event without a pre-dispatch... Use stacked cases but ONLY 2: hmm.

Cleanest low-CC: pre-dispatch with a single `is` check against a helper... Dart has no multi-is. What about:

```dart
void _record(AgentEvent event) {
  if (event is ToolExecutionStartEvent ||
      event is ToolExecutionEndEvent ||
      event is ToolCallHeartbeatEvent ||
      event is ToolCallStuckEvent) {
    _recordToolEvent(event);
    return;
  }
  _recordRunPhase(event);
}
```
CC = 1 + 1(if) + 3(||) = 5. 
`_recordToolEvent`: switch statement, 4 cases (exhaustive over the four types? no — compiler can't know; needs default or end) → CC = 1+4+1(default) = 6. At 100% cov = 6. 
`_recordRunPhase`: switch with AgentStart, TurnStart, MessageUpdate+when, TurnEnd, AgentEnd, default → CC = 1+5+1 = 7. Existing tests cover it 100% → CRAP 7. 

Wait — can I do better? switch expression for _recordRunPhase: switch EXPRESSIONS count 0! But the cases have side effects and one has a when-guard... switch expressions support when-guards. Side effects in expression cases are fine (each branch an expression). E.g.:

```dart
void _recordRunPhase(AgentEvent event) => switch (event) {
  AgentStartEvent() => _onRunStart(),
  TurnStartEvent() => _emit(AgentTelemetryEventKind.turnStart),
  MessageUpdateEvent() when !_sawFirstToken => _onFirstStreamedUpdate(),
  TurnEndEvent(:final message) => _emit(..., stopReason: message.stopReason.name),
  AgentEndEvent() => _onAgentEnd(event),
  _ => null,  // hmm — expression must return a value; use void-ish
};
```
Each case returns void — switch expression arms returning void is allowed? The expression type would be void — `void switchExpr` — allowed in Dart? An expression switch whose arms all have type void: the switch expression's static type is void, and `void _recordRunPhase(AgentEvent event) => switch ...` works. Hmm, `when` guard +1 (when counts even in expressions? Probably same counting — probe didn't test switch-expression with when. Conservative: assume +1).

But honestly CC 7 @ 100% cov (CRAP 7) is comfortably under 12. And even if CI coverage dipped to 80%: 49×0.008+7 = 7.4. Totally safe. Keep switch STATEMENT (matches existing file style — `_record` was a statement switch; minimal diff).

Same for _recordToolEvent (CC 6) — must be 100% covered via new tests, else CC 6 @ 0% = 36+6 = 42. New tests required for all four kinds.

For `resolveKey` (CC 15 @ 100% = 15): refactor into helpers, each ≤ 6:
- `resolveKey` body: canonical + chained + name + return HostKeyResolution(...) → CC ~2
- `_effectiveSlotName(canonical, chained)`: firstWhere closure — does the closure's inner ||s count toward the METHOD's CC? `probeLogicalOr` counted them as top-level statements; closures — likely counted within the enclosing function by crap4dart's visitor (typical). firstWhere closure: `(slot) => slot != canonical && ... && _hasStoreValue(...)` — 2 &&s. Also, `fromEnv` computation: `name != null && name == chained && envNames.contains(name) && _isGenuineEnv(...)` = 3 &&s + ternary — extract `_isEnvResolution(...)` static helper: CC 1+3 = 4-5.

`_missingKeyHint`: if + ternary → CC ~3-4.

blocks.text:
Empirical CC counting rules in crap4dart:
- `if`: +1 each ✓ (3 ifs → CC 4)
- ternary: +1 ✓
- **switch statement: +1 per case** (4 cases → CC 5)
- **switch expression: +0 (!)** — CC 1
- **stacked cases: +1 per case LABEL** (4 labels over 2 bodies → CC 5)
- `||`: +1 each (3 || → CC 5)
- collection-if: +0
- for/catch: +1 each
- when guard: case +1, `when` +1 (CC 3 = base + case + when)

So the plan for `_record`:
- Split into `_record` (run-phase switch: AgentStart, TurnStart, MessageUpdate+when, TurnEnd, AgentEnd, default → CC = 1+5+1(when) = 7) + `_recordToolEvent` (4 cases + default → CC 5-6).
- Dispatch: `if (event is Tool...) { _recordToolEvent(event); return; }` would add if+||s. Alternative: use a switch EXPRESSION or avoid the or-pattern...

Option: `_record` keeps ALL cases but tool cases just call `_recordToolEvent(event)` — stacked labels each +1: tool case labels = 4 stacked → +4, run cases 5 + when 1 → CC = 1 + 4 + 5 + 1 = 11. Too high.

Better: two independent switches is impossible one event without a pre-dispatch... Use stacked cases but ONLY 2: hmm.

Cleanest low-CC: pre-dispatch with a single `is` check against a helper... Dart has no multi-is. What about:

```dart
void _record(AgentEvent event) {
  if (event is ToolExecutionStartEvent ||
      event is ToolExecutionEndEvent ||
      event is ToolCallHeartbeatEvent ||
      event is ToolCallStuckEvent) {
    _recordToolEvent(event);
    return;
  }
  _recordRunPhase(event);
}
```
CC = 1 + 1(if) + 3(||) = 5. 
`_recordToolEvent`: switch statement, 4 cases (exhaustive over the four types? no — compiler can't know; needs default or end) → CC = 1+4+1(default) = 6. At 100% cov = 6. 
`_recordRunPhase`: switch with AgentStart, TurnStart, MessageUpdate+when, TurnEnd, AgentEnd, default → CC = 1+5+1 = 7. Existing tests cover it 100% → CRAP 7. 

Wait — can I do better? switch expression for _recordRunPhase: switch EXPRESSIONS count 0! But the cases have side effects and one has a when-guard... switch expressions support when-guards. Side effects in expression cases are fine (each branch an expression). E.g.:

```dart
void _recordRunPhase(AgentEvent event) => switch (event) {
  AgentStartEvent() => _onRunStart(),
  TurnStartEvent() => _emit(AgentTelemetryEventKind.turnStart),
  MessageUpdateEvent() when !_sawFirstToken => _onFirstStreamedUpdate(),
  TurnEndEvent(:final message) => _emit(..., stopReason: message.stopReason.name),
  AgentEndEvent() => _onAgentEnd(event),
  _ => null,  // hmm — expression must return a value; use void-ish
};
```
Each case returns void — switch expression arms returning void is allowed? The expression type would be void — `void switchExpr` — allowed in Dart? An expression switch whose arms all have type void: the switch expression's static type is void, and `void _recordRunPhase(AgentEvent event) => switch ...` works. Hmm, `when` guard +1 (when counts even in expressions? Probably same counting — probe didn't test switch-expression with when. Conservative: assume +1).

But honestly CC 7 @ 100% cov (CRAP 7) is comfortably under 12. And even if CI coverage dipped to 80%: 49×0.008+7 = 7.4. Totally safe. Keep switch STATEMENT (matches existing file style — `_record` was a statement switch; minimal diff).

Same for _recordToolEvent (CC 6) — must be 100% covered via new tests, else CC 6 @ 0% = 36+6 = 42. New tests required for all four kinds.

For `resolveKey` (CC 15 @ 100% = 15): refactor into helpers, each ≤ 6:
- `resolveKey` body: canonical + chained + name + return HostKeyResolution(...) → CC ~2
- `_effectiveSlotName(canonical, chained)`: firstWhere closure — does the closure's inner ||s count toward the METHOD's CC? `probeLogicalOr` counted them as top-level statements; closures — likely counted within the enclosing function by crap4dart's visitor (typical). firstWhere closure: `(slot) => slot != canonical && ... && _hasStoreValue(...)` — 2 &&s. Plus ternary + || → CC ≈ 1+2(&&)+1(ternary)+1(|| from chained==null || ==canonical)... let me just write it and measure.

Also, `fromEnv` computation: `name != null && name == chained && envNames.contains(name) && _isGenuineEnv(...)` = 3 &&s + ternary — extract `_isEnvResolution(...)` static helper: CC 1+3 = 4-5.

`_driftHint`: ifs (3 conditions via || or separate ifs) + ternary → CC ~6.
`_missingKeyHint`: if + ternary → CC ~3-4.

Let me now delete the probe and write the refactors. Also double-check `firstWhere` with orElse — covered by tests (pinned twin scenarios exist in provider_key_resolver_test.dart — I saw "all drift scenarios" pass; coverage was 100% for resolveKey, so every branch IS covered — the helpers will inherit 100% coverage from the same tests).

Also check: does anything else in the changed files read above threshold in the full suite? From the targeted output: max 11 (resolveEndpointKeyName) — safe.

One more consideration: `host_agent_wiring.dart` — `buildAgentStack` CC 4 @100%, `_wireFabric` 8.09 @ 88.9% (pre-existing? `_wireFabric` is not in the PR diff — line 692 — the PR added imports/fields/buildAgentStack seams only; _wireFabric is from main. Fine.)

**Root cause found.** The `guards` job's CRAP ratchet (threshold 12.0) fails on the PR's new code:

- `HostKeyResolver.resolveKey` — CC 15, **CRAP 15.0 at 100% coverage** → mathematically over the rat…

blocks.text:
Found it. Two offenders above the 12.0 CRAP threshold:

1. **`AgentTelemetry._record`** — CRAP 23.34, coverage 57.1%, CC 12. The targeted tests leave parts of the switch uncovered (MessageUpdateEvent firstToken fallback at line 181, ToolCallStuckEvent, maybe ToolCallHeartbeatEvent...). With the FULL suite coverage in CI it might better, but 57.1% with CC 12 → CRAP 23.3 > 12. Even with slightly better coverage in CI, still likely over. CC 12 itself means CRAP ≥ 12 even at 100% coverage! CC 12 at 100% = 12.0 — hmm, at exactly 12.0, is it > threshold? "Only down from here", threshold 12.0 — the existing worst offenders at CRAP 12 pass, so the check is CRAP > 12.0 fails. CC 12 fully covered = CRAP 12.0 → borderline pass. But at 57.1% → 23.34 → FAIL.

2. **`HostKeyResolver.resolveKey`** — CRAP 15.0 at CC 15, 100% coverage → 15 > 12 → **FAIL even with perfect coverage**. This is a hard fail in CI: the coverage is complete (100%), so CI's merged coverage also reads CC 15 → CRAP 15 > 12 → the CRAP ratchet fails. That's the root cause of the guards failure!

Note: the switch-expressions in `_message`/`_tail` apparently don't count per-case (CC 2 for `_message` — so crap4dart doesn't count switch expression cases, or counts them as 1 total). Good.

So the CRAP ratchet failure is real: `HostKeyResolver.resolveKey` CC 15 → CRAP 15 (> 12) even fully covered. And `AgentTelemetry._record` CC 12 with partial coverage → 23.34.

Wait — but let me confirm the formula: CRAP = comp² × (1 − cov)³ + comp. For CC 15, cov 100%: 15. Yes → 15 > 12 → fails. For CC 12, cov 57.1%: 144 × 0.429³ + 12 = 144 × 0.0789 + 12 = 11.36 + 12 = 23.36 ≈ 23.34 ✓.

In CI with the full suite, `AgentTelemetry._record` coverage might be higher (the full suite might exercise more of the switch — e.g. stuck-tool heartbeats might be covered by other tests? Unlikely — heartbeat/stuck events only come from stuckTool supervision tests, which are in the PR's own tests... but the PR's targeted tests I ran DO include the telemetry tests). Hmm — actually wait, maybe more of `_record` gets covered in CI: `AgentEndEvent` error path is covered... Let me see which parts are uncovered at 57.1%: the switch has cases: AgentStart ✓, TurnStart ✓, MessageUpdate firstToken (covered? the file-sink test uses hand-built events; the adapter test... the review thread says the `MessageUpdateEvent` fallback is a real path — presumably covered by adapter tests), ToolExecutionStart/End ✓ (integration wiring), ToolCallHeartbeat (maybe not — heartbeat events require stuckTool supervision in a long-running tool test), ToolCallStuck (probably not), TurnEnd ✓, AgentEnd ✓, default.

Whatever the exact CI coverage is, `HostKeyResolver.resolveKey` at CRAP 15 with 100% cov is a definite ratchet failure — that alone fails the guards job. And `_record` at CC 12/57.1% is another likely failure (CI coverage won't hit 100%: heartbeat/stuck paths need specific wiring; even if they are covered, CRAP = 12.0 exactly = borderline pass — too risky).

So the fix (TDD):

**Finding 1: `HostKeyResolver.resolveKey` CC 15 → CRAP 15 > 12.**
Fix: refactor to reduce CC below the ratchet — extract helper(s). The method does: canonical, chained resolution, pinned-twin registry leg, fromEnv computation, driftHint, missingKeyHint. Extract e.g. `_resolvePinnedTwin` / `_driftHint` / `_missingKeyHint` helpers. Each helper needs 100% coverage to keep CRAP = CC ≤ 12. Tests exist covering all these branches (the PR's resolver tests — 240 lines). Let me verify coverage of each extracted piece stays 100%.

**Finding 2: `AgentTelemetry._record` CC 12, cov 57.1% (targeted) → CRAP 23.34.**
Fix options: (a) increase coverage to 100% — requires tests for heartbeat/stuck/fallback paths; (b) reduce CC by splitting the switch; (c) both. Empirical CC counting rules in crap4dart:
- `if`: +1 each ✓ (3 ifs → CC 4)
- ternary: +1 ✓
- **switch statement: +1 per case** (4 cases → CC 5)
- **switch expression: +0 (!)** — CC 1
- **stacked cases: +1 per case LABEL** (4 labels over 2 bodies → CC 5)
- `||`: +1 each (3 || → CC 5)
- collection-if: +0
- for/catch: +1 each
- when guard: case +1, `when` +1 (CC 3 = base + case + when)

So the plan for `_record`:
- Split into `_record` (run-phase switch: AgentStart, TurnStart, MessageUpdate+when, TurnEnd, AgentEnd, default → CC = 1+5+1(when) = 7) + `_recordToolEvent` (4 cases + default → CC 5-6).

Option: `_record` keeps ALL cases but tool cases just call `_recordToolEvent(event)` — stacked labels each +1: tool case labels = 4 stacked → +4, run cases 5 + when 1 → CC = 1 + 4 + 5 + 1 = 11. Too high.

Better: two independent switches is impossible one event without a pre-dispatch... Use stacked cases but ONLY 2: hmm.

Cleanest low-CC: pre-dispatch with a single `is` check against a helper... Dart has no multi-is. What about:

void _record(AgentEvent event) {

}

- `if`: +1 each ✓ (3 ifs → CC 4)
- ternary: +1 ✓
- **switch statement: +1 per case** (4 cases → CC 5)
- **switch expression: +0 (!)** — CC 1
- **stacked cases: +1 per case LABEL** (4 labels over 2 bodies → CC 5)
- `||`: +1 each (3 || → CC 5)
- collection-if: +0
- for/catch: +1 each
- when guard: case +1, `when` +1 (CC 3 = base + case + when)

So the plan for `_record`:

blocks.text:
Empirical CC counting rules in crap4dart:
- `if`: +1 each ✓ (3 ifs → CC 4)
- ternary: +1 ✓
- **switch statement: +1 per case** (4 cases → CC 5)
- **switch expression: +0 (!)** — CC 1
- **stacked cases: +1 per case LABEL** (4 labels over 2 bodies → CC 5)
- `||`: +1 each (3 || → CC 5)
- collection-if: +0
- for/catch: +1 each
- when guard: case +1, `when` +1 (CC 3 = base + case + when)

So the plan for `_record`:
- Split into `_record` (run-phase switch: AgentStart, TurnStart, MessageUpdate+when, TurnEnd, AgentEnd, default → CC = 1+5+1(when) = 7) + `_recordToolEvent` (4 cases + default → CC 5-6).
- Dispatch: `if (event is Tool...) { _recordToolEvent(event); return; }` would add if+||s. Alternative: use a switch EXPRESSION or avoid the or-pattern...

Option: `_record` keeps ALL cases but tool cases just call `_recordToolEvent(event)` — stacked labels each +1: tool case labels = 4 stacked → +4, run cases 5 + when 1 → CC = 1 + 4 + 5 + 1 = 11. Too high.

Better: two independent switches is impossible one event without a pre-dispatch... Use stacked cases but ONLY 2: hmm.

Cleanest low-CC: pre-dispatch with a single `is` check against a helper... Dart has no multi-is. What about:

```dart
void _record(AgentEvent event) {
  if (event is ToolExecutionStartEvent ||
      event is ToolExecutionEndEvent ||
      event is ToolCallHeartbeatEvent ||
      event is ToolCallStuckEvent) {
    _recordToolEvent(event);
    return;
  }
  _recordRunPhase(event);
}
```
CC = 1 + 1(if) + 3(||) = 5. 
`_recordToolEvent`: switch statement, 4 cases (exhaustive over the four types? no — compiler can't know; needs default or end) → CC = 1+4+1(default) = 6. At 100% cov = 6. 
`_recordRunPhase`: switch with AgentStart, TurnStart, MessageUpdate+when, TurnEnd, AgentEnd, default → CC = 1+5+1 = 7. Existing tests cover it 100% → CRAP 7. 

Wait — can I do better? switch expression for _recordRunPhase: switch EXPRESSIONS count 0! But the cases have side effects and one has a when-guard... switch expressions support when-guards. Side effects in expression cases are fine (each branch an expression). E.g.:

```dart
void _recordRunPhase(AgentEvent event) => switch (event) {
  AgentStartEvent() => _onRunStart(),
  TurnStartEvent() => _emit(AgentTelemetryEventKind.turnStart),
  MessageUpdateEvent() when !_sawFirstToken => _onFirstStreamedUpdate(),
  TurnEndEvent(:final message) => _emit(..., stopReason: message.stopReason.name),
  AgentEndEvent() => _onAgentEnd(event),
  _ => null,  // hmm — expression must return a value; use void-ish
};
```
Each case returns void — switch expression arms returning void is allowed? The expression type would be void — `void switchExpr` — allowed in Dart? An expression switch whose arms all have type void: the switch expression's static type is void, and `void _recordRunPhase(AgentEvent event) => switch ...` works. Hmm, `when` guard +1 (when counts even in expressions? Probably same counting — probe didn't test switch-expression with when. Conservative: assume +1).

But honestly CC 7 @ 100% cov (CRAP 7) is comfortably under 12. And even if CI coverage dipped to 80%: 49×0.008+7 = 7.4. Totally safe. Keep switch STATEMENT (matches existing file style — `_record` was a statement switch; minimal diff).

Same for _recordToolEvent (CC 6) — must be 100% covered via new tests, else CC 6 @ 0% = 36+6 = 42. New tests required for all four kinds.

- `resolveKey` body: canonical + chained + name + return HostKeyResolution(...) → CC ~2
- `_effectiveSlotName(canonical, chained)`: firstWhere closure — does the closure's inner ||s count toward the METHOD's CC? `probeLogicalOr` counted them as top-level statements; closures — likely counted within the enclosing function by crap4dart's visitor (typical). firstWhere closure: `(slot) => slot != canonical && ... && _hasStoreValue(...)` — 2 &&s. `_missingKeyHint`: if + ternary → CC ~3-4.

**Root cause found.** The `guards` job's CRAP ratchet (threshold 12.0) fails on the PR's new code:

- `HostKeyResolver.resolveKey` — CC 15, **CRAP 15.0 at 100% coverage** → mathematically over the rat…

blocks.text:
Found it. Two offenders above the 12.0 CRAP threshold:

1. **`AgentTelemetry._record`** — CRAP 23.34, coverage 57.1%, CC 12. The targeted tests leave parts of the switch uncovered (MessageUpdateEvent firstToken fallback at line 181, ToolCallStuckEvent, maybe ToolCallHeartbeatEvent...). With the FULL suite coverage in CI it might better, but 57.1% with CC 12 → CRAP 23.3 > 12. Even with slightly better coverage in CI, still likely over. CC 12 itself means CRAP ≥ 12 even at 100% coverage! CC 12 at 100% = 12.0 — hmm, at exactly 12.0, is it > threshold? "Only down from here", threshold 12.0 — the existing worst offenders at CRAP 12 pass, so the check is CRAP > 12.0 fails. CC 12 fully covered = CRAP 12.0 → borderline pass. But at 57.1% → 23.34 → FAIL.

2. **`HostKeyResolver.resolveKey`** — CRAP 15.0 at CC 15, 100% coverage → 15 > 12 → **FAIL even with perfect coverage**. This is a hard fail in CI: the coverage is complete (100%), so CI's merged coverage also reads CC 15 → CRAP 15 > 12 → the CRAP ratchet fails. That's the root cause of the guards failure!

Note: the switch-expressions in `_message`/`_tail` apparently don't count per-case (CC 2 for `_message` — so crap4dart doesn't count switch expression cases, or counts them as 1 total). Good.

So the CRAP ratchet failure is real: `HostKeyResolver.resolveKey` CC 15 → CRAP 15 (> 12) even fully covered. And `AgentTelemetry._record` CC 12 with partial coverage → 23.34.

Wait — but let me confirm the formula: CRAP = comp² × (1 − cov)³ + comp. For CC 15, cov 100%: 15. Yes → 15 > 12 → fails. For CC 12, cov 57.1%: 144 × 0.429³ + 12 = 144 × 0.0789 + 12 = 11.36 + 12 = 23.36 ≈ 23.34 ✓.

In CI with the full suite, `AgentTelemetry._record` coverage might be higher (the full suite might exercise more of the switch — e.g. stuck-tool heartbeats might be covered by other tests? Unlikely — heartbeat/stuck events only come from stuckTool supervision tests, which are in the PR's own tests... but the PR's targeted tests I ran DO include the telemetry tests). Hmm — actually wait, maybe more of `_record` gets covered in CI: `AgentEndEvent` error path is covered... Let me see which parts are uncovered at 57.1%: the switch has cases: AgentStart ✓, TurnStart ✓, MessageUpdate firstToken (covered? the file-sink test uses hand-built events; the adapter test... the review thread says the `MessageUpdateEvent` fallback is a real path — presumably covered by adapter tests), ToolExecutionStart/End ✓ (integration wiring), ToolCallHeartbeat (maybe not — heartbeat events require stuckTool supervision in a long-running tool test), ToolCallStuck (probably not), TurnEnd ✓, AgentEnd ✓, default.

Whatever the exact CI coverage is, `HostKeyResolver.resolveKey` at CRAP 15 with 100% cov is a definite ratchet failure — that alone fails the guards job. And `_record` at CC 12/57.1% is another likely failure (CI coverage won't hit 100%: heartbeat/stuck paths need specific wiring; even if they are covered, CRAP = 12.0 exactly = borderline pass — too risky).

Empirical CC counting rules in crap4dart:
- `if`: +1 each ✓ (3 ifs → CC 4)
- ternary: +1 ✓
- **switch statement: +1 per case** (4 cases → CC 5)
- **switch expression: +0 (!)** — CC 1
- **stacked cases: +1 per case LABEL** (4 labels over 2 bodies → CC 5)
- `||`: +1 each (3 || → CC 5)
- collection-if: +0
- for/catch: +1 each
- when guard: case +1, `when` +1 (CC 3 = base + case + when)

So the plan for `_record`:
- Split into `_record` (run-phase switch: AgentStart, TurnStart, MessageUpdate+when, TurnEnd, AgentEnd, default → CC = 1+5+1(when) = 7) + `_recordToolEvent` (4 cases + default → CC 5-6).
- Dispatch: `if (event is Tool...) { _recordToolEvent(event); return; }` would add if+||s. Alternative: use a switch EXPRESSION or avoid the or-pattern...

Option: `_record` keeps ALL cases but tool cases just call `_recordToolEvent(event)` — stacked labels each +1: tool case labels = 4 stacked → +4, run cases 5 + when 1 → CC = 1 + 4 + 5 + 1 = 11. Too high.

Better: two independent switches is impossible one event without a pre-dispatch... Use stacked cases but ONLY 2: hmm.

Cleanest low-CC: pre-dispatch with a single `is` check against a helper... Dart has no multi-is. What about:

```dart
void _record(AgentEvent event) {
  if (event is ToolExecutionStartEvent ||
      event is ToolExecutionEndEvent ||
      event is ToolCallHeartbeatEvent ||
      event is ToolCallStuckEvent) {
    _recordToolEvent(event);
    return;
  }
  _recordRunPhase(event);
}
```
CC = 1 + 1(if) + 3(||) = 5. 
`_recordToolEvent`: switch statement, 4 cases (exhaustive over the four types? no — compiler can't know; needs default or end) → CC = 1+4+1(default) = 6. At 100% cov = 6. 
`_recordRunPhase`: switch with AgentStart, TurnStart, MessageUpdate+when, TurnEnd, AgentEnd, default → CC = 1+5+1 = 7. Existing tests cover it 100% → CRAP 7. 

Wait — can I do better? switch expression for _recordRunPhase: switch EXPRESSIONS count 0! But the cases have side effects and one has a when-guard... switch expressions support when-guards. Side effects in expression cases are fine (each branch an expression). E.g.:

```dart
void _recordRunPhase(AgentEvent event) => switch (event) {
  AgentStartEvent() => _onRunStart(),
  TurnStartEvent() => _emit(AgentTelemetryEventKind.turnStart),
  MessageUpdateEvent() when !_sawFirstToken => _onFirstStreamedUpdate(),
  TurnEndEvent(:final message) => _emit(..., stopReason: message.stopReason.name),
  AgentEndEvent() => _onAgentEnd(event),
  _ => null,  // hmm — expression must return a value; use void-ish
};
```
Each case returns void — switch expression arms returning void is allowed? The expression type would be void — `void switchExpr` — allowed in Dart? An expression switch whose arms all have type void: the switch expression's static type is void, and `void _recordRunPhase(AgentEvent event) => switch ...` works. Hmm, `when` guard +1 (when counts even in expressions? Probably same counting — probe didn't test switch-expression with when. Conservative: assume +1).

But honestly CC 7 @ 100% cov (CRAP 7) is comfortably under 12. And even if CI coverage dipped to 80%: 49×0.008+7 = 7.4. Totally safe. Keep switch STATEMENT (matches existing file style — `_record` was a statement switch; minimal diff).

- **switch expression: +0 (!)** — CC 1
- **stacked cases: +1 per case LABEL** (4 labels over 2 bodies → CC 5)
- `||`: +1 each (3 || → CC 5)
- collection-if: +0
- for/catch: +1 each
- when guard: case +1, `when` +1 (CC 3 = base + case + when)

blocks.text:
Empirical CC counting rules in crap4dart:
- `if`: +1 each ✓ (3 ifs → CC 4)
- ternary: +1 ✓
- **switch statement: +1 per case** (4 cases → CC 5)
- **switch expression: +0 (!)** — CC 1
- **stacked cases: +1 per case LABEL** (4 labels over 2 bodies → CC 5)
- `||`: +1 each (3 || → CC 5)
- collection-if: +0
- for/catch: +1 each
- when guard: case +1, `when` +1 (CC 3 = base + case + when)

So the plan for `_record`:
- Split into `_record` (run-phase switch: AgentStart, TurnStart, MessageUpdate+when, TurnEnd, AgentEnd, default → CC = 1+5+1(when) = 7) + `_recordToolEvent` (4 cases + default → CC 5-6).
- Dispatch: `if (event is Tool...) { _recordToolEvent(event); return; }` would add if+||s. Alternative: use a switch EXPRESSION or avoid the or-pattern...

Option: `_record` keeps ALL cases but tool cases just call `_recordToolEvent(event)` — stacked labels each +1: tool case labels = 4 stacked → +4, run cases 5 + when 1 → CC = 1 + 4 + 5 + 1 = 11. Too high.

Better: two independent switches is impossible one event without a pre-dispatch... Use stacked cases but ONLY 2: hmm.

Cleanest low-CC: pre-dispatch with a single `is` check against a helper... Dart has no multi-is. What about:

```dart
void _record(AgentEvent event) {
  if (event is ToolExecutionStartEvent ||
      event is ToolExecutionEndEvent ||
      event is ToolCallHeartbeatEvent ||
      event is ToolCallStuckEvent) {
    _recordToolEvent(event);
    return;
  }
  _recordRunPhase(event);
}
```
CC = 1 + 1(if) + 3(||) = 5. 
`_recordToolEvent`: switch statement, 4 cases (exhaustive over the four types? no — compiler can't know; needs default or end) → CC = 1+4+1(default) = 6. At 100% cov = 6. 
`_recordRunPhase`: switch with AgentStart, TurnStart, MessageUpdate+when, TurnEnd, AgentEnd, default → CC = 1+5+1 = 7. Existing tests cover it 100% → CRAP 7. 

Wait — can I do better? switch expression for _recordRunPhase: switch EXPRESSIONS count 0! But the cases have side effects and one has a when-guard... switch expressions support when-guards. Side effects in expression cases are fine (each branch an expression). E.g.:

```dart
void _recordRunPhase(AgentEvent event) => switch (event) {
  AgentStartEvent() => _onRunStart(),
  TurnStartEvent() => _emit(AgentTelemetryEventKind.turnStart),
  MessageUpdateEvent() when !_sawFirstToken => _onFirstStreamedUpdate(),
  TurnEndEvent(:final message) => _emit(..., stopReason: message.stopReason.name),
  AgentEndEvent() => _onAgentEnd(event),
  _ => null,  // hmm — expression must return a value; use void-ish
};
```
Each case returns void — switch expression arms returning void is allowed? The expression type would be void — `void switchExpr` — allowed in Dart? An expression switch whose arms all have type void: the switch expression's static type is void, and `void _recordRunPhase(AgentEvent event) => switch ...` works. Hmm, `when` guard +1 (when counts even in expressions? Probably same counting — probe didn't test switch-expression with when. Conservative: assume +1).

But honestly CC 7 @ 100% cov (CRAP 7) is comfortably under 12. And even if CI coverage dipped to 80%: 49×0.008+7 = 7.4. Totally safe. Keep switch STATEMENT (matches existing file style — `_record` was a statement switch; minimal diff).

Same for _recordToolEvent (CC 6) — must be 100% covered via new tests, else CC 6 @ 0% = 36+6 = 42. New tests required for all four kinds.

For `resolveKey` (CC 15 @ 100% = 15): refactor into helpers, each ≤ 6:
- `resolveKey` body: canonical + chained + name + return HostKeyResolution(...) → CC ~2
- `_effectiveSlotName(canonical, chained)`: firstWhere closure — does the closure's inner ||s count toward the METHOD's CC? `probeLogicalOr` counted them as top-level statements; closures — likely counted within the enclosing function by crap4dart's visitor (typical). firstWhere closure: `(slot) => slot != canonical && ... && _hasStoreValue(...)` — 2 &&s. Empirical CC counting rules in crap4dart:
- `if`: +1 each ✓ (3 ifs → CC 4)
- ternary: +1 ✓
- **switch statement: +1 per case** (4 cases → CC 5)
- **switch expression: +0 (!)** — CC 1
- **stacked cases: +1 per case LABEL** (4 labels over 2 bodies → CC 5)
- `||`: +1 each (3 || → CC 5)
- collection-if: +0
- for/catch: +1 each
- when guard: case +1, `when` +1 (CC 3 = base + case + when)

So the plan for `_record`:
- Split into `_record` (run-phase switch: AgentStart, TurnStart, MessageUpdate+when, TurnEnd, AgentEnd, default → CC = 1+5+1(when) = 7) + `_recordToolEvent` (4 cases + default → CC 5-6).
- Dispatch: `if (event is Tool...) { _recordToolEvent(event); return; }` would add if+||s. Alternative: use a switch EXPRESSION or avoid the or-pattern...

Option: `_record` keeps ALL cases but tool cases just call `_recordToolEvent(event)` — stacked labels each +1: tool case labels = 4 stacked → +4, run cases 5 + when 1 → CC = 1 + 4 + 5 + 1 = 11. Too high.

Better: two independent switches is impossible one event without a pre-dispatch... Use stacked cases but ONLY 2: hmm.

Cleanest low-CC: pre-dispatch with a single `is` check against a helper... Dart has no multi-is. What about:

```dart
void _record(AgentEvent event) {
  if (event is ToolExecutionStartEvent ||
      event is ToolExecutionEndEvent ||
      event is ToolCallHeartbeatEvent ||
      event is ToolCallStuckEvent) {
    _recordToolEvent(event);
    return;
  }
  _recordRunPhase(event);
}
```
CC = 1 + 1(if) + 3(||) = 5. 
`_recordToolEvent`: switch statement, 4 cases (exhaustive over the four types? no — compiler can't know; needs default or end) → CC = 1+4+1(default) = 6. At 100% cov = 6. 
`_recordRunPhase`: switch with AgentStart, TurnStart, MessageUpdate+when, TurnEnd, AgentEnd, default → CC = 1+5+1 = 7. Existing tests cover it 100% → CRAP 7. 

Wait — can I do better? switch expression for _recordRunPhase: switch EXPRESSIONS count 0! But the cases have side effects and one has a when-guard... switch expressions support when-guards. Side effects in expression cases are fine (each branch an expression). E.g.:

```dart
void _recordRunPhase(AgentEvent event) => switch (event) {
  AgentStartEvent() => _onRunStart(),
  TurnStartEvent() => _emit(AgentTelemetryEventKind.turnStart),
  MessageUpdateEvent() when !_sawFirstToken => _onFirstStreamedUpdate(),
  TurnEndEvent(:final message) => _emit(..., stopReason: message.stopReason.name),
  AgentEndEvent() => _onAgentEnd(event),
  _ => null,  // hmm — expression must return a value; use void-ish
};
```
Each case returns void — switch expression arms returning void is allowed? The expression type would be void — `void switchExpr` — allowed in Dart? An expression switch whose arms all have type void: the switch expression's static type is void, and `void _recordRunPhase(AgentEvent event) => switch ...` works. Hmm, `when` guard +1 (when counts even in expressions? Probably same counting — probe didn't test switch-expression with when. Conservative: assume +1).

But honestly CC 7 @ 100% cov (CRAP 7) is comfortably under 12. And even if CI coverage dipped to 80%: 49×0.008+7 = 7.4. Totally safe. Keep switch STATEMENT (matches existing file style — `_record` was a statement switch; minimal diff).

blocks.text:
Empirical CC counting rules in crap4dart:
- `if`: +1 each ✓ (3 ifs → CC 4)
- ternary: +1 ✓
- **switch statement: +1 per case** (4 cases → CC 5)
- **switch expression: +0 (!)** — CC 1
- **stacked cases: +1 per case LABEL** (4 labels over 2 bodies → CC 5)
- `||`: +1 each (3 || → CC 5)
- collection-if: +0
- for/catch: +1 each
- when guard: case +1, `when` +1 (CC 3 = base + case + when)

So the plan for `_record`:
- Split into `_record` (run-phase switch: AgentStart, TurnStart, MessageUpdate+when, TurnEnd, AgentEnd, default → CC = 1+5+1(when) = 7) + `_recordToolEvent` (4 cases + default → CC 5-6).
- Dispatch: `if (event is Tool...) { _recordToolEvent(event); return; }` would add if+||s. Alternative: use a switch EXPRESSION or avoid the or-pattern...

Option: `_record` keeps ALL cases but tool cases just call `_recordToolEvent(event)` — stacked labels each +1: tool case labels = 4 stacked → +4, run cases 5 + when 1 → CC = 1 + 4 + 5 + 1 = 11. Too high.

Better: two independent switches is impossible one event without a pre-dispatch... Use stacked cases but ONLY 2: hmm.

Cleanest low-CC: pre-dispatch with a single `is` check against a helper... Dart has no multi-is. What about:

```dart
void _record(AgentEvent event) {
  if (event is ToolExecutionStartEvent ||
      event is ToolExecutionEndEvent ||
      event is ToolCallHeartbeatEvent ||
      event is ToolCallStuckEvent) {
    _recordToolEvent(event);
    return;
  }
  _recordRunPhase(event);
}
```
CC = 1 + 1(if) + 3(||) = 5. 
`_recordToolEvent`: switch statement, 4 cases (exhaustive over the four types? no — compiler can't know; needs default or end) → CC = 1+4+1(default) = 6. At 100% cov = 6. 
`_recordRunPhase`: switch with AgentStart, TurnStart, MessageUpdate+when, TurnEnd, AgentEnd, default → CC = 1+5+1 = 7. Existing tests cover it 100% → CRAP 7. 

Wait — can I do better? switch expression for _recordRunPhase: switch EXPRESSIONS count 0! But the cases have side effects and one has a when-guard... switch expressions support when-guards. Side effects in expression cases are fine (each branch an expression). E.g.:

```dart
void _recordRunPhase(AgentEvent event) => switch (event) {
  AgentStartEvent() => _onRunStart(),
  TurnStartEvent() => _emit(AgentTelemetryEventKind.turnStart),
  MessageUpdateEvent() when !_sawFirstToken => _onFirstStreamedUpdate(),
  TurnEndEvent(:final message) => _emit(..., stopReason: message.stopReason.name),
  AgentEndEvent() => _onAgentEnd(event),
  _ => null,  // hmm — expression must return a value; use void-ish
};
```
Each case returns void — switch expression arms returning void is allowed? The expression type would be void — `void switchExpr` — allowed in Dart? An expression switch whose arms all have type void: the switch expression's static type is void, and `void _recordRunPhase(AgentEvent event) => switch ...` works. Hmm, `when` guard +1 (when counts even in expressions? Probably same counting — probe didn't test switch-expression with when. Conservative: assume +1).

But honestly CC 7 @ 100% cov (CRAP 7) is comfortably under 12. And even if CI coverage dipped to 80%: 49×0.008+7 = 7.4. Totally safe. Keep switch STATEMENT (matches existing file style — `_record` was a statement switch; minimal diff).

Empirical CC counting rules in crap4dart:
- `if`: +1 each ✓ (3 ifs → CC 4)
- ternary: +1 ✓
- **switch statement: +1 per case** (4 cases → CC 5)
- **switch expression: +0 (!)** — CC 1
- **stacked cases: +1 per case LABEL** (4 labels over 2 bodies → CC 5)
- `||`: +1 each (3 || → CC 5)
- collection-if: +0
- for/catch: +1 each
- when guard: case +1, `when` +1 (CC 3 = base + case + when)

So the plan for `_record`:
- Split into `_record` (run-phase switch: AgentStart, TurnStart, MessageUpdate+when, TurnEnd, AgentEnd, default → CC = 1+5+1(when) = 7) + `_recordToolEvent` (4 cases + default → CC 5-6).
- Dispatch: `if (event is Tool...) { _recordToolEvent(event); return; }` would add if+||s. Alternative: use a switch EXPRESSION or avoid the or-pattern...

Option: `_record` keeps ALL cases but tool cases just call `_recordToolEvent(event)` — stacked labels each +1: tool case labels = 4 stacked → +4, run cases 5 + when 1 → CC = 1 + 4 + 5 + 1 = 11. Too high.

Better: two independent switches is impossible one event without a pre-dispatch... Use stacked cases but ONLY 2: hmm.

Cleanest low-CC: pre-dispatch with a single `is` check against a helper... Dart has no multi-is. What about:

```dart
void _record(AgentEvent event) {
  if (event is ToolExecutionStartEvent ||
      event is ToolExecutionEndEvent ||
      event is ToolCallHeartbeatEvent ||
      event is ToolCallStuckEvent) {
    _recordToolEvent(event);
    return;
  }
  _recordRunPhase(event);
}
```
CC = 1 + 1(if) + 3(||) = 5. 
`_recordToolEvent`: switch statement, 4 cases (exhaustive over the four types? no — compiler can't know; needs default or end) → CC = 1+4+1(default) = 6. At 100% cov = 6. 
`_recordRunPhase`: switch with AgentStart, TurnStart, MessageUpdate+when, TurnEnd, AgentEnd, default → CC = 1+5+1 = 7. Existing tests cover it 100% → CRAP 7.

};
```

blocks.text:
Empirical CC counting rules in crap4dart:
- `if`: +1 each ✓ (3 ifs → CC 4)
- ternary: +1 ✓
- **switch statement: +1 per case** (4 cases → CC 5)
- **switch expression: +0 (!)** — CC 1
- **stacked cases: +1 per case LABEL** (4 labels over 2 bodies → CC 5)
- `||`: +1 each (3 || → CC 5)
- collection-if: +0
- for/catch: +1 each
- when guard: case +1, `when` +1 (CC 3 = base + case + when)

So the plan for `_record`:
- Split into `_record` (run-phase switch: AgentStart, TurnStart, MessageUpdate+when, TurnEnd, AgentEnd, default → CC = 1+5+1(when) = 7) + `_recordToolEvent` (4 cases + default → CC 5-6).
- Dispatch: `if (event is Tool...) { _recordToolEvent(event); return; }` would add if+||s. Alternative: use a switch EXPRESSION or avoid the or-pattern...

Option: `_record` keeps ALL cases but tool cases just call `_recordToolEvent(event)` — stacked labels each +1: tool case labels = 4 stacked → +4, run cases 5 + when 1 → CC = 1 + 4 + 5 + 1 = 11. Too high.

Better: two independent switches is impossible one event without a pre-dispatch... Use stacked cases but ONLY 2: hmm.

Cleanest low-CC: pre-dispatch with a single `is` check against a helper... Dart has no multi-is. What about:

```dart
void _record(AgentEvent event) {
  if (event is ToolExecutionStartEvent ||
      event is ToolExecutionEndEvent ||
      event is ToolCallHeartbeatEvent ||
      event is ToolCallStuckEvent) {
    _recordToolEvent(event);
    return;
  }
  _recordRunPhase(event);
}
```
CC = 1 + 1(if) + 3(||) = 5. 
`_recordToolEvent`: switch statement, 4 cases (exhaustive over the four types? no — compiler can't know; needs default or end) → CC = 1+4+1(default) = 6. At 100% cov = 6. 
`_recordRunPhase`: switch with AgentStart, TurnStart, MessageUpdate+when, TurnEnd, AgentEnd, default → CC = 1+5+1 = 7. Existing tests cover it 100% → CRAP 7. 

Wait — can I do better? switch expression for _recordRunPhase: switch EXPRESSIONS count 0! But the cases have side effects and one has a when-guard... switch expressions support when-guards. Side effects in expression cases are fine (each branch an expression). E.g.:

```dart
void _recordRunPhase(AgentEvent event) => switch (event) {
  AgentStartEvent() => _onRunStart(),
  TurnStartEvent() => _emit(AgentTelemetryEventKind.turnStart),
  MessageUpdateEvent() when !_sawFirstToken => _onFirstStreamedUpdate(),
  TurnEndEvent(:final message) => _emit(..., stopReason: message.stopReason.name),
  AgentEndEvent() => _onAgentEnd(event),
  _ => null,  // hmm — expression must return a value; use void-ish
};
```
Each case returns void — switch expression arms returning void is allowed? The expression type would be void — `void switchExpr` — allowed in Dart? An expression switch whose arms all have type void: the switch expression's static type is void, and `void _recordRunPhase(AgentEvent event) => switch ...` works. Hmm, `when` guard +1 (when counts even in expressions? Probably same counting — probe didn't test switch-expression with when. Conservative: assume +1).

But honestly CC 7 @ 100% cov (CRAP 7) is comfortably under 12. And even if CI coverage dipped to 80%: 49×0.008+7 = 7.4. Totally safe. Keep switch STATEMENT (matches existing file style — `_record` was a statement switch; minimal diff).

Same for _recordToolEvent (CC 6) — must be 100% covered via new tests, else CC 6 @ 0% = 36+6 = 42. New tests required for all four kinds.

For `resolveKey` (CC 15 @ 100% = 15): refactor into helpers, each ≤ 6:
- `resolveKey` body: canonical + chained + name + return HostKeyResolution(...) → CC ~2
- `_effectiveSlotName(canonical, chained)`: firstWhere closure — does the closure's inner ||s count toward the METHOD's CC? `probeLogicalOr` counted them as top-level statements; closures — likely counted within the enclosing function by crap4dart's visitor (typical). firstWhere closure: `(slot) => slot != canonical && ... && _hasStoreValue(...)` — 2 &&s. Plus ternary + || → CC ≈ 1+2(&&)+1(ternary)+1(|| from chained==null || ==canonical)... let me just write it and measure.

Also, `fromEnv` computation: `name != null && name == chained && envNames.contains(name) && _isGenuineEnv(...)` = 3 &&s + ternary — extract `_isEnvResolution(...)` static helper: CC 1+3 = 4-5.

`_driftHint`: ifs (3 conditions via || or separate ifs) + ternary → CC ~6.
`_missingKeyHint`: if + ternary → CC ~3-4.

Also double-check `firstWhere` with orElse — covered by tests (pinned twin scenarios exist in provider_key_resolver_test.dart — I saw "all drift scenarios" pass; coverage was 100% for resolveKey, so every branch IS covered — the helpers will inherit 100% coverage from the same tests).

  llm:
    # Real-provider smoke tests (issue #551): hit live provider APIs and need
    # secrets. They carry `integration` too and run ONLY in the tag-only
    # provider-smoke job (v* tags) and nightly — every per-PR suite excludes
    # them: dart test --exclude-tags llm
    #
    # gh-1199: the boundary is now enforced at the gate's integration shard
    # SELECTION too (shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm, asserted by

    # scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py — a live-looking integration file
    # without this tag fails the static gate. See docs/live-llm-testing.md.

    # Rate limiting (issue #931 part 3.3): package:test forbids `concurrency`
    # in tag overrides (test_core _disallow('concurrency') for tag scopes, v1.32),

Empirical CC counting rules in crap4dart:
- `if`: +1 each ✓ (3 ifs → CC 4)
- ternary: +1 ✓
- **switch statement: +1 per case** (4 cases → CC 5)
- **switch expression: +0 (!)** — CC 1
- **stacked cases: +1 per case LABEL** (4 labels over 2 bodies → CC 5)
- `||`: +1 each (3 || → CC 5)
- collection-if: +0
- for/catch: +1 each
- when guard: case +1, `when` +1 (CC 3 = base + case + when)

So the plan for `_record`:
- Split into `_record` (run-phase switch: AgentStart, TurnStart, MessageUpdate+when, TurnEnd, AgentEnd, default → CC = 1+5+1(when) = 7) + `_recordToolEvent` (4 cases + default → CC 5-6).
- Dispatch: `if (event is Tool...) { _recordToolEvent(event); return; }` would add if+||s. Alternative: use a switch EXPRESSION or avoid the or-pattern...

Option: `_record` keeps ALL cases but tool cases just call `_recordToolEvent(event)` — stacked labels each +1: tool case labels = 4 stacked → +4, run cases 5 + when 1 → CC = 1 + 4 + 5 + 1 = 11. Too high.

Better: two independent switches is impossible one event without a pre-dispatch... Use stacked cases but ONLY 2: hmm.

Cleanest low-CC: pre-dispatch with a single `is` check against a helper... Dart has no multi-is. What about:

```dart
void _record(AgentEvent event) {
  if (event is ToolExecutionStartEvent ||
      event is ToolExecutionEndEvent ||
      event is ToolCallHeartbeatEvent ||
      event is ToolCallStuckEvent) {
    _recordToolEvent(event);
    return;
  }
  _recordRunPhase(event);
}
```
CC = 1 + 1(if) + 3(||) = 5. 
`_recordToolEvent`: switch statement, 4 cases (exhaustive over the four types? no — compiler can't know; needs default or end) → CC = 1+4+1(default) = 6. At 100% cov = 6. 
`_recordRunPhase`: switch with AgentStart, TurnStart, MessageUpdate+when, TurnEnd, AgentEnd, default → CC = 1+5+1 = 7. Existing tests cover it 100% → CRAP 7.

void _recordRunPhase(AgentEvent event) => switch (event) {
  AgentStartEvent() => _onRunStart(),

  _ => null,  // hmm — expression must return a value; use void-ish
};
```

An expression switch whose arms all have type void: the switch expression's static type is void, and `void _recordRunPhase(AgentEvent event) => switch ...` works. blocks.text:
Empirical CC counting rules in crap4dart:
- `if`: +1 each ✓ (3 ifs → CC 4)
- ternary: +1 ✓
- **switch statement: +1 per case** (4 cases → CC 5)
- **switch expression: +0 (!)** — CC 1
- **stacked cases: +1 per case LABEL** (4 labels over 2 bodies → CC 5)
- `||`: +1 each (3 || → CC 5)
- collection-if: +0
- for/catch: +1 each
- when guard: case +1, `when` +1 (CC 3 = base + case + when)

So the plan for `_record`:
- Split into `_record` (run-phase switch: AgentStart, TurnStart, MessageUpdate+when, TurnEnd, AgentEnd, default → CC = 1+5+1(when) = 7) + `_recordToolEvent` (4 cases + default → CC 5-6).
- Dispatch: `if (event is Tool...) { _recordToolEvent(event); return; }` would add if+||s. Alternative: use a switch EXPRESSION or avoid the or-pattern...

Option: `_record` keeps ALL cases but tool cases just call `_recordToolEvent(event)` — stacked labels each +1: tool case labels = 4 stacked → +4, run cases 5 + when 1 → CC = 1 + 4 + 5 + 1 = 11. Too high.

Better: two independent switches is impossible one event without a pre-dispatch... Use stacked cases but ONLY 2: hmm.

Cleanest low-CC: pre-dispatch with a single `is` check against a helper... Dart has no multi-is. What about:

```dart
void _record(AgentEvent event) {
  if (event is ToolExecutionStartEvent ||
      event is ToolExecutionEndEvent ||
      event is ToolCallHeartbeatEvent ||
      event is ToolCallStuckEvent) {
    _recordToolEvent(event);
    return;
  }
  _recordRunPhase(event);
}
```
CC = 1 + 1(if) + 3(||) = 5. 
`_recordToolEvent`: switch statement, 4 cases (exhaustive over the four types? no — compiler can't know; needs default or end) → CC = 1+4+1(default) = 6. At 100% cov = 6. 
`_recordRunPhase`: switch with AgentStart, TurnStart, MessageUpdate+when, TurnEnd, AgentEnd, default → CC = 1+5+1 = 7. Existing tests cover it 100% → CRAP 7. 

Wait — can I do better? switch expression for _recordRunPhase: switch EXPRESSIONS count 0! But the cases have side effects and one has a when-guard... switch expressions support when-guards. Side effects in expression cases are fine (each branch an expression). E.g.:

```dart
void _recordRunPhase(AgentEvent event) => switch (event) {
  AgentStartEvent() => _onRunStart(),
  TurnStartEvent() => _emit(AgentTelemetryEventKind.turnStart),
  MessageUpdateEvent() when !_sawFirstToken => _onFirstStreamedUpdate(),
  TurnEndEvent(:final message) => _emit(..., stopReason: message.stopReason.name),
  AgentEndEvent() => _onAgentEnd(event),
  _ => null,  // hmm — expression must return a value; use void-ish
};
```
Each case returns void — switch expression arms returning void is allowed? The expression type would be void — `void switchExpr` — allowed in Dart? An expression switch whose arms all have type void: the switch expression's static type is void, and `void _recordRunPhase(AgentEvent event) => switch ...` works. Hmm, `when` guard +1 (when counts even in expressions? Probably same counting — probe didn't test switch-expression with when. Conservative: assume +1).

But honestly CC 7 @ 100% cov (CRAP 7) is comfortably under 12. And even if CI coverage dipped to 80%: 49×0.008+7 = 7.4. Totally safe. Keep switch STATEMENT (matches existing file style — `_record` was a statement switch; minimal diff).

Same for _recordToolEvent (CC 6) — must be 100% covered via new tests, else CC 6 @ 0% = 36+6 = 42. New tests required for all four kinds.

For `resolveKey` (CC 15 @ 100% = 15): refactor into helpers, each ≤ 6:
- `resolveKey` body: canonical + chained + name + return HostKeyResolution(...) → CC ~2
- `_effectiveSlotName(canonical, chained)`: firstWhere closure — does the closure's inner ||s count toward the METHOD's CC? `probeLogicalOr` counted them as top-level statements; closures — likely counted within the enclosing function by crap4dart's visitor (typical). firstWhere closure: `(slot) => slot != canonical && ... && _hasStoreValue(...)` — 2 &&s. Plus ternary + || → CC ≈ 1+2(&&)+1(ternary)+1(|| from chained==null || ==canonical)... let me just write it and measure.

Also, `fromEnv` computation: `name != null && name == chained && envNames.contains(name) && _isGenuineEnv(...)` = 3 &&s + ternary — extract `_isEnvResolution(...)` static helper: CC 1+3 = 4-5.

`_driftHint`: ifs (3 conditions via || or separate ifs) + ternary → CC ~6.
`_missingKeyHint`: if + ternary → CC ~3-4.

Also double-check `firstWhere` with orElse — covered by tests (pinned twin scenarios exist in provider_key_resolver_test.dart — I saw "all drift scenarios" pass; coverage was 100% for resolveKey, so every branch IS covered — the helpers will inherit 100% coverage from the same tests).

blocks.text:
Empirical CC counting rules in crap4dart:
- `if`: +1 each ✓ (3 ifs → CC 4)
- ternary: +1 ✓
- **switch statement: +1 per case** (4 cases → CC 5)
- **switch expression: +0 (!)** — CC 1
- **stacked cases: +1 per case LABEL** (4 labels over 2 bodies → CC 5)
- `||`: +1 each (3 || → CC 5)
- collection-if: +0
- for/catch: +1 each
- when guard: case +1, `when` +1 (CC 3 = base + case + when)

So the plan for `_record`:
- Split into `_record` (run-phase switch: AgentStart, TurnStart, MessageUpdate+when, TurnEnd, AgentEnd, default → CC = 1+5+1(when) = 7) + `_recordToolEvent` (4 cases + default → CC 5-6).
- Dispatch: `if (event is Tool...) { _recordToolEvent(event); return; }` would add if+||s. Alternative: use a switch EXPRESSION or avoid the or-pattern...

Option: `_record` keeps ALL cases but tool cases just call `_recordToolEvent(event)` — stacked labels each +1: tool case labels = 4 stacked → +4, run cases 5 + when 1 → CC = 1 + 4 + 5 + 1 = 11. Too high.

Better: two independent switches is impossible one event without a pre-dispatch... Use stacked cases but ONLY 2: hmm.

Cleanest low-CC: pre-dispatch with a single `is` check against a helper... Dart has no multi-is. What about:

```dart
void _record(AgentEvent event) {
  if (event is ToolExecutionStartEvent ||
      event is ToolExecutionEndEvent ||
      event is ToolCallHeartbeatEvent ||
      event is ToolCallStuckEvent) {
    _recordToolEvent(event);
    return;
  }
  _recordRunPhase(event);
}
```
CC = 1 + 1(if) + 3(||) = 5. 
`_recordToolEvent`: switch statement, 4 cases (exhaustive over the four types? no — compiler can't know; needs default or end) → CC = 1+4+1(default) = 6. At 100% cov = 6. 
`_recordRunPhase`: switch with AgentStart, TurnStart, MessageUpdate+when, TurnEnd, AgentEnd, default → CC = 1+5+1 = 7. Existing tests cover it 100% → CRAP 7. 

Wait — can I do better? switch expression for _recordRunPhase: switch EXPRESSIONS count 0! But the cases have side effects and one has a when-guard... switch expressions support when-guards. Side effects in expression cases are fine (each branch an expression). E.g.:

```dart
void _recordRunPhase(AgentEvent event) => switch (event) {
  AgentStartEvent() => _onRunStart(),
  TurnStartEvent() => _emit(AgentTelemetryEventKind.turnStart),
  MessageUpdateEvent() when !_sawFirstToken => _onFirstStreamedUpdate(),
  TurnEndEvent(:final message) => _emit(..., stopReason: message.stopReason.name),
  AgentEndEvent() => _onAgentEnd(event),
  _ => null,  // hmm — expression must return a value; use void-ish
};
```
Each case returns void — switch expression arms returning void is allowed? The expression type would be void — `void switchExpr` — allowed in Dart? An expression switch whose arms all have type void: the switch expression's static type is void, and `void _recordRunPhase(AgentEvent event) => switch ...` works. Hmm, `when` guard +1 (when counts even in expressions? Probably same counting — probe didn't test switch-expression with when. Conservative: assume +1).

But honestly CC 7 @ 100% cov (CRAP 7) is comfortably under 12. And even if CI coverage dipped to 80%: 49×0.008+7 = 7.4. Totally safe. Keep switch STATEMENT (matches existing file style — `_record` was a statement switch; minimal diff).

Same for _recordToolEvent (CC 6) — must be 100% covered via new tests, else CC 6 @ 0% = 36+6 = 42. New tests required for all four kinds.

For `resolveKey` (CC 15 @ 100% = 15): refactor into helpers, each ≤ 6:
- `resolveKey` body: canonical + chained + name + return HostKeyResolution(...) → CC ~2
- `_effectiveSlotName(canonical, chained)`: firstWhere closure — does the closure's inner ||s count toward the METHOD's CC? `probeLogicalOr` counted them as top-level statements; closures — likely counted within the enclosing function by crap4dart's visitor (typical). firstWhere closure: `(slot) => slot != canonical && ... && _hasStoreValue(...)` — 2 &&s. Plus ternary + || → CC ≈ 1+2(&&)+1(ternary)+1(|| from chained==null || ==canonical)... let me just write it and measure.

Also, `fromEnv` computation: `name != null && name == chained && envNames.contains(name) && _isGenuineEnv(...)` = 3 &&s + ternary — extract `_isEnvResolution(...)` static helper: CC 1+3 = 4-5.

`_driftHint`: ifs (3 conditions via || or separate ifs) + ternary → CC ~6.
`_missingKeyHint`: if + ternary → CC ~3-4.

Also double-check `firstWhere` with orElse — covered by tests (pinned twin scenarios exist in provider_key_resolver_test.dart — I saw "all drift scenarios" pass; coverage was 100% for resolveKey, so every branch IS covered — the helpers will inherit 100% coverage from the same tests).

blocks.text:
Empirical CC counting rules in crap4dart:
- `if`: +1 each ✓ (3 ifs → CC 4)
- ternary: +1 ✓
- **switch statement: +1 per case** (4 cases → CC 5)
- **switch expression: +0 (!)** — CC 1
- **stacked cases: +1 per case LABEL** (4 labels over 2 bodies → CC 5)
- `||`: +1 each (3 || → CC 5)
- collection-if: +0
- for/catch: +1 each
- when guard: case +1, `when` +1 (CC 3 = base + case + when)

So the plan for `_record`:
- Split into `_record` (run-phase switch: AgentStart, TurnStart, MessageUpdate+when, TurnEnd, AgentEnd, default → CC = 1+5+1(when) = 7) + `_recordToolEvent` (4 cases + default → CC 5-6).
- Dispatch: `if (event is Tool...) { _recordToolEvent(event); return; }` would add if+||s. Alternative: use a switch EXPRESSION or avoid the or-pattern...

Option: `_record` keeps ALL cases but tool cases just call `_recordToolEvent(event)` — stacked labels each +1: tool case labels = 4 stacked → +4, run cases 5 + when 1 → CC = 1 + 4 + 5 + 1 = 11. Too high.

Better: two independent switches is impossible one event without a pre-dispatch... Use stacked cases but ONLY 2: hmm.

Cleanest low-CC: pre-dispatch with a single `is` check against a helper... Dart has no multi-is. What about:

```dart
void _record(AgentEvent event) {
  if (event is ToolExecutionStartEvent ||
      event is ToolExecutionEndEvent ||
      event is ToolCallHeartbeatEvent ||
      event is ToolCallStuckEvent) {
    _recordToolEvent(event);
    return;
  }
  _recordRunPhase(event);
}
```
CC = 1 + 1(if) + 3(||) = 5. 
`_recordToolEvent`: switch statement, 4 cases (exhaustive over the four types? no — compiler can't know; needs default or end) → CC = 1+4+1(default) = 6. At 100% cov = 6. 
`_recordRunPhase`: switch with AgentStart, TurnStart, MessageUpdate+when, TurnEnd, AgentEnd, default → CC = 1+5+1 = 7. Existing tests cover it 100% → CRAP 7. 

Wait — can I do better? switch expression for _recordRunPhase: switch EXPRESSIONS count 0! But the cases have side effects and one has a when-guard... switch expressions support when-guards. Side effects in expression cases are fine (each branch an expression). E.g.:

```dart
void _recordRunPhase(AgentEvent event) => switch (event) {
  AgentStartEvent() => _onRunStart(),
  TurnStartEvent() => _emit(AgentTelemetryEventKind.turnStart),
  MessageUpdateEvent() when !_sawFirstToken => _onFirstStreamedUpdate(),
  TurnEndEvent(:final message) => _emit(..., stopReason: message.stopReason.name),
  AgentEndEvent() => _onAgentEnd(event),
  _ => null,  // hmm — expression must return a value; use void-ish
};
```
Each case returns void — switch expression arms returning void is allowed? The expression type would be void — `void switchExpr` — allowed in Dart? An expression switch whose arms all have type void: the switch expression's static type is void, and `void _recordRunPhase(AgentEvent event) => switch ...` works. Hmm, `when` guard +1 (when counts even in expressions? Probably same counting — probe didn't test switch-expression with when. Conservative: assume +1).

But honestly CC 7 @ 100% cov (CRAP 7) is comfortably under 12. And even if CI coverage dipped to 80%: 49×0.008+7 = 7.4. Totally safe. Keep switch STATEMENT (matches existing file style — `_record` was a statement switch; minimal diff).

Same for _recordToolEvent (CC 6) — must be 100% covered via new tests, else CC 6 @ 0% = 36+6 = 42. New tests required for all four kinds.

For `resolveKey` (CC 15 @ 100% = 15): refactor into helpers, each ≤ 6:
- `resolveKey` body: canonical + chained + name + return HostKeyResolution(...) → CC ~2
- `_effectiveSlotName(canonical, chained)`: firstWhere closure — does the closure's inner ||s count toward the METHOD's CC? `probeLogicalOr` counted them as top-level statements; closures — likely counted within the enclosing function by crap4dart's visitor (typical). firstWhere closure: `(slot) => slot != canonical && ... && _hasStoreValue(...)` — 2 &&s. Plus ternary + || → CC ≈ 1+2(&&)+1(ternary)+1(|| from chained==null || ==canonical)... let me just write it and measure.

Also, `fromEnv` computation: `name != null && name == chained && envNames.contains(name) && _isGenuineEnv(...)` = 3 &&s + ternary — extract `_isEnvResolution(...)` static helper: CC 1+3 = 4-5.

`_driftHint`: ifs (3 conditions via || or separate ifs) + ternary → CC ~6.
`_missingKeyHint`: if + ternary → CC ~3-4.

Let me now delete the probe and write the refactors. Also double-check `firstWhere` with orElse — covered by tests (pinned twin scenarios exist in provider_key_resolver_test.dart — I saw "all drift scenarios" pass; coverage was 100% for resolveKey, so every branch IS covered — the helpers will inherit 100% coverage from the same tests).

Wait — careful with `_effectiveSlotName` as an INSTANCE method (uses knownSlotNames + storeRead fields): fine.

Also check: does anything else in the changed files read above threshold in the full suite? From the targeted output: max 11 (resolveEndpointKeyName) — safe.

One more consideration: `host_agent_wiring.dart` — `buildAgentStack` CC 4 @100%, `_wireFabric` 8.09 @ 88.9% (pre-existing? `_wireFabric` is not in the PR diff — line 692 — the PR added imports/fields/buildAgentStack seams only; _wireFabric is from main. Fine.)

Delete probe, refactor now.

blocks.text:
Empirical CC counting rules in crap4dart:
- `if`: +1 each ✓ (3 ifs → CC 4)
- ternary: +1 ✓
- **switch statement: +1 per case** (4 cases → CC 5)
- **switch expression: +0 (!)** — CC 1
- **stacked cases: +1 per case LABEL** (4 labels over 2 bodies → CC 5)
- `||`: +1 each (3 || → CC 5)
- collection-if: +0
- for/catch: +1 each
- when guard: case +1, `when` +1 (CC 3 = base + case + when)

So the plan for `_record`:

# PR #1327 rework — CI red on head `5b0a01b6` fixed

## Issues/Notes

Two CI checks failed on the head commit: the aggregate **Quality gate** and the
**CRAP + duplication** (`guards`) job. The root cause was the guards job's
**CRAP ratchet** (`crap4dart analyze`, threshold pinned at `12.0`,
coverage-required) — two of the PR's brand-new functions exceeded it:

| Function | CC | Coverage | CRAP | Threshold |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `HostKeyResolver.resolveKey` (`provider_key_resolver.dart`) | 15 | 100% | **15.0** | 12.0 |
| `AgentTelemetry._record` (`agent_telemetry.dart`) | 12 | ~57% | **23.34** | 12.0 |

`resolveKey` failed even at full coverage (CRAP ≥ CC when covered), and
`_record`'s four tool-event switch cases (`toolStart`/`toolEnd`/heartbeat/
`stuck`) had **no test driving them through the adapter**, leaving the switch
under-covered and the score far over. The other guards steps were verified
clean on the updated tree: jscpd `lib/` 0.82% (< 1.0%), cross-module dupx
0.2426% (< 0.31%), `crap4dart check --baseline` green (duplication gate is
warning-severity), `dart analyze` clean.

No open threadable review threads remained: threads 1–9 (the automated
review's findings) are already resolved with the `6eacb559d` fixes present in
the tree; the remaining un-resolved entries in `pr_discussions_raw.json`
(threads 10–13) are PR-level notices with no `threadId`/`rootCommentId`, so
nothing is threadable — `review_replies.json` is therefore empty.

## Approach

CRAP-ratchet fix, no behavior change — the ratchet is the reproducing "red",
the existing suites are the behavior proof:

- **`AgentTelemetry._record` split by event family** (CC 12 → 1 + 7 + 6):

      "body": "⚠️ **IMPORTANT: aborted runs are recorded as `run error`**

`AgentTelemetry.agentErrorMessage` treats *any* `AssistantMessage.errorMessage` as a run error — but the loop's abort terminal also carries one: `_terminalMessage(model, StopReason.aborted, 'Operation aborted')` (`agent_loop.dart:1578`). So every `agent.abort()` (user stop button) and every run-idle-watchdog fire produces:

- a `run error elapsed=…s: Operation aborted` fa.log line, and
- a `runEnd` record with `httpStatus` forced to `null` (`error == null ? _lastHttpStatus : null`).

That pollutes the exact forensics signal this PR ships: grepping a shared `fa.log` for `run error` will surface routine cancels alongside real provider failures, and it diverges from the CLI's own convention (the CLI logs those runs as a plain `run end sid=…`; `turn end stop=aborted` already carries the distinction — no error line).

Suggested fix: gate on the stop reason, e.g.

```dart
String? agentErrorMessage(AgentEndEvent event) {
  for (final message in event.messages.reversed) {
    if (message is AssistantMessage &&
        message.stopReason == StopReason.error &&
        message.errorMessage != null) {
      return message.errorMessage;
    }
  }
  return null;
}
```

…and pin it with a test that aborts a run mid-request and asserts no `error` record lands (the current suite covers clean runs and provider errors but not the abort path)."

The field doc promises: *"on `runEnd`, the status of the LAST request (2xx when any token streamed, else null)"*.

The implementation can't deliver that: `_lastHttpStatus` is only ever assigned inside `_statusFromError` (typed `ProviderHttpError`, or the `<status>: ` string parse) — there is no success-path assignment anywhere — and the `AgentEndEvent` handler explicitly passes `null` on the error branch:

```dart
_emit(AgentTelemetryEventKind.runEnd,
    httpStatus: error == null ? _lastHttpStatus : null);
```

So `runEnd.httpStatus` is **always null**: clean runs have nothing recorded, failed runs get the explicit `null`. `docs/embedding.md` repeats the claim ("runEnd/error with durations and the provider HTTP status when known"). A host building hang/failure dashboards on this contract will wait forever for a 2xx `runEnd`.

Either fix the doc to match the shipped behavior ("the status of the last *failed* request; `null` otherwise"), or implement the capture if adapters can surface a success status. As written, this is a contract-vs-code mismatch on brand-new public API."
