The stated AC (issue note + `docs/embedding.md`) is that host lines are *the SAME lines* as the CLI's, so "a host embed and a CLI session are post-mortem-identical; grep one log for either". But every CLI lifecycle line deliberately carries `sid=<8-char session id>` (`agent_cli_diag_log.dart`: *"parallel fa processes share one fa.log, so every lifecycle line names its session"*):

```
run start sid=1a2b3c4d
tool start sid=1a2b3c4d name=bash
tool heartbeat sid=1a2b3c4d name=bash elapsed=12s out=834B attempt=1
```

The sink writes `run start` / `tool start name=bash` with no correlation field, and the heartbeat record drops `out=…B attempt=…` (`AgentTelemetryEvent` has no fields for them). Since hosts and the CLI append to the **same** `~/.fah/logs/fa.log`, interleaved host lines cannot be attributed to a run, a session, or even to the host vs a concurrent CLI process — the one scenario the shared-file design advertises.

`AgentCoreServices`/`AgentWiringSpec` carry no session id, so the sink can't fabricate one. Suggest a host-supplied tag, e.g. `FileAgentTelemetrySink(path, tag: 'yoclip-<runId>')` (rendered as `run start sid=<tag>`) or a `correlationId` on the services bundle — and carry heartbeat `outputBytes`/`attempt` through `AgentTelemetryEvent` to close the fidelity gap."

      "body": "⚠️ **IMPORTANT: aborted runs are recorded as `run error`**

`AgentTelemetry.agentErrorMessage` treats *any* `AssistantMessage.errorMessage` as a run error — but the loop's abort terminal also carries one: `_terminalMessage(model, StopReason.aborted, 'Operation aborted')` (`agent_loop.dart:1578`). So every `agent.abort()` (user stop button) and every run-idle-watchdog fire produces:

- a `run error elapsed=…s: Operation aborted` fa.log line, and
- a `runEnd` record with `httpStatus` forced to `null` (`error == null ? _lastHttpStatus : null`).

That pollutes the exact forensics signal this PR ships: grepping a shared `fa.log` for `run error` will surface routine cancels alongside real provider failures, and it diverges from the CLI's own convention (the CLI logs those runs as a plain `run end sid=…`; `turn end stop=aborted` already carries the distinction — no error line).

Suggested fix: gate on the stop reason, e.g.

```dart
String? agentErrorMessage(AgentEndEvent event) {
  for (final message in event.messages.reversed) {
    if (message is AssistantMessage &&
        message.stopReason == StopReason.error &&
        message.errorMessage != null) {
      return message.errorMessage;
    }
  }
  return null;
}
```

…and pin it with a test that aborts a run mid-request and asserts no `error` record lands (the current suite covers clean runs and provider errors but not the abort path)."

{"content":"# PR #1327 rework — CI red on head `5b0a01b6` fixed

## Issues/Notes

Two CI checks failed on the head commit: the aggregate **Quality gate** and the
**CRAP + duplication** (`guards`) job. The root cause was the guards job's
**CRAP ratchet** (`crap4dart analyze`, threshold pinned at `12.0`,
coverage-required) — two of the PR's brand-new functions exceeded it:

| Function | CC | Coverage | CRAP | Threshold |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `HostKeyResolver.resolveKey` (`provider_key_resolver.dart`) | 15 | 100% | **15.0** | 12.0 |
| `AgentTelemetry._record` (`agent_telemetry.dart`) | 12 | ~57% | **23.34** | 12.0 |

`resolveKey` failed even at full coverage (CRAP ≥ CC when covered), and
`_record`'s four tool-event switch cases (`toolStart`/`toolEnd`/heartbeat/
`stuck`) had **no test driving them through the adapter**, leaving the switch
under-covered and the score far over. The other guards steps were verified
clean on the updated tree: jscpd `lib/` 0.82% (< 1.0%), cross-module dupx
0.2426% (< 0.31%), `crap4dart check --baseline` green (duplication gate is
warning-severity), `dart analyze` clean.

No open threadable review threads remained: threads 1–9 (the automated
review's findings) are already resolved with the `6eacb559d` fixes present in
the tree; the remaining un-resolved entries in `pr_discussions_raw.json`
(threads 10–13) are PR-level notices with no `threadId`/`rootCommentId`, so
nothing is threadable — `review_replies.json` is therefore empty.

## Approach

CRAP-ratchet fix, no behavior change — the ratchet is the reproducing "red",
the existing suites are the behavior proof:

- **`AgentTelemetry._record` split by event family** (CC 12 → 1 + 7 + 6):
  - `_record` is now a total switch **expression** routing tool events vs
    run phases (switch expressions are free under the complexity counter),
  - `_recordRunPhase` — run/turn/first-token/turn-end/agent-end cases (CC 7),
  - `_recordToolEvent` — the four tool-execution phases (CC 6),
  - `_recordAgentEnd` — the error-then-`run end` terminal (unchanged logic:
    aborts still record as plain `run end`, per the resolved thread 1 fix).
- **`HostKeyResolver.resolveKey` decomposed** (CC 15 → 2 + 6 + 4 + 5 + 3):
  `_effectiveSlotName` (chain + known-pinned-twin registry leg),
  `_isEnvResolution`, `_driftHint`, `_missingKeyHint` — same chain order,
  same hint text, same precedence.
- **`resolveEndpointKeyName` decomposed** for ratchet margin (CC 11 → 6):
  extracted `_pinnedSlotName` (non-default endpoints only) and
  `_legacyEnvSlotName` (default-endpoint legacy env-name slots) — the env

- a `run error elapsed=…s: Operation aborted` fa.log line, and
- a `runEnd` record with `httpStatus` forced to `null` (`error == null ? _lastHttpStatus : null`).

That pollutes the exact forensics signal this PR ships: grepping a shared `fa.log` for `run error` will surface routine cancels alongside real provider failures, and it diverges from the CLI's own convention (the CLI logs those runs as a plain `run end sid=…`; `turn end stop=aborted` already carries the distinction — no error line).

```dart
String? agentErrorMessage(AgentEndEvent event) {
  for (final message in event.messages.reversed) {
    if (message is AssistantMessage &&

  return null;

{"content":"# PR #1327 rework — CI red on head `5b0a01b6` fixed

## Issues/Notes

Two CI checks failed on the head commit: the aggregate **Quality gate** and the
**CRAP + duplication** (`guards`) job. The root cause was the guards job's
**CRAP ratchet** (`crap4dart analyze`, threshold pinned at `12.0`,
coverage-required) — two of the PR's brand-new functions exceeded it:

| Function | CC | Coverage | CRAP | Threshold |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `HostKeyResolver.resolveKey` (`provider_key_resolver.dart`) | 15 | 100% | **15.0** | 12.0 |
| `AgentTelemetry._record` (`agent_telemetry.dart`) | 12 | ~57% | **23.34** | 12.0 |

`resolveKey` failed even at full coverage (CRAP ≥ CC when covered), and
`_record`'s four tool-event switch cases (`toolStart`/`toolEnd`/heartbeat/
`stuck`) had **no test driving them through the adapter**, leaving the switch
under-covered and the score far over. The other guards steps were verified
clean on the updated tree: jscpd `lib/` 0.82% (< 1.0%), cross-module dupx
0.2426% (< 0.31%), `crap4dart check --baseline` green (duplication gate is
warning-severity), `dart analyze` clean.

No open threadable review threads remained: threads 1–9 (the automated
review's findings) are already resolved with the `6eacb559d` fixes present in
the tree; the remaining un-resolved entries in `pr_discussions_raw.json`
(threads 10–13) are PR-level notices with no `threadId`/`rootCommentId`, so
nothing is threadable — `review_replies.json` is therefore empty.

## Approach

CRAP-ratchet fix, no behavior change — the ratchet is the reproducing "red",
the existing suites are the behavior proof:

- **`AgentTelemetry._record` split by event family** (CC 12 → 1 + 7 + 6):
  - `_record` is now a total switch **expression** routing tool events vs
    run phases (switch expressions are free under the complexity counter),
  - `_recordRunPhase` — run/turn/first-token/turn-end/agent-end cases (CC 7),
  - `_recordToolEvent` — the four tool-execution phases (CC 6),
  - `_recordAgentEnd` — the error-then-`run end` terminal (unchanged logic:
    aborts still record as plain `run end`, per the resolved thread 1 fix).
- **`HostKeyResolver.resolveKey` decomposed** (CC 15 → 2 + 6 + 4 + 5 + 3):
  `_effectiveSlotName` (chain + known-pinned-twin registry leg),
  `_isEnvResolution`, `_driftHint`, `_missingKeyHint` — same chain order,
  same hint text, same precedence.
- **`resolveEndpointKeyName` decomposed** for ratchet margin (CC 11 → 6):
  extracted `_pinnedSlotName` (non-default endpoints only) and
  `_legacyEnvSlotName` (default-endpoint legacy env-name slots) — the env
  leg still can never hijack a custom endpoint (issue #40 rule).
- **New regression tests for the uncovered tool phases** (the coverage half
  of the failure): a scripted tool-use turn drives `toolStart`/`toolEnd`
  records through the adapter (name/id/`isError=false`, phase ordering
  between `turnStart`/`turnEnd`), and a stuck-tool supervision leg
  (tiny `StuckToolConfig` timers, hanging executor reporting partial
  output) drives `toolHeartbeat` (`attempt=1`, `outputBytes`,
  `elapsed=…s` detail) and `toolStuck` records.

## Files Modified

- `lib/src/telemetry/agent_telemetry.dart` — `_record` split into
  `_recordRunPhase` / `_recordToolEvent` / `_recordAgentEnd`; no
  record-shape or phase-map change.
- `lib/src/model_roles/provider_key_resolver.dart` — `resolveKey` and
  `resolveEndpointKeyName` decomposed into named helpers; resolution
  order and hint text byte-identical.
- `test/telemetry/agent_telemetry_test.dart` — two new adapter tests
  (tool phase records; stuck-supervision heartbeat/stuck records) plus the
  shared scripted-multi-turn helper.

## Test Coverage

- New tests: `tool execution lands as toolStart/toolEnd records`,
  `stuck-tool supervision lands as heartbeat and stuck records` — both
  green; the full targeted set (telemetry 14 + key resolver 22 + host
  wiring + hosts/model_roles dirs = 287 tests) green.
- CRAP ratchet re-measured against fresh targeted coverage: every
  PR-touched function now reads ≤ 11.0, and the two offenders read
  `_recordRunPhase` 7.0 / `_recordToolEvent` 6.0 (both 100% covered) with
  the resolver helpers at 3.0–6.0 (100% covered) — all under the 12.0
  ceiling. CI's merged full-suite coverage is a superset of this targeted
  coverage, so the ratchet cannot read higher there.
- Duplication gates re-run on the updated tree: jscpd `lib/` 0.82%,
  dupx 0.2426%, `crap4dart check --baseline` green.
- `dart analyze` clean; `dart format` clean on all touched files.
- Diff coverage (changed lib/ lines, targeted lcov): **93.4%** ≥ 80% gate;
  CI's full-suite union only adds hits.

      "body": "⚠️ **IMPORTANT: aborted runs are recorded as `run error`**

`AgentTelemetry.agentErrorMessage` treats *any* `AssistantMessage.errorMessage` as a run error — but the loop's abort terminal also carries one: `_terminalMessage(model, StopReason.aborted, 'Operation aborted')` (`agent_loop.dart:1578`). So every `agent.abort()` (user stop button) and every run-idle-watchdog fire produces:

- a `run error elapsed=…s: Operation aborted` fa.log line, and
- a `runEnd` record with `httpStatus` forced to `null` (`error == null ? _lastHttpStatus : null`).

That pollutes the exact forensics signal this PR ships: grepping a shared `fa.log` for `run error` will surface routine cancels alongside real provider failures, and it diverges from the CLI's own convention (the CLI logs those runs as a plain `run end sid=…`; `turn end stop=aborted` already carries the distinction — no error line).

Suggested fix: gate on the stop reason, e.g.

```dart
String? agentErrorMessage(AgentEndEvent event) {
  for (final message in event.messages.reversed) {
    if (message is AssistantMessage &&
        message.stopReason == StopReason.error &&
        message.errorMessage != null) {
      return message.errorMessage;
    }
  }
  return null;
}
```

…and pin it with a test that aborts a run mid-request and asserts no `error` record lands (the current suite covers clean runs and provider errors but not the abort path)."

      "body": "⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `runEnd.httpStatus` is documented but can never be non-null**

The field doc promises: *"on `runEnd`, the status of the LAST request (2xx when any token streamed, else null)"*.

The implementation can't deliver that: `_lastHttpStatus` is only ever assigned inside `_statusFromError` (typed `ProviderHttpError`, or the `<status>: ` string parse) — there is no success-path assignment anywhere — and the `AgentEndEvent` handler explicitly passes `null` on the error branch:

```dart
_emit(AgentTelemetryEventKind.runEnd,
    httpStatus: error == null ? _lastHttpStatus : null);
```

So `runEnd.httpStatus` is **always null**: clean runs have nothing recorded, failed runs get the explicit `null`. `docs/embedding.md` repeats the claim ("runEnd/error with durations and the provider HTTP status when known"). A host building hang/failure dashboards on this contract will wait forever for a 2xx `runEnd`.

Either fix the doc to match the shipped behavior ("the status of the last *failed* request; `null` otherwise"), or implement the capture if adapters can surface a success status. As written, this is a contract-vs-code mismatch on brand-new public API."

So every `agent.abort()` (user stop button) and every run-idle-watchdog fire produces:

- a `run error elapsed=…s: Operation aborted` fa.log line, and
- a `runEnd` record with `httpStatus` forced to `null` (`error == null ? _lastHttpStatus : null`).

That pollutes the exact forensics signal this PR ships: grepping a shared `fa.log` for `run error` will surface routine cancels alongside real provider failures, and it diverges from the CLI's own convention (the CLI logs those runs as a plain `run end sid=…`; `turn end stop=aborted` already carries the distinction — no error line).

Suggested fix: gate on the stop reason, e.g.

```dart
String? agentErrorMessage(AgentEndEvent event) {
  for (final message in event.messages.reversed) {
    if (message is AssistantMessage &&
        message.stopReason == StopReason.error &&
        message.errorMessage != null) {
      return message.errorMessage;
    }
  }
  return null;
}
```

`AgentTelemetry.agentErrorMessage` treats *any* `AssistantMessage.errorMessage` as a run error — but the loop's abort terminal also carries one: `_terminalMessage(model, StopReason.aborted, 'Operation aborted')` (`agent_loop.dart:1578`). So every `agent.abort()` (user stop button) and every run-idle-watchdog fire produces:

- a `run error elapsed=…s: Operation aborted` fa.log line, and
- a `runEnd` record with `httpStatus` forced to `null` (`error == null ? _lastHttpStatus : null`).

That pollutes the exact forensics signal this PR ships: grepping a shared `fa.log` for `run error` will surface routine cancels alongside real provider failures, and it diverges from the CLI's own convention (the CLI logs those runs as a plain `run end sid=…`; `turn end stop=aborted` already carries the distinction — no error line).

Suggested fix: gate on the stop reason, e.g.

```dart
String? agentErrorMessage(AgentEndEvent event) {
  for (final message in event.messages.reversed) {
    if (message is AssistantMessage &&
        message.stopReason == StopReason.error &&
        message.errorMessage != null) {
      return message.errorMessage;
    }
  }
  return null;
}
```

…and pin it with a test that aborts a run mid-request and asserts no `error` record lands (the current suite covers clean runs and provider errors but not the abort path)."

The field doc promises: *"on `runEnd`, the status of the LAST request (2xx when any token streamed, else null)"*.

The implementation can't deliver that: `_lastHttpStatus` is only ever assigned inside `_statusFromError` (typed `ProviderHttpError`, or the `<status>: ` string parse) — there is no success-path assignment anywhere — and the `AgentEndEvent` handler explicitly passes `null` on the error branch:

```dart
_emit(AgentTelemetryEventKind.runEnd,
    httpStatus: error == null ? _lastHttpStatus : null);
```

But every CLI lifecycle line deliberately carries `sid=<8-char session id>` (`agent_cli_diag_log.dart`: *"parallel fa processes share one fa.log, so every lifecycle line names its session"*):

```
run start sid=1a2b3c4d
tool start sid=1a2b3c4d name=bash
tool heartbeat sid=1a2b3c4d name=bash elapsed=12s out=834B attempt=1
```

The sink writes `run start` / `tool start name=bash` with no correlation field, and the heartbeat record drops `out=…B attempt=…` (`AgentTelemetryEvent` has no fields for them). Since hosts and the CLI append to the **same** `~/.fah/logs/fa.log`, interleaved host lines cannot be attributed to a run, a session, or even to the host vs a concurrent CLI process — the one scenario the shared-file design advertises.

`AgentCoreServices`/`AgentWiringSpec` carry no session id, so the sink can't fabricate one. Suggest a host-supplied tag, e.g. `FileAgentTelemetrySink(path, tag: 'yoclip-<runId>')` (rendered as `run start sid=<tag>`) or a `correlationId` on the services bundle — and carry heartbeat `outputBytes`/`attempt` through `AgentTelemetryEvent` to close the fidelity gap."

**CRAP + duplication** (`guards`) job. The root cause was the guards job's
**CRAP ratchet** (`crap4dart analyze`, threshold pinned at `12.0`,
coverage-required) — two of the PR's brand-new functions exceeded it:

| Function | CC | Coverage | CRAP | Threshold |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `HostKeyResolver.resolveKey` (`provider_key_resolver.dart`) | 15 | 100% | **15.0** | 12.0 |
| `AgentTelemetry._record` (`agent_telemetry.dart`) | 12 | ~57% | **23.34** | 12.0 |

`resolveKey` failed even at full coverage (CRAP ≥ CC when covered), and
`_record`'s four tool-event switch cases (`toolStart`/`toolEnd`/heartbeat/
`stuck`) had **no test driving them through the adapter**, leaving the switch
under-covered and the score far over. The other guards steps were verified
clean on the updated tree: jscpd `lib/` 0.82% (< 1.0%), cross-module dupx
0.2426% (< 0.31%), `crap4dart check --baseline` green (duplication gate is
warning-severity), `dart analyze` clean.

No open threadable review threads remained: threads 1–9 (the automated
review's findings) are already resolved with the `6eacb559d` fixes present in
the tree; the remaining un-resolved entries in `pr_discussions_raw.json`
(threads 10–13) are PR-level notices with no `threadId`/`rootCommentId`, so
nothing is threadable — `review_replies.json` is therefore empty.

## Approach

CRAP-ratchet fix, no behavior change — the ratchet is the reproducing "red",
the existing suites are the behavior proof:

- **`AgentTelemetry._record` split by event family** (CC 12 → 1 + 7 + 6):
  - `_record` is now a total switch **expression** routing tool events vs
    run phases (switch expressions are free under the complexity counter),
  - `_recordRunPhase` — run/turn/first-token/turn-end/agent-end cases (CC 7),
  - `_recordToolEvent` — the four tool-execution phases (CC 6),
  - `_recordAgentEnd` — the error-then-`run end` terminal (unchanged logic:
    aborts still record as plain `run end`, per the resolved thread 1 fix).
- **`HostKeyResolver.resolveKey` decomposed** (CC 15 → 2 + 6 + 4 + 5 + 3):
  `_effectiveSlotName` (chain + known-pinned-twin registry leg),
  `_isEnvResolution`, `_driftHint`, `_missingKeyHint` — same chain order,
  same hint text, same precedence.
- **`resolveEndpointKeyName` decomposed** for ratchet margin (CC 11 → 6):
  extracted `_pinnedSlotName` (non-default endpoints only) and
  `_legacyEnvSlotName` (default-endpoint legacy env-name slots) — the env
  leg still can never hijack a custom endpoint (issue #40 rule).
- **New regression tests for the uncovered tool phases** (the coverage half
  of the failure): a scripted tool-use turn drives `toolStart`/`toolEnd`
  records through the adapter (name/id/`isError=false`, phase ordering
  between `turnStart`/`turnEnd`), and a stuck-tool supervision leg
  (tiny `StuckToolConfig` timers, hanging executor reporting partial
  output) drives `toolHeartbeat` (`attempt=1`, `outputBytes`,
  `elapsed=…s` detail) and `toolStuck` records.

## Files Modified

- `lib/src/telemetry/agent_telemetry.dart` — `_record` split into
  `_recordRunPhase` / `_recordToolEvent` / `_recordAgentEnd`; no
  record-shape or phase-map change.
- `lib/src/model_roles/provider_key_resolver.dart` — `resolveKey` and
  `resolveEndpointKeyName` decomposed into named helpers; resolution

- `test/telemetry/agent_telemetry_test.dart` — two new adapter tests

  - `_recordRunPhase` — run/turn/first-token/turn-end/agent-end cases (CC 7),

So every `agent.abort()` (user stop button) and every run-idle-watchdog fire produces:

- a `run error elapsed=…s: Operation aborted` fa.log line, and
- a `runEnd` record with `httpStatus` forced to `null` (`error == null ? _lastHttpStatus : null`).

That pollutes the exact forensics signal this PR ships: grepping a shared `fa.log` for `run error` will surface routine cancels alongside real provider failures, and it diverges from the CLI's own convention (the CLI logs those runs as a plain `run end sid=…`; `turn end stop=aborted` already carries the distinction — no error line).

Suggested fix: gate on the stop reason, e.g.

```dart
String? agentErrorMessage(AgentEndEvent event) {
  for (final message in event.messages.reversed) {
    if (message is AssistantMessage &&
        message.stopReason == StopReason.error &&
        message.errorMessage != null) {
      return message.errorMessage;
    }
  }
  return null;
}
```

So every `agent.abort()` (user stop button) and every run-idle-watchdog fire produces:

- a `run error elapsed=…s: Operation aborted` fa.log line, and
- a `runEnd` record with `httpStatus` forced to `null` (`error == null ? _lastHttpStatus : null`).

That pollutes the exact forensics signal this PR ships: grepping a shared `fa.log` for `run error` will surface routine cancels alongside real provider failures, and it diverges from the CLI's own convention (the CLI logs those runs as a plain `run end sid=…`; `turn end stop=aborted` already carries the distinction — no error line).

Suggested fix: gate on the stop reason, e.g.

```dart
String? agentErrorMessage(AgentEndEvent event) {
  for (final message in event.messages.reversed) {
    if (message is AssistantMessage &&
        message.stopReason == StopReason.error &&
        message.errorMessage != null) {
      return message.errorMessage;
    }
  }
  return null;
}
```

# PR #1327 rework — CI red on head `5b0a01b6` fixed

## Issues/Notes

Two CI checks failed on the head commit: the aggregate **Quality gate** and the
**CRAP + duplication** (`guards`) job. The root cause was the guards job's
**CRAP ratchet** (`crap4dart analyze`, threshold pinned at `12.0`,
coverage-required) — two of the PR's brand-new functions exceeded it:

| Function | CC | Coverage | CRAP | Threshold |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `HostKeyResolver.resolveKey` (`provider_key_resolver.dart`) | 15 | 100% | **15.0** | 12.0 |
| `AgentTelemetry._record` (`agent_telemetry.dart`) | 12 | ~57% | **23.34** | 12.0 |

`resolveKey` failed even at full coverage (CRAP ≥ CC when covered), and
`_record`'s four tool-event switch cases (`toolStart`/`toolEnd`/heartbeat/
`stuck`) had **no test driving them through the adapter**, leaving the switch
under-covered and the score far over. The other guards steps were verified
clean on the updated tree: jscpd `lib/` 0.82% (< 1.0%), cross-module dupx
0.2426% (< 0.31%), `crap4dart check --baseline` green (duplication gate is
warning-severity), `dart analyze` clean.

No open threadable review threads remained: threads 1–9 (the automated
review's findings) are already resolved with the `6eacb559d` fixes present in
the tree; the remaining un-resolved entries in `pr_discussions_raw.json`
(threads 10–13) are PR-level notices with no `threadId`/`rootCommentId`, so
nothing is threadable — `review_replies.json` is therefore empty.

## Approach

CRAP-ratchet fix, no behavior change — the ratchet is the reproducing "red",
the existing suites are the behavior proof:

- **`AgentTelemetry._record` split by event family** (CC 12 → 1 + 7 + 6):
  - `_record` is now a total switch **expression** routing tool events vs
    run phases (switch expressions are free under the complexity counter),
  - `_recordRunPhase` — run/turn/first-token/turn-end/agent-end cases (CC 7),
  - `_recordToolEvent` — the four tool-execution phases (CC 6),
  - `_recordAgentEnd` — the error-then-`run end` terminal (unchanged logic:
    aborts still record as plain `run end`, per the resolved thread 1 fix).
- **`HostKeyResolver.resolveKey` decomposed** (CC 15 → 2 + 6 + 4 + 5 + 3):
  `_effectiveSlotName` (chain + known-pinned-twin registry leg),
  `_isEnvResolution`, `_driftHint`, `_missingKeyHint` — same chain order,
  same hint text, same precedence.
- **`resolveEndpointKeyName` decomposed** for ratchet margin (CC 11 → 6):
  extracted `_pinnedSlotName` (non-default endpoints only) and
  `_legacyEnvSlotName` (default-endpoint legacy env-name slots) — the env
  leg still can never hijack a custom endpoint (issue #40 rule).
- **New regression tests for the uncovered tool phases** (the coverage half
  of the failure): a scripted tool-use turn drives `toolStart`/`toolEnd`
  records through the adapter (name/id/`isError=false`, phase ordering
  between `turnStart`/`turnEnd`), and a stuck-tool supervision leg
  (tiny `StuckToolConfig` timers, hanging executor reporting partial
  output) drives `toolHeartbeat` (`attempt=1`, `outputBytes`,
  `elapsed=…s` detail) and `toolStuck` records.

## Files Modified

- `lib/src/telemetry/agent_telemetry.dart` — `_record` split into
  `_recordRunPhase` / `_recordToolEvent` / `_recordAgentEnd`; no
  record-shape or phase-map change.
- `lib/src/model_roles/provider_key_resolver.dart` — `resolveKey` and
  `resolveEndpointKeyName` decomposed into named helpers; resolution
  order and hint text byte-identical.
- `test/telemetry/agent_telemetry_test.dart` — two new adapter tests
  (tool phase records; stuck-supervision heartbeat/stuck records) plus the
  shared scripted-multi-turn helper.

## Test Coverage

# PR #1327 rework — CI red on head `5b0a01b6` fixed

## Issues/Notes

Two CI checks failed on the head commit: the aggregate **Quality gate** and the
**CRAP + duplication** (`guards`) job. The root cause was the guards job's
**CRAP ratchet** (`crap4dart analyze`, threshold pinned at `12.0`,
coverage-required) — two of the PR's brand-new functions exceeded it:

| Function | CC | Coverage | CRAP | Threshold |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `HostKeyResolver.resolveKey` (`provider_key_resolver.dart`) | 15 | 100% | **15.0** | 12.0 |
| `AgentTelemetry._record` (`agent_telemetry.dart`) | 12 | ~57% | **23.34** | 12.0 |

`resolveKey` failed even at full coverage (CRAP ≥ CC when covered), and
`_record`'s four tool-event switch cases (`toolStart`/`toolEnd`/heartbeat/
`stuck`) had **no test driving them through the adapter**, leaving the switch
under-covered and the score far over. The other guards steps were verified
clean on the updated tree: jscpd `lib/` 0.82% (< 1.0%), cross-module dupx
0.2426% (< 0.31%), `crap4dart check --baseline` green (duplication gate is
warning-severity), `dart analyze` clean.

No open threadable review threads remained: threads 1–9 (the automated
review's findings) are already resolved with the `6eacb559d` fixes present in
the tree; the remaining un-resolved entries in `pr_discussions_raw.json`
(threads 10–13) are PR-level notices with no `threadId`/`rootCommentId`, so
nothing is threadable — `review_replies.json` is therefore empty.

## Approach

CRAP-ratchet fix, no behavior change — the ratchet is the reproducing "red",
the existing suites are the behavior proof:

- **`AgentTelemetry._record` split by event family** (CC 12 → 1 + 7 + 6):
  - `_record` is now a total switch **expression** routing tool events vs
    run phases (switch expressions are free under the complexity counter),
  - `_recordRunPhase` — run/turn/first-token/turn-end/agent-end cases (CC 7),
  - `_recordToolEvent` — the four tool-execution phases (CC 6),
  - `_recordAgentEnd` — the error-then-`run end` terminal (unchanged logic:
    aborts still record as plain `run end`, per the resolved thread 1 fix).
- **`HostKeyResolver.resolveKey` decomposed** (CC 15 → 2 + 6 + 4 + 5 + 3):
  `_effectiveSlotName` (chain + known-pinned-twin registry leg),
  `_isEnvResolution`, `_driftHint`, `_missingKeyHint` — same chain order,
  same hint text, same precedence.
- **`resolveEndpointKeyName` decomposed** for ratchet margin (CC 11 → 6):
  extracted `_pinnedSlotName` (non-default endpoints only) and
  `_legacyEnvSlotName` (default-endpoint legacy env-name slots) — the env
  leg still can never hijack a custom endpoint (issue #40 rule).
- **New regression tests for the uncovered tool phases** (the coverage half
  of the failure): a scripted tool-use turn drives `toolStart`/`toolEnd`
  records through the adapter (name/id/`isError=false`, phase ordering
  between `turnStart`/`turnEnd`), and a stuck-tool supervision leg
  (tiny `StuckToolConfig` timers, hanging executor reporting partial
  output) drives `toolHeartbeat` (`attempt=1`, `outputBytes`,
  `elapsed=…s` detail) and `toolStuck` records.

## Files Modified

- `lib/src/telemetry/agent_telemetry.dart` — `_record` split into
  `_recordRunPhase` / `_recordToolEvent` / `_recordAgentEnd`; no
  record-shape or phase-map change.
- `lib/src/model_roles/provider_key_resolver.dart` — `resolveKey` and
  `resolveEndpointKeyName` decomposed into named helpers; resolution
  order and hint text byte-identical.
- `test/telemetry/agent_telemetry_test.dart` — two new adapter tests
  (tool phase records; stuck-supervision heartbeat/stuck records) plus the
  shared scripted-multi-turn helper.

## Test Coverage

- New tests: `tool execution lands as toolStart/toolEnd records`,
  `stuck-tool supervision lands as heartbeat and stuck records` — both
  green; the full targeted set (telemetry 14 + key resolver 22 + host
  wiring + hosts/model_roles dirs = 287 tests) green.
- CRAP ratchet re-measured against fresh targeted coverage: every
  PR-touched function now reads ≤ 11.0, and the two offenders read
  `_recordRunPhase` 7.0 / `_recordToolEvent` 6.0 (both 100% covered) with
  the resolver helpers at 3.0–6.0 (100% covered) — all under the 12.0
  ceiling. CI's merged full-suite coverage is a superset of this targeted
  coverage, so the ratchet cannot read higher there.
- Duplication gates re-run on the updated tree: jscpd `lib/` 0.82%,
  dupx 0.2426%, `crap4dart check --baseline` green.
- `dart analyze` clean; `dart format` clean on all touched files.
- Diff coverage (changed lib/ lines, targeted lcov): **93.4%** ≥ 80% gate;

      "body": "⚠️ **IMPORTANT: aborted runs are recorded as `run error`**

`AgentTelemetry.agentErrorMessage` treats *any* `AssistantMessage.errorMessage` as a run error — but the loop's abort terminal also carries one: `_terminalMessage(model, StopReason.aborted, 'Operation aborted')` (`agent_loop.dart:1578`). So every `agent.abort()` (user stop button) and every run-idle-watchdog fire produces:

- a `run error elapsed=…s: Operation aborted` fa.log line, and
- a `runEnd` record with `httpStatus` forced to `null` (`error == null ? _lastHttpStatus : null`).

That pollutes the exact forensics signal this PR ships: grepping a shared `fa.log` for `run error` will surface routine cancels alongside real provider failures, and it diverges from the CLI's own convention (the CLI logs those runs as a plain `run end sid=…`; `turn end stop=aborted` already carries the distinction — no error line).

Suggested fix: gate on the stop reason, e.g.

```dart
String? agentErrorMessage(AgentEndEvent event) {
  for (final message in event.messages.reversed) {
    if (message is AssistantMessage &&
        message.stopReason == StopReason.error &&
        message.errorMessage != null) {
      return message.errorMessage;
    }
  }
  return null;
}
```

…and pin it with a test that aborts a run mid-request and asserts no `error` record lands (the current suite covers clean runs and provider errors but not the abort path)."

      "resolved": true,
      "body": "⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `runEnd.httpStatus` is documented but can never be non-null**

The field doc promises: *"on `runEnd`, the status of the LAST request (2xx when any token streamed, else null)"*.

The implementation can't deliver that: `_lastHttpStatus` is only ever assigned inside `_statusFromError` (typed `ProviderHttpError`, or the `<status>: ` string parse) — there is no success-path assignment anywhere — and the `AgentEndEvent` handler explicitly passes `null` on the error branch:

```dart
_emit(AgentTelemetryEventKind.runEnd,
    httpStatus: error == null ? _lastHttpStatus : null);
```

So `runEnd.httpStatus` is **always null**: clean runs have nothing recorded, failed runs get the explicit `null`. `docs/embedding.md` repeats the claim ("runEnd/error with durations and the provider HTTP status when known"). A host building hang/failure dashboards on this contract will wait forever for a 2xx `runEnd`.

Either fix the doc to match the shipped behavior ("the status of the last *failed* request; `null` otherwise"), or implement the capture if adapters can surface a success status. As written, this is a contract-vs-code mismatch on brand-new public API."

      "body": "⚠️ **IMPORTANT: host lines in the shared `fa.log` have no session/correlation id — "post-mortem-identical" doesn't hold**

The stated AC (issue note + `docs/embedding.md`) is that host lines are *the SAME lines* as the CLI's, so "a host embed and a CLI session are post-mortem-identical; grep one log for either". But every CLI lifecycle line deliberately carries `sid=<8-char session id>` (`agent_cli_diag_log.dart`: *"parallel fa processes share one fa.log, so every lifecycle line names its session"*):

```
run start sid=1a2b3c4d
tool start sid=1a2b3c4d name=bash
tool heartbeat sid=1a2b3c4d name=bash elapsed=12s out=834B attempt=1
```

The sink writes `run start` / `tool start name=bash` with no correlation field, and the heartbeat record drops `out=…B attempt=…` (`AgentTelemetryEvent` has no fields for them). Since hosts and the CLI append to the **same** `~/.fah/logs/fa.log`, interleaved host lines cannot be attributed to a run, a session, or even to the host vs a concurrent CLI process — the one scenario the shared-file design advertises.

`AgentCoreServices`/`AgentWiringSpec` carry no session id, so the sink can't fabricate one. Suggest a host-supplied tag, e.g. `FileAgentTelemetrySink(path, tag: 'yoclip-<runId>')` (rendered as `run start sid=<tag>`) or a `correlationId` on the services bundle — and carry heartbeat `outputBytes`/`attempt` through `AgentTelemetryEvent` to close the fidelity gap."

`docs/embedding.md:110-111`:

```dart
if (resolution?.slotName == null) {
  myUi.showBanner(resolution!.missingKeyHint!);  // names the slot to set

```

`AgentCoreServices.resolveKey` returns `null` when no `keyResolver` is configured — and `resolution?.slotName == null` is **true** in that case, so a host that copies this pattern before wiring a resolver crashes on `resolution!`. In the snippet's context a resolver is set, but the pattern invites the crash. Safer shape:

# PR #1327 rework — CI red on head `5b0a01b6` fixed

## Issues/Notes

Two CI checks failed on the head commit: the aggregate **Quality gate** and the
**CRAP + duplication** (`guards`) job. The root cause was the guards job's
**CRAP ratchet** (`crap4dart analyze`, threshold pinned at `12.0`,
coverage-required) — two of the PR's brand-new functions exceeded it:

| Function | CC | Coverage | CRAP | Threshold |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `HostKeyResolver.resolveKey` (`provider_key_resolver.dart`) | 15 | 100% | **15.0** | 12.0 |
| `AgentTelemetry._record` (`agent_telemetry.dart`) | 12 | ~57% | **23.34** | 12.0 |

`resolveKey` failed even at full coverage (CRAP ≥ CC when covered), and
`_record`'s four tool-event switch cases (`toolStart`/`toolEnd`/heartbeat/
`stuck`) had **no test driving them through the adapter**, leaving the switch
under-covered and the score far over. The other guards steps were verified
clean on the updated tree: jscpd `lib/` 0.82% (< 1.0%), cross-module dupx
0.2426% (< 0.31%), `crap4dart check --baseline` green (duplication gate is
warning-severity), `dart analyze` clean.

No open threadable review threads remained: threads 1–9 (the automated
review's findings) are already resolved with the `6eacb559d` fixes present in
the tree; the remaining un-resolved entries in `pr_discussions_raw.json`
(threads 10–13) are PR-level notices with no `threadId`/`rootCommentId`, so
nothing is threadable — `review_replies.json` is therefore empty.

## Approach

CRAP-ratchet fix, no behavior change — the ratchet is the reproducing "red",
the existing suites are the behavior proof:

- **`AgentTelemetry._record` split by event family** (CC 12 → 1 + 7 + 6):
  - `_record` is now a total switch **expression** routing tool events vs
    run phases (switch expressions are free under the complexity counter),
  - `_recordRunPhase` — run/turn/first-token/turn-end/agent-end cases (CC 7),
  - `_recordToolEvent` — the four tool-execution phases (CC 6),
  - `_recordAgentEnd` — the error-then-`run end` terminal (unchanged logic:
    aborts still record as plain `run end`, per the resolved thread 1 fix).
- **`HostKeyResolver.resolveKey` decomposed** (CC 15 → 2 + 6 + 4 + 5 + 3):
  `_effectiveSlotName` (chain + known-pinned-twin registry leg),
  `_isEnvResolution`, `_driftHint`, `_missingKeyHint` — same chain order,
  same hint text, same precedence.
- **`resolveEndpointKeyName` decomposed** for ratchet margin (CC 11 → 6):
  extracted `_pinnedSlotName` (non-default endpoints only) and
  `_legacyEnvSlotName` (default-endpoint legacy env-name slots) — the env
  leg still can never hijack a custom endpoint (issue #40 rule).
- **New regression tests for the uncovered tool phases** (the coverage half
  of the failure): a scripted tool-use turn drives `toolStart`/`toolEnd`
  records through the adapter (name/id/`isError=false`, phase ordering
  between `turnStart`/`turnEnd`), and a stuck-tool supervision leg
  (tiny `StuckToolConfig` timers, hanging executor reporting partial
  output) drives `toolHeartbeat` (`attempt=1`, `outputBytes`,
  `elapsed=…s` detail) and `toolStuck` records.

## Files Modified

- `lib/src/telemetry/agent_telemetry.dart` — `_record` split into
  `_recordRunPhase` / `_recordToolEvent` / `_recordAgentEnd`; no
  record-shape or phase-map change.
- `lib/src/model_roles/provider_key_resolver.dart` — `resolveKey` and
  `resolveEndpointKeyName` decomposed into named helpers; resolution
  order and hint text byte-identical.
- `test/telemetry/agent_telemetry_test.dart` — two new adapter tests
  (tool phase records; stuck-supervision heartbeat/stuck records) plus the
  shared scripted-multi-turn helper.

## Test Coverage

- New tests: `tool execution lands as toolStart/toolEnd records`,
  `stuck-tool supervision lands as heartbeat and stuck records` — both
  green; the full targeted set (telemetry 14 + key resolver 22 + host
  wiring + hosts/model_roles dirs = 287 tests) green.
- CRAP ratchet re-measured against fresh targeted coverage: every
  PR-touched function now reads ≤ 11.0, and the two offenders read
  `_recordRunPhase` 7.0 / `_recordToolEvent` 6.0 (both 100% covered) with
  the resolver helpers at 3.0–6.0 (100% covered) — all under the 12.0
  ceiling. CI's merged full-suite coverage is a superset of this targeted

`AgentTelemetry.agentErrorMessage` treats *any* `AssistantMessage.errorMessage` as a run error — but the loop's abort terminal also carries one: `_terminalMessage(model, StopReason.aborted, 'Operation aborted')` (`agent_loop.dart:1578`). So every `agent.abort()` (user stop button) and every run-idle-watchdog fire produces:

- a `run error elapsed=…s: Operation aborted` fa.log line, and
- a `runEnd` record with `httpStatus` forced to `null` (`error == null ? _lastHttpStatus : null`).

That pollutes the exact forensics signal this PR ships: grepping a shared `fa.log` for `run error` will surface routine cancels alongside real provider failures, and it diverges from the CLI's own convention (the CLI logs those runs as a plain `run end sid=…`; `turn end stop=aborted` already carries the distinction — no error line).

Suggested fix: gate on the stop reason, e.g.

```dart
String? agentErrorMessage(AgentEndEvent event) {
  for (final message in event.messages.reversed) {
    if (message is AssistantMessage &&
        message.stopReason == StopReason.error &&
        message.errorMessage != null) {
      return message.errorMessage;
    }
  }
  return null;
}
```

…and pin it with a test that aborts a run mid-request and asserts no `error` record lands (the current suite covers clean runs and provider errors but not the abort path)."

```dart
_emit(AgentTelemetryEventKind.runEnd,
    httpStatus: error == null ? _lastHttpStatus : null);
```

A host building hang/failure dashboards on this contract will wait forever for a 2xx `runEnd`.

But every CLI lifecycle line deliberately carries `sid=<8-char session id>` (`agent_cli_diag_log.dart`: *"parallel fa processes share one fa.log, so every lifecycle line names its session"*):

tool start sid=1a2b3c4d name=bash
tool heartbeat sid=1a2b3c4d name=bash elapsed=12s out=834B attempt=1
```

Since hosts and the CLI append to the **same** `~/.fah/logs/fa.log`, interleaved host lines cannot be attributed to a run, a session, or even to the host vs a concurrent CLI process — the one scenario the shared-file design advertises.

# PR #1327 rework — CI red on head `5b0a01b6` fixed

## Issues/Notes

Two CI checks failed on the head commit: the aggregate **Quality gate** and the
**CRAP + duplication** (`guards`) job. The root cause was the guards job's
**CRAP ratchet** (`crap4dart analyze`, threshold pinned at `12.0`,
coverage-required) — two of the PR's brand-new functions exceeded it:

| Function | CC | Coverage | CRAP | Threshold |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `HostKeyResolver.resolveKey` (`provider_key_resolver.dart`) | 15 | 100% | **15.0** | 12.0 |
| `AgentTelemetry._record` (`agent_telemetry.dart`) | 12 | ~57% | **23.34** | 12.0 |

`resolveKey` failed even at full coverage (CRAP ≥ CC when covered), and
`_record`'s four tool-event switch cases (`toolStart`/`toolEnd`/heartbeat/
`stuck`) had **no test driving them through the adapter**, leaving the switch
under-covered and the score far over. The other guards steps were verified
clean on the updated tree: jscpd `lib/` 0.82% (< 1.0%), cross-module dupx
0.2426% (< 0.31%), `crap4dart check --baseline` green (duplication gate is
warning-severity), `dart analyze` clean.

No open threadable review threads remained: threads 1–9 (the automated
review's findings) are already resolved with the `6eacb559d` fixes present in
the tree; the remaining un-resolved entries in `pr_discussions_raw.json`
(threads 10–13) are PR-level notices with no `threadId`/`rootCommentId`, so
nothing is threadable — `review_replies.json` is therefore empty.

## Approach

CRAP-ratchet fix, no behavior change — the ratchet is the reproducing "red",
the existing suites are the behavior proof:

- **`AgentTelemetry._record` split by event family** (CC 12 → 1 + 7 + 6):
  - `_record` is now a total switch **expression** routing tool events vs
    run phases (switch expressions are free under the complexity counter),
  - `_recordRunPhase` — run/turn/first-token/turn-end/agent-end cases (CC 7),
  - `_recordToolEvent` — the four tool-execution phases (CC 6),
  - `_recordAgentEnd` — the error-then-`run end` terminal (unchanged logic:
    aborts still record as plain `run end`, per the resolved thread 1 fix).
- **`HostKeyResolver.resolveKey` decomposed** (CC 15 → 2 + 6 + 4 + 5 + 3):
  `_effectiveSlotName` (chain + known-pinned-twin registry leg),
  `_isEnvResolution`, `_driftHint`, `_missingKeyHint` — same chain order,
  same hint text, same precedence.
- **`resolveEndpointKeyName` decomposed** for ratchet margin (CC 11 → 6):
  extracted `_pinnedSlotName` (non-default endpoints only) and
  `_legacyEnvSlotName` (default-endpoint legacy env-name slots) — the env
  leg still can never hijack a custom endpoint (issue #40 rule).
- **New regression tests for the uncovered tool phases** (the coverage half
  of the failure): a scripted tool-use turn drives `toolStart`/`toolEnd`
  records through the adapter (name/id/`isError=false`, phase ordering
  between `turnStart`/`turnEnd`), and a stuck-tool supervision leg
  (tiny `StuckToolConfig` timers, hanging executor reporting partial
  output) drives `toolHeartbeat` (`attempt=1`, `outputBytes`,
  `elapsed=…s` detail) and `toolStuck` records.

## Files Modified

- `lib/src/telemetry/agent_telemetry.dart` — `_record` split into
  `_recordRunPhase` / `_recordToolEvent` / `_recordAgentEnd`; no
  record-shape or phase-map change.
- `lib/src/model_roles/provider_key_resolver.dart` — `resolveKey` and
  `resolveEndpointKeyName` decomposed into named helpers; resolution
  order and hint text byte-identical.
- `test/telemetry/agent_telemetry_test.dart` — two new adapter tests
  (tool phase records; stuck-supervision heartbeat/stuck records) plus the
  shared scripted-multi-turn helper.

## Test Coverage

- New tests: `tool execution lands as toolStart/toolEnd records`,
  `stuck-tool supervision lands as heartbeat and stuck records` — both
  green; the full targeted set (telemetry 14 + key resolver 22 + host
  wiring + hosts/model_roles dirs = 287 tests) green.
- CRAP ratchet re-measured against fresh targeted coverage: every
  PR-touched function now reads ≤ 11.0, and the two offenders read
  `_recordRunPhase` 7.0 / `_recordToolEvent` 6.0 (both 100% covered) with
  the resolver helpers at 3.0–6.0 (100% covered) — all under the 12.0
  ceiling. CI's merged full-suite coverage is a superset of this targeted
  coverage, so the ratchet cannot read higher there.
- Duplication gates re-run on the updated tree: jscpd `lib/` 0.82%,
  dupx 0.2426%, `crap4dart check --baseline` green.
- `dart analyze` clean; `dart format` clean on all touched files.
- Diff coverage (changed lib/ lines, targeted lcov): **93.4%** ≥ 80% gate;
  CI's full-suite union only adds hits.
- Pushed as head `c973f0809` on `feat/1322-faui-option-a-flows`

{"content":"# PR #1327 rework — CI red on head `5b0a01b6` fixed

## Issues/Notes

Two CI checks failed on the head commit: the aggregate **Quality gate** and the
**CRAP + duplication** (`guards`) job. The root cause was the guards job's
**CRAP ratchet** (`crap4dart analyze`, threshold pinned at `12.0`,
coverage-required) — two of the PR's brand-new functions exceeded it:

| Function | CC | Coverage | CRAP | Threshold |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `HostKeyResolver.resolveKey` (`provider_key_resolver.dart`) | 15 | 100% | **15.0** | 12.0 |
| `AgentTelemetry._record` (`agent_telemetry.dart`) | 12 | ~57% | **23.34** | 12.0 |

`resolveKey` failed even at full coverage (CRAP ≥ CC when covered), and
`_record`'s four tool-event switch cases (`toolStart`/`toolEnd`/heartbeat/
`stuck`) had **no test driving them through the adapter**, leaving the switch
under-covered and the score far over. The other guards steps were verified
clean on the updated tree: jscpd `lib/` 0.82% (< 1.0%), cross-module dupx
0.2426% (< 0.31%), `crap4dart check --baseline` green (duplication gate is
warning-severity), `dart analyze` clean.

No open threadable review threads remained: threads 1–9 (the automated
review's findings) are already resolved with the `6eacb559d` fixes present in
the tree; the remaining un-resolved entries in `pr_discussions_raw.json`
(threads 10–13) are PR-level notices with no `threadId`/`rootCommentId`, so
nothing is threadable — `review_replies.json` is therefore empty.

## Approach

CRAP-ratchet fix, no behavior change — the ratchet is the reproducing "red",
the existing suites are the behavior proof:

- **`AgentTelemetry._record` split by event family** (CC 12 → 1 + 7 + 6):
  - `_record` is now a total switch **expression** routing tool events vs
    run phases (switch expressions are free under the complexity counter),
  - `_recordRunPhase` — run/turn/first-token/turn-end/agent-end cases (CC 7),
  - `_recordToolEvent` — the four tool-execution phases (CC 6),
  - `_recordAgentEnd` — the error-then-`run end` terminal (unchanged logic:
    aborts still record as plain `run end`, per the resolved thread 1 fix).
- **`HostKeyResolver.resolveKey` decomposed** (CC 15 → 2 + 6 + 4 + 5 + 3):
  `_effectiveSlotName` (chain + known-pinned-twin registry leg),
  `_isEnvResolution`, `_driftHint`, `_missingKeyHint` — same chain order,
  same hint text, same precedence.
- **`resolveEndpointKeyName` decomposed** for ratchet margin (CC 11 → 6):
  extracted `_pinnedSlotName` (non-default endpoints only) and
  `_legacyEnvSlotName` (default-endpoint legacy env-name slots) — the env
  leg still can never hijack a custom endpoint (issue #40 rule).
- **New regression tests for the uncovered tool phases** (the coverage half
  of the failure): a scripted tool-use turn drives `toolStart`/`toolEnd`
  records through the adapter (name/id/`isError=false`, phase ordering
  between `turnStart`/`turnEnd`), and a stuck-tool supervision leg
  (tiny `StuckToolConfig` timers, hanging executor reporting partial
  output) drives `toolHeartbeat` (`attempt=1`, `outputBytes`,
  `elapsed=…s` detail) and `toolStuck` records.

## Files Modified

- `lib/src/telemetry/agent_telemetry.dart` — `_record` split into
  `_recordRunPhase` / `_recordToolEvent` / `_recordAgentEnd`; no
  record-shape or phase-map change.
- `lib/src/model_roles/provider_key_resolver.dart` — `resolveKey` and
  `resolveEndpointKeyName` decomposed into named helpers; resolution
  order and hint text byte-identical.
- `test/telemetry/agent_telemetry_test.dart` — two new adapter tests
  (tool phase records; stuck-supervision heartbeat/stuck records) plus the
  shared scripted-multi-turn helper.

## Test Coverage

- New tests: `tool execution lands as toolStart/toolEnd records`,
  `stuck-tool supervision lands as heartbeat and stuck records` — both
  green; the full targeted set (telemetry 14 + key resolver 22 + host
  wiring + hosts/model_roles dirs = 287 tests) green.
- CRAP ratchet re-measured against fresh targeted coverage: every
  PR-touched function now reads ≤ 11.0, and the two offenders read
  `_recordRunPhase` 7.0 / `_recordToolEvent` 6.0 (both 100% covered) with
  the resolver helpers at 3.0–6.0 (100% covered) — all under the 12.0
  ceiling. CI's merged full-suite coverage is a superset of this targeted
  coverage, so the ratchet cannot read higher there.
- Duplication gates re-run on the updated tree: jscpd `lib/` 0.82%,
  dupx 0.2426%, `crap4dart check --baseline` green.
- `dart analyze` clean; `dart format` clean on all touched files.
- Diff coverage (changed lib/ lines, targeted lcov): **93.4%** ≥ 80% gate;
  CI's full-suite union only adds hits.

# PR #1327 rework — CI red on head `5b0a01b6` fixed

## Issues/Notes

Two CI checks failed on the head commit: the aggregate **Quality gate** and the
**CRAP + duplication** (`guards`) job. The root cause was the guards job's
**CRAP ratchet** (`crap4dart analyze`, threshold pinned at `12.0`,
coverage-required) — two of the PR's brand-new functions exceeded it:

| Function | CC | Coverage | CRAP | Threshold |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `HostKeyResolver.resolveKey` (`provider_key_resolver.dart`) | 15 | 100% | **15.0** | 12.0 |
| `AgentTelemetry._record` (`agent_telemetry.dart`) | 12 | ~57% | **23.34** | 12.0 |

`resolveKey` failed even at full coverage (CRAP ≥ CC when covered), and
`_record`'s four tool-event switch cases (`toolStart`/`toolEnd`/heartbeat/
`stuck`) had **no test driving them through the adapter**, leaving the switch
under-covered and the score far over. The other guards steps were verified
clean on the updated tree: jscpd `lib/` 0.82% (< 1.0%), cross-module dupx
0.2426% (< 0.31%), `crap4dart check --baseline` green (duplication gate is
warning-severity), `dart analyze` clean.

No open threadable review threads remained: threads 1–9 (the automated
review's findings) are already resolved with the `6eacb559d` fixes present in
the tree; the remaining un-resolved entries in `pr_discussions_raw.json`
(threads 10–13) are PR-level notices with no `threadId`/`rootCommentId`, so
nothing is threadable — `review_replies.json` is therefore empty.

## Approach

CRAP-ratchet fix, no behavior change — the ratchet is the reproducing "red",
the existing suites are the behavior proof:

- **`AgentTelemetry._record` split by event family** (CC 12 → 1 + 7 + 6):
  - `_record` is now a total switch **expression** routing tool events vs
    run phases (switch expressions are free under the complexity counter),
  - `_recordRunPhase` — run/turn/first-token/turn-end/agent-end cases (CC 7),
  - `_recordToolEvent` — the four tool-execution phases (CC 6),
  - `_recordAgentEnd` — the error-then-`run end` terminal (unchanged logic:
    aborts still record as plain `run end`, per the resolved thread 1 fix).
- **`HostKeyResolver.resolveKey` decomposed** (CC 15 → 2 + 6 + 4 + 5 + 3):
  `_effectiveSlotName` (chain + known-pinned-twin registry leg),
  `_isEnvResolution`, `_driftHint`, `_missingKeyHint` — same chain order,
  same hint text, same precedence.
- **`resolveEndpointKeyName` decomposed** for ratchet margin (CC 11 → 6):
  extracted `_pinnedSlotName` (non-default endpoints only) and
  `_legacyEnvSlotName` (default-endpoint legacy env-name slots) — the env
  leg still can never hijack a custom endpoint (issue #40 rule).
- **New regression tests for the uncovered tool phases** (the coverage half
  of the failure): a scripted tool-use turn drives `toolStart`/`toolEnd`
  records through the adapter (name/id/`isError=false`, phase ordering
  between `turnStart`/`turnEnd`), and a stuck-tool supervision leg
  (tiny `StuckToolConfig` timers, hanging executor reporting partial
  output) drives `toolHeartbeat` (`attempt=1`, `outputBytes`,
  `elapsed=…s` detail) and `toolStuck` records.

## Files Modified

- `lib/src/telemetry/agent_telemetry.dart` — `_record` split into
  `_recordRunPhase` / `_recordToolEvent` / `_recordAgentEnd`; no
  record-shape or phase-map change.
- `lib/src/model_roles/provider_key_resolver.dart` — `resolveKey` and
  `resolveEndpointKeyName` decomposed into named helpers; resolution
  order and hint text byte-identical.
- `test/telemetry/agent_telemetry_test.dart` — two new adapter tests
  (tool phase records; stuck-supervision heartbeat/stuck records) plus the
  shared scripted-multi-turn helper.

## Test Coverage

- New tests: `tool execution lands as toolStart/toolEnd records`,
  `stuck-tool supervision lands as heartbeat and stuck records` — both
  green; the full targeted set (telemetry 14 + key resolver 22 + host
  wiring + hosts/model_roles dirs = 287 tests) green.
- CRAP ratchet re-measured against fresh targeted coverage: every
  PR-touched function now reads ≤ 11.0, and the two offenders read
  `_recordRunPhase` 7.0 / `_recordToolEvent` 6.0 (both 100% covered) with
  the resolver helpers at 3.0–6.0 (100% covered) — all under the 12.0
  ceiling. CI's merged full-suite coverage is a superset of this targeted
  coverage, so the ratchet cannot read higher there.
- Duplication gates re-run on the updated tree: jscpd `lib/` 0.82%,
  dupx 0.2426%, `crap4dart check --baseline` green.
- `dart analyze` clean; `dart format` clean on all touched files.
- Diff coverage (changed lib/ lines, targeted lcov): **93.4%** ≥ 80% gate;
  CI's full-suite union only adds hits.
- Pushed as head `c973f0809` on `feat/1322-faui-option-a-flows`
  (no history rewrite — the auto-save commits carry the complete fix);
  validation re-runs on that head.

`_record`'s four tool-event switch cases (`toolStart`/`toolEnd`/heartbeat/

clean on the updated tree: jscpd `lib/` 0.82% (< 1.0%), cross-module dupx

nothing is threadable — `review_replies.json` is therefore empty.

CRAP-ratchet fix, no behavior change — the ratchet is the reproducing "red",
the existing suites are the behavior proof:

- **`AgentTelemetry._record` split by event family** (CC 12 → 1 + 7 + 6):
  - `_record` is now a total switch **expression** routing tool events vs
    run phases (switch expressions are free under the complexity counter),
  - `_recordRunPhase` — run/turn/first-token/turn-end/agent-end cases (CC 7),

  - `_recordAgentEnd` — the error-then-`run end` terminal (unchanged logic:
    aborts still record as plain `run end`, per the resolved thread 1 fix).

# PR #1327 rework — CI red on head `5b0a01b6` fixed

## Issues/Notes

Two CI checks failed on the head commit: the aggregate **Quality gate** and the
**CRAP + duplication** (`guards`) job. The root cause was the guards job's
**CRAP ratchet** (`crap4dart analyze`, threshold pinned at `12.0`,
coverage-required) — two of the PR's brand-new functions exceeded it:

| Function | CC | Coverage | CRAP | Threshold |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `HostKeyResolver.resolveKey` (`provider_key_resolver.dart`) | 15 | 100% | **15.0** | 12.0 |
| `AgentTelemetry._record` (`agent_telemetry.dart`) | 12 | ~57% | **23.34** | 12.0 |

`resolveKey` failed even at full coverage (CRAP ≥ CC when covered), and
`_record`'s four tool-event switch cases (`toolStart`/`toolEnd`/heartbeat/
`stuck`) had **no test driving them through the adapter**, leaving the switch
under-covered and the score far over. The other guards steps were verified
clean on the updated tree: jscpd `lib/` 0.82% (< 1.0%), cross-module dupx
0.2426% (< 0.31%), `crap4dart check --baseline` green (duplication gate is
warning-severity), `dart analyze` clean.

No open threadable review threads remained: threads 1–9 (the automated
review's findings) are already resolved with the `6eacb559d` fixes present in
the tree; the remaining un-resolved entries in `pr_discussions_raw.json`
(threads 10–13) are PR-level notices with no `threadId`/`rootCommentId`, so
nothing is threadable — `review_replies.json` is therefore empty.

## Approach

CRAP-ratchet fix, no behavior change — the ratchet is the reproducing "red",
the existing suites are the behavior proof:

- **`AgentTelemetry._record` split by event family** (CC 12 → 1 + 7 + 6):
  - `_record` is now a total switch **expression** routing tool events vs
    run phases (switch expressions are free under the complexity counter),
  - `_recordRunPhase` — run/turn/first-token/turn-end/agent-end cases (CC 7),
  - `_recordToolEvent` — the four tool-execution phases (CC 6),
  - `_recordAgentEnd` — the error-then-`run end` terminal (unchanged logic:
    aborts still record as plain `run end`, per the resolved thread 1 fix).
- **`HostKeyResolver.resolveKey` decomposed** (CC 15 → 2 + 6 + 4 + 5 + 3):
  `_effectiveSlotName` (chain + known-pinned-twin registry leg),
  `_isEnvResolution`, `_driftHint`, `_missingKeyHint` — same chain order,
  same hint text, same precedence.
- **`resolveEndpointKeyName` decomposed** for ratchet margin (CC 11 → 6):
  extracted `_pinnedSlotName` (non-default endpoints only) and
  `_legacyEnvSlotName` (default-endpoint legacy env-name slots) — the env
  leg still can never hijack a custom endpoint (issue #40 rule).
- **New regression tests for the uncovered tool phases** (the coverage half
  of the failure): a scripted tool-use turn drives `toolStart`/`toolEnd`
  records through the adapter (name/id/`isError=false`, phase ordering
  between `turnStart`/`turnEnd`), and a stuck-tool supervision leg
  (tiny `StuckToolConfig` timers, hanging executor reporting partial
  output) drives `toolHeartbeat` (`attempt=1`, `outputBytes`,
  `elapsed=…s` detail) and `toolStuck` records.

## Files Modified

- `lib/src/telemetry/agent_telemetry.dart` — `_record` split into
  `_recordRunPhase` / `_recordToolEvent` / `_recordAgentEnd`; no
  record-shape or phase-map change.
- `lib/src/model_roles/provider_key_resolver.dart` — `resolveKey` and
  `resolveEndpointKeyName` decomposed into named helpers; resolution
  order and hint text byte-identical.
- `test/telemetry/agent_telemetry_test.dart` — two new adapter tests
  (tool phase records; stuck-supervision heartbeat/stuck records) plus the
  shared scripted-multi-turn helper.

## Test Coverage

- New tests: `tool execution lands as toolStart/toolEnd records`,
  `stuck-tool supervision lands as heartbeat and stuck records` — both
  green; the full targeted set (telemetry 14 + key resolver 22 + host
  wiring + hosts/model_roles dirs = 287 tests) green.
- CRAP ratchet re-measured against fresh targeted coverage: every
  PR-touched function now reads ≤ 11.0, and the two offenders read
  `_recordRunPhase` 7.0 / `_recordToolEvent` 6.0 (both 100% covered) with
  the resolver helpers at 3.0–6.0 (100% covered) — all under the 12.0
  ceiling. CI's merged full-suite coverage is a superset of this targeted
  coverage, so the ratchet cannot read higher there.
- Duplication gates re-run on the updated tree: jscpd `lib/` 0.82%,
  dupx 0.2426%, `crap4dart check --baseline` green.
- `dart analyze` clean; `dart format` clean on all touched files.
- Diff coverage (changed lib/ lines, targeted lcov): **93.4%** ≥ 80% gate;
  CI's full-suite union only adds hits.
- Pushed as head `c973f0809` on `feat/1322-faui-option-a-flows`
  (no history rewrite — the auto-save commits carry the complete fix);
  validation re-runs on that head.

# PR #1327 rework — CI red on head `5b0a01b6` fixed

## Issues/Notes

Two CI checks failed on the head commit: the aggregate **Quality gate** and the
**CRAP + duplication** (`guards`) job. The root cause was the guards job's
**CRAP ratchet** (`crap4dart analyze`, threshold pinned at `12.0`,
coverage-required) — two of the PR's brand-new functions exceeded it:

| Function | CC | Coverage | CRAP | Threshold |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `HostKeyResolver.resolveKey` (`provider_key_resolver.dart`) | 15 | 100% | **15.0** | 12.0 |
| `AgentTelemetry._record` (`agent_telemetry.dart`) | 12 | ~57% | **23.34** | 12.0 |

`resolveKey` failed even at full coverage (CRAP ≥ CC when covered), and
`_record`'s four tool-event switch cases (`toolStart`/`toolEnd`/heartbeat/
`stuck`) had **no test driving them through the adapter**, leaving the switch
under-covered and the score far over. The other guards steps were verified
clean on the updated tree: jscpd `lib/` 0.82% (< 1.0%), cross-module dupx
0.2426% (< 0.31%), `crap4dart check --baseline` green (duplication gate is
warning-severity), `dart analyze` clean.

No open threadable review threads remained: threads 1–9 (the automated
review's findings) are already resolved with the `6eacb559d` fixes present in
the tree; the remaining un-resolved entries in `pr_discussions_raw.json`
(threads 10–13) are PR-level notices with no `threadId`/`rootCommentId`, so
nothing is threadable — `review_replies.json` is therefore empty.

## Approach

CRAP-ratchet fix, no behavior change — the ratchet is the reproducing "red",
the existing suites are the behavior proof:

- **`AgentTelemetry._record` split by event family** (CC 12 → 1 + 7 + 6):
  - `_record` is now a total switch **expression** routing tool events vs
    run phases (switch expressions are free under the complexity counter),
  - `_recordRunPhase` — run/turn/first-token/turn-end/agent-end cases (CC 7),
  - `_recordToolEvent` — the four tool-execution phases (CC 6),
  - `_recordAgentEnd` — the error-then-`run end` terminal (unchanged logic:
    aborts still record as plain `run end`, per the resolved thread 1 fix).
- **`HostKeyResolver.resolveKey` decomposed** (CC 15 → 2 + 6 + 4 + 5 + 3):
  `_effectiveSlotName` (chain + known-pinned-twin registry leg),
  `_isEnvResolution`, `_driftHint`, `_missingKeyHint` — same chain order,
  same hint text, same precedence.
- **`resolveEndpointKeyName` decomposed** for ratchet margin (CC 11 → 6):
  extracted `_pinnedSlotName` (non-default endpoints only) and
  `_legacyEnvSlotName` (default-endpoint legacy env-name slots) — the env
  leg still can never hijack a custom endpoint (issue #40 rule).
- **New regression tests for the uncovered tool phases** (the coverage half
  of the failure): a scripted tool-use turn drives `toolStart`/`toolEnd`
  records through the adapter (name/id/`isError=false`, phase ordering
  between `turnStart`/`turnEnd`), and a stuck-tool supervision leg
  (tiny `StuckToolConfig` timers, hanging executor reporting partial
  output) drives `toolHeartbeat` (`attempt=1`, `outputBytes`,
  `elapsed=…s` detail) and `toolStuck` records.

## Files Modified

- `lib/src/telemetry/agent_telemetry.dart` — `_record` split into
  `_recordRunPhase` / `_recordToolEvent` / `_recordAgentEnd`; no
  record-shape or phase-map change.
- `lib/src/model_roles/provider_key_resolver.dart` — `resolveKey` and
  `resolveEndpointKeyName` decomposed into named helpers; resolution
  order and hint text byte-identical.
- `test/telemetry/agent_telemetry_test.dart` — two new adapter tests
  (tool phase records; stuck-supervision heartbeat/stuck records) plus the
  shared scripted-multi-turn helper.

## Test Coverage

- New tests: `tool execution lands as toolStart/toolEnd records`,
  `stuck-tool supervision lands as heartbeat and stuck records` — both
  green; the full targeted set (telemetry 14 + key resolver 22 + host
  wiring + hosts/model_roles dirs = 287 tests) green.
- CRAP ratchet re-measured against fresh targeted coverage: every
  PR-touched function now reads ≤ 11.0, and the two offenders read
  `_recordRunPhase` 7.0 / `_recordToolEvent` 6.0 (both 100% covered) with
  the resolver helpers at 3.0–6.0 (100% covered) — all under the 12.0
  ceiling. CI's merged full-suite coverage is a superset of this targeted
  coverage, so the ratchet cannot read higher there.
- Duplication gates re-run on the updated tree: jscpd `lib/` 0.82%,
  dupx 0.2426%, `crap4dart check --baseline` green.
- `dart analyze` clean; `dart format` clean on all touched files.
- Diff coverage (changed lib/ lines, targeted lcov): **93.4%** ≥ 80% gate;
  CI's full-suite union only adds hits.
- Pushed as head `c973f0809` on `feat/1322-faui-option-a-flows`
  (no history rewrite — the auto-save commits carry the complete fix);
  validation re-runs on that head.

# PR #1327 rework — CI red on head `5b0a01b6` fixed

## Issues/Notes

Two CI checks failed on the head commit: the aggregate **Quality gate** and the
**CRAP + duplication** (`guards`) job. The root cause was the guards job's
**CRAP ratchet** (`crap4dart analyze`, threshold pinned at `12.0`,
coverage-required) — two of the PR's brand-new functions exceeded it:

| Function | CC | Coverage | CRAP | Threshold |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `HostKeyResolver.resolveKey` (`provider_key_resolver.dart`) | 15 | 100% | **15.0** | 12.0 |
| `AgentTelemetry._record` (`agent_telemetry.dart`) | 12 | ~57% | **23.34** | 12.0 |

`resolveKey` failed even at full coverage (CRAP ≥ CC when covered), and
`_record`'s four tool-event switch cases (`toolStart`/`toolEnd`/heartbeat/
`stuck`) had **no test driving them through the adapter**, leaving the switch
under-covered and the score far over. The other guards steps were verified
clean on the updated tree: jscpd `lib/` 0.82% (< 1.0%), cross-module dupx
0.2426% (< 0.31%), `crap4dart check --baseline` green (duplication gate is
warning-severity), `dart analyze` clean.

No open threadable review threads remained: threads 1–9 (the automated
review's findings) are already resolved with the `6eacb559d` fixes present in
the tree; the remaining un-resolved entries in `pr_discussions_raw.json`
(threads 10–13) are PR-level notices with no `threadId`/`rootCommentId`, so
nothing is threadable — `review_replies.json` is therefore empty.

## Approach

CRAP-ratchet fix, no behavior change — the ratchet is the reproducing "red",
the existing suites are the behavior proof:

- **`AgentTelemetry._record` split by event family** (CC 12 → 1 + 7 + 6):
  - `_record` is now a total switch **expression** routing tool events vs
    run phases (switch expressions are free under the complexity counter),
  - `_recordRunPhase` — run/turn/first-token/turn-end/agent-end cases (CC 7),
  - `_recordToolEvent` — the four tool-execution phases (CC 6),
  - `_recordAgentEnd` — the error-then-`run end` terminal (unchanged logic:
    aborts still record as plain `run end`, per the resolved thread 1 fix).
- **`HostKeyResolver.resolveKey` decomposed** (CC 15 → 2 + 6 + 4 + 5 + 3):
  `_effectiveSlotName` (chain + known-pinned-twin registry leg),
  `_isEnvResolution`, `_driftHint`, `_missingKeyHint` — same chain order,
  same hint text, same precedence.
- **`resolveEndpointKeyName` decomposed** for ratchet margin (CC 11 → 6):
  extracted `_pinnedSlotName` (non-default endpoints only) and
  `_legacyEnvSlotName` (default-endpoint legacy env-name slots) — the env
  leg still can never hijack a custom endpoint (issue #40 rule).
- **New regression tests for the uncovered tool phases** (the coverage half
  of the failure): a scripted tool-use turn drives `toolStart`/`toolEnd`
  records through the adapter (name/id/`isError=false`, phase ordering
  between `turnStart`/`turnEnd`), and a stuck-tool supervision leg
  (tiny `StuckToolConfig` timers, hanging executor reporting partial
  output) drives `toolHeartbeat` (`attempt=1`, `outputBytes`,
  `elapsed=…s` detail) and `toolStuck` records.

## Files Modified

- `lib/src/telemetry/agent_telemetry.dart` — `_record` split into
  `_recordRunPhase` / `_recordToolEvent` / `_recordAgentEnd`; no
  record-shape or phase-map change.
- `lib/src/model_roles/provider_key_resolver.dart` — `resolveKey` and
  `resolveEndpointKeyName` decomposed into named helpers; resolution
  order and hint text byte-identical.
- `test/telemetry/agent_telemetry_test.dart` — two new adapter tests
  (tool phase records; stuck-supervision heartbeat/stuck records) plus the
  shared scripted-multi-turn helper.

## Test Coverage

- New tests: `tool execution lands as toolStart/toolEnd records`,
  `stuck-tool supervision lands as heartbeat and stuck records` — both
  green; the full targeted set (telemetry 14 + key resolver 22 + host
  wiring + hosts/model_roles dirs = 287 tests) green.
- CRAP ratchet re-measured against fresh targeted coverage: every
  PR-touched function now reads ≤ 11.0, and the two offenders read
  `_recordRunPhase` 7.0 / `_recordToolEvent` 6.0 (both 100% covered) with
  the resolver helpers at 3.0–6.0 (100% covered) — all under the 12.0
  ceiling. CI's merged full-suite coverage is a superset of this targeted
  coverage, so the ratchet cannot read higher there.
- Duplication gates re-run on the updated tree: jscpd `lib/` 0.82%,

# PR #1327 rework — CI red on head `5b0a01b6` fixed

## Issues/Notes

Two CI checks failed on the head commit: the aggregate **Quality gate** and the
**CRAP + duplication** (`guards`) job. The root cause was the guards job's
**CRAP ratchet** (`crap4dart analyze`, threshold pinned at `12.0`,
coverage-required) — two of the PR's brand-new functions exceeded it:

| Function | CC | Coverage | CRAP | Threshold |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `HostKeyResolver.resolveKey` (`provider_key_resolver.dart`) | 15 | 100% | **15.0** | 12.0 |
| `AgentTelemetry._record` (`agent_telemetry.dart`) | 12 | ~57% | **23.34** | 12.0 |

`resolveKey` failed even at full coverage (CRAP ≥ CC when covered), and
`_record`'s four tool-event switch cases (`toolStart`/`toolEnd`/heartbeat/
`stuck`) had **no test driving them through the adapter**, leaving the switch
under-covered and the score far over. The other guards steps were verified
clean on the updated tree: jscpd `lib/` 0.82% (< 1.0%), cross-module dupx
0.2426% (< 0.31%), `crap4dart check --baseline` green (duplication gate is
warning-severity), `dart analyze` clean.

No open threadable review threads remained: threads 1–9 (the automated
review's findings) are already resolved with the `6eacb559d` fixes present in
the tree; the remaining un-resolved entries in `pr_discussions_raw.json`
(threads 10–13) are PR-level notices with no `threadId`/`rootCommentId`, so
nothing is threadable — `review_replies.json` is therefore empty.

## Approach

CRAP-ratchet fix, no behavior change — the ratchet is the reproducing "red",
the existing suites are the behavior proof:

- **`AgentTelemetry._record` split by event family** (CC 12 → 1 + 7 + 6):
  - `_record` is now a total switch **expression** routing tool events vs
    run phases (switch expressions are free under the complexity counter),
  - `_recordRunPhase` — run/turn/first-token/turn-end/agent-end cases (CC 7),
  - `_recordToolEvent` — the four tool-execution phases (CC 6),
  - `_recordAgentEnd` — the error-then-`run end` terminal (unchanged logic:
    aborts still record as plain `run end`, per the resolved thread 1 fix).
- **`HostKeyResolver.resolveKey` decomposed** (CC 15 → 2 + 6 + 4 + 5 + 3):
  `_effectiveSlotName` (chain + known-pinned-twin registry leg),
  `_isEnvResolution`, `_driftHint`, `_missingKeyHint` — same chain order,
  same hint text, same precedence.
- **`resolveEndpointKeyName` decomposed** for ratchet margin (CC 11 → 6):
  extracted `_pinnedSlotName` (non-default endpoints only) and
  `_legacyEnvSlotName` (default-endpoint legacy env-name slots) — the env
  leg still can never hijack a custom endpoint (issue #40 rule).
- **New regression tests for the uncovered tool phases** (the coverage half
  of the failure): a scripted tool-use turn drives `toolStart`/`toolEnd`
  records through the adapter (name/id/`isError=false`, phase ordering
  between `turnStart`/`turnEnd`), and a stuck-tool supervision leg
  (tiny `StuckToolConfig` timers, hanging executor reporting partial
  output) drives `toolHeartbeat` (`attempt=1`, `outputBytes`,
  `elapsed=…s` detail) and `toolStuck` records.

## Files Modified

- `lib/src/telemetry/agent_telemetry.dart` — `_record` split into
  `_recordRunPhase` / `_recordToolEvent` / `_recordAgentEnd`; no
  record-shape or phase-map change.
- `lib/src/model_roles/provider_key_resolver.dart` — `resolveKey` and
  `resolveEndpointKeyName` decomposed into named helpers; resolution
  order and hint text byte-identical.
- `test/telemetry/agent_telemetry_test.dart` — two new adapter tests
  (tool phase records; stuck-supervision heartbeat/stuck records) plus the
  shared scripted-multi-turn helper.

## Test Coverage

- New tests: `tool execution lands as toolStart/toolEnd records`,
  `stuck-tool supervision lands as heartbeat and stuck records` — both
  green; the full targeted set (telemetry 14 + key resolver 22 + host
  wiring + hosts/model_roles dirs = 287 tests) green.
- CRAP ratchet re-measured against fresh targeted coverage: every
  PR-touched function now reads ≤ 11.0, and the two offenders read
  `_recordRunPhase` 7.0 / `_recordToolEvent` 6.0 (both 100% covered) with
  the resolver helpers at 3.0–6.0 (100% covered) — all under the 12.0
  ceiling. CI's merged full-suite coverage is a superset of this targeted
  coverage, so the ratchet cannot read higher there.
- Duplication gates re-run on the updated tree: jscpd `lib/` 0.82%,
  dupx 0.2426%, `crap4dart check --baseline` green.
- `dart analyze` clean; `dart format` clean on all touched files.
- Diff coverage (changed lib/ lines, targeted lcov): **93.4%** ≥ 80% gate;
  CI's full-suite union only adds hits.
- Pushed as head `c973f0809` on `feat/1322-faui-option-a-flows`
  (no history rewrite — the auto-save commits carry the complete fix);
  validation re-runs on that head.
